The star product is La Estufita (Little Stove) a resistant and portable stove that works with an ecological liquid fuel.
 
As a multisegment product, Glatt Stove is targeting different markets. From the family in rural areas that still cooks with fuelwood or charcoal, to the builder that needs to live in the construction areas temporarily. La Estufita was designed so the fuel is used as efficiently as possible to give a real solution to these people. It only emits 7.5 ppm and doesn’t produce smoke.
 
It started as an entrepreneurial project and now it has the infrastructure and the team to produce 10,000 stoves daily. It is expected to grow to 20,000 stoves per day and 100,000 liters per day. Thanks to the production process that it is based on, the industry can handle the fuel easily. Hence, the global demand can be satisfied easily.

Pringle Creek Community (PCC) is a fully sustainable residential development located in the heart of Oregon’s flourishing Willamette Valley. The recipient of many awards, PCC is grounded in sustainable principles, including the use of earth-friendly building materials, energy efficient processes, respect for the natural environment, and community-oriented planning.
 
They intentionally re-developed a former state-owned institutional site for their mixed-use development, creating a new, vibrant space to live and work, reincorporating the property into the fabric of the Salem community. The natural assets inherent to the site were the first elements to inform their master plan. Pringle Creek, the community’s namesake, naturally provided the initial structure on which all planning decisions were based. The natural topography allowed them to create a fully solar neighborhood and existing wells allowed them to create a geothermal system loop that serves the heating and cooling needs of 70 homes and businesses.
 
Pringle Creek Community is building neighborhoods and selling homes while employing a variety of resources that encourage interaction and healthy living in a beautiful community.

Thx solves this problem with a transparent pricing model based on affordability and customizable giving. By selling their products at cost, free of all traditional markup prices, they're on a mission to make giving back accessible to everyone.

Thx aims to be the first social good brand to provide affordable, high-quality products that let consumers give what they'd like to any registered charity of their choice. Their database allows customers to access over 1.8 million registered charities in America, from veteran homelessness in Los Angeles to youth intervention programs in Miami and city in between.

Ultimately, THX is about empowering people to create the impact they want to have on the world.

At Leap, as sustainable designers, web developers and change-makers, being a B Corp is in their blood. 

They’ve run their business this way for nearly 20 years, from the beginning. And if there ever was another way to run a business, it never made any economic, practical or emotional sense to them, any more than it does now. In fact, it seems to them that the need for change has never been greater, that the impulse to work collectively for the greater good has never felt stronger.

And it’s because they believe in business done this way, and because they’re optimistic enough to think that business done better makes the world better, that they actively seek not just partnerships with other B Corps worldwide, but to communicate –  with customers – the benefits of working together and with purpose. The more transparent this is in everything they do and say, the clearer they can be about the positive impacts they make.

Maybe one day all businesses will run this way. Until they are, those who know what they mean – and mean what they say – should work together to change the world, one job at a time.

Founded in 1998, GoLite is the premier global manufacturer of high performance, responsible apparel and equipment designed specifically for outdoor athletes. But GoLite is far more than a collection of products. Our very name is a philosophy, a commandment to do more with less, and a foundationally sustainable proposition. We believe that lighter products are not only better for the environment, but they make the experience of being outdoors more fun. The more fun people have outdoors, the more they want to spend time in nature. And more people in nature means more people dedicated to the cause of preserving and protecting our planet.

While business is the problem, we believe that business can, and must be, the primary solution. The B Corporation Certification is one important step forward on this journey. The voluntary and independent - yet collective - nature of this certification allows forward-thinking companies to provide an example to others so that we can speed capitalism's renovation process.

Corporate responsibility has been part of GoLite’s ethos since our founding in 1998. GoLite is following a multi-year, metrics-based path to sustainability. We are striving to eliminate or mitigate 100% of our environmental footprint and be a model company in how we treat our people and community. Our long-term objective is to aim past neutrality towards becoming “net positive” to environment and civilization across our entire value chain. We don’t have a “green collection:” we are striving to address 100% of our products and 100% of our operations. As we do this, we are maintaining or increasing our stringent end-use and testing requirements so that as we move forward, we are actually improving product quality and technical performance, not sacrificing them. We have an integrated set of mission, vision, values, policies, guidelines, and goals that guide every decision we make.The Change We Seek	

GoLite is dedicated to transforming the outdoor athlete’s trail experience by designing and developing simple, beautiful high performance gear that lets people experience nature more with less. GoLite is committed to building a truly sustainable business, one that minimizes its environmental impacts and produces its products in factories that are fair, safe, and non-discriminatory.

The company's practice embodies this sense of harmony in the inviting public spaces and overall great places they create in their town planning practice, as well as in the well proportioned and comforting traditional and classical buildings they craft.

Locus Agricultural Solutions® (Locus AG) uses unique, microbrewery-type production technology to develop non-GMO, organic solutions that sustainably feed the world, improve plant vitality and minimize environmental impact—starting from the ground up. The treatments are customized to local conditions, soil types and plant types, and are delivered refrigerated for maximum freshness. Ongoing treatments result in improved plant resilience and vigor, higher productivity, more soil carbon deposition and reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. The cost-effective solutions are easily applied without changing standard practices and specifically address major challenges, including soil health, plant productivity, and climate change—while improving user profits.

Locus AG’s first commercial soil amendment Rhizolizer® concentrates on improving soil health to address productivity challenges. In the coming years, Locus AG plans to introduce more products such as additional soil amendments, biopesticides, and bioinsecticides.

Dansko, literally translated as “Danish Shoe,” was founded in 1990 with a simple, flexible-bottom clog. The brand has since expanded significantly, adding more diverse products from casual to dress, and from sandals to boots.

Dansko became a Founding B Corporation because the Community of B Corporations offers us the perspectives and collective power of many like-minded business leaders who strive for excellence in everything they do.

Dansko strives to be a rewarding company for our stakeholders, our customers, our employees, and our community. We want to be a company that serves to inspire others to become a responsible business. We came from humble beginnings – selling shoes out of the trunk of our car – so we understand the importance of engaging our local community. When we recognized that people were crazy about our shoes, we thought the natural step was to form Dansko and create a platform to amplify our social mission (and obsession with shoes).

The Change We Seek	

Dansko is a vibrant example of using for-profit business to effect social change – to initiate and exemplify ethical governance, personal and professional growth, community service and philanthropy, and to take responsible and meaningful measures to reduce our negative impact on the planet.

• Dansko is proud to announce that our new office building is LEED	 Gold Certified! Certification is awarded by the U.S. Green Building Council for Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) and is independent, third party proof that Dansko is committed to being environmentally responsible. Welcome to our 80,000 sq. foot declaration of eco-independence.

• Our headquarters features a “living wall” of plant life in the lobby (one of only four in the United States). Not only eyecatching, it also catches volatile organic compounds from the air. The living wall acts as an air filter for the entire building.

• Dansko is proud to host our township’s only Community Recycling Station, based at our company headquarters in West Grove, PA. We are happy to take care of our neighbor’s unwanted cans, glass containers, plastics, paper, flattened cardboard and other recyclable waste.

• Not only do we pay our employees to take time off to go and volunteer, we take their salary, match it, and give that amount to the organization with which they volunteer.

Rooted in Western Massachusetts, Northeast Solar grew to share sustainable solar power with residents, businesses and farmers throughout the Pioneer Valley. As citizens of a global community, Northeast Solar feels a calling to do their part in reshaping the way electricity is generated and consumed. We became a B Corp as a declaration of our commitment to model a vitally necessary standard for business operating ethics in the changing landscape of capitalism. Since its founding in San Antonio in 1984, Lake|Flato has designed buildings that respond to the culture and climate of each unique place. To support its mission to create environments that enrich communities and nurture life, the firm employs an honest and artful approach to design that places the human experience and natural environment at the center of the design process. In collaboration with clients and communities, Lake|Flato creates buildings that are tactile and modern, environmentally responsible, artful and crafted.
The firm’s design evolves from an appreciation for pragmatic solutions to vernacular architecture, the honesty of modernism, and the context of rich and varied landscapes. By employing sustainable strategies in a wide variety of building types and scales, Lake|Flato designs architecture that conserves energy and natural resources while creating high performance buildings. The firm’s industry-leading 15 AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) Top Ten Awards (the highest recognition for sustainable design in the U.S.), a recently certified Living Building and numerous LEED Platinum and Gold certified projects attest to the firm’s passion for an architecture that thoughtfully engages and enhances its place.

Vaya provides working capital loans for small and micro enterprises. Established by a team of seasoned microfinance professionals, Vaya uses the latest technology to deliver timely and relevant financial services to underserved rural geographies in India.

Vaya was the first company to use tablet banking in rural India. Since then, Vaya has added other state-of-the-art technology, from QR readers to iris-scan biometric authentication, and Data Analytics to Business Intelligence.
Vaya has a heightened focus on the seven principles of customer protection: fair and respectful treatment, transparency, designing suitable products, preventing over-indebtedness, privacy, and having a mechanism for complaint resolution.

Since Vaya customers are not familiar with conventional banking, Vaya trains them. Vaya uses simple and relatable methods to explain loan terms, interest rates, joint liability and other features. Such training not only imparts awareness but also serves to bolster trust and strengthen the credit culture.

Vaya's field staff invest significant time in developing good relationships with customers. There are extensive checks and balances in place to ensure fair and respectful treatment of customers. Field staff undergo thorough and ongoing training and evaluation.

Since they have had a clear vision of their role as a change agent both in the workplace and in their community since their foundation, their actions were within the B Corp certifications.

As a combination of profit with the solution of social and environmental problems, both in welfare measures and a mission plan to follow, they offer their employees a wide range of health care and educational and sports programs focused on quality of life and development. In this way, they do not measure resources to make sure that, in addition to high quality products, they make people happy and a community that supports and values ​​the company's activities.

EVERGREEN is the first fee of charge digital asset manager in Germany. They offer a transparent, simple and flexible way for everyone to invest or save your money. On their website, you can start investing with as little as 1€, save on different savings targets with digital sub-deposits (called Pockets), transfer or withdraw any sum, any time and check the movement of the investment on a daily basis - all free of charge.

Based on the ESG framework and the 17 UN sustainable development goals, EVERGREEN strictly selects assets for their sustainable mutual funds. According to the EU Taxonomy regulations, both funds are officially declared as sustainable financial products.

To keep things simple for you, EVERGREENs daily in-house risk management protects against high fluctuations of the investment while ensuring a steady increase in value. When things get critical on the capital markets, their experienced fund managers reduce the risk in the customer portfolio and ensure participation when markets are rising, using their own forecast-free risk management tools. 

Saving up for retirement, your next project or buying a home must become a basic right for everyone. That's the idea behind EVERGREEN.

Zullo's is an Illinois corporation--a brand--with a history.  Since 2009, Adriana has operated Zullo's Markets, LLC and Zullo's, Inc.  Through the former, she and Chef Christian serve sustainable pizza, fiadoni (hand pies) zeppole (Italian donuts) and paninis among other  Italian recipes, to food-obsessed market-goers at Chicagoland's most prestigious farmers' markets.  Through Zullo's, Inc., these sustainability  warriors provide green catering for parties of up to five-thousand.


We became a B Corp because we're stubborn enough to believe that through cooking, we can change the world--producing healthier, happier citizens on a healthier, happier planet.  As a B Corp, we strive to profit and grow while balancing our shareholders' needs with those of our employees, our community, and our environment.
The Change We Seek®


Zullo's found Adriana Marzullo learned her cooking chops in the kitchen of her childhood home, where generations of Marzullo women would come
together to assemble holiday feasts.  The company's central insight is this--the traiditional world of rural Italy was a sustainable world.  Adriana's Italian
grandmas --her nonnas--cooked in a world where ingredients were fresh and untainted by additives.  Where cooks knew their farmers, and farm animals ranged unfettered.
Where foodstuffs were gown close at hand.

But recreating that world in today's environment of genetic modification and factory farming is no simple feat.  The gastronomic and sustainability expertise of
Chef Greg Christian helps Zullo's perform that feat.  With his deep knowledge of local sourcing, relationships with Chicagoland-area farmers, and abundant "chefness," Christian adds a cup and a pinch of "can do" to Adriana's overarching vision.

Almach Energy is an ethical, clean and innovative energy consultancy dedicated to buying exclusively 100% renewable energy directly from the wholesale market.

They achieve this by using technology and buying the energy directly from the wholesale market at the lowest points. Almach also groups companies and by doing this, has managed to negotiate a reduction of the green premium with key green suppliers.
 
Almach's mission is to help companies reduce cost & environmental impact, create demand and support further investment in clean technologies.

We want to lead in the area of green energy procurement and convince as many companies as possible to buy only clean renewable energy. By becoming a B Corp we want to affirm our commitment to use business as a force of good and are excited to be part of a community with similar values.
 
Almach Energy is a small company with a big commitment: they want to innovate the way companies buy energy, but not only that, they want every company in the UK to be supplied by clean, renewable energy.

Born and Raised in Northern California, brothers and outdoor enthusiasts, Nate and Matt Oscamou spent their weekends exploring the great outdoors. Although their adventures varied, their snacks were always the same- laden with sugar and packed full of ingredients they could hardly pronounce.

Tired of the “one-size-fits-all” energy and granola bars on the market, they decided to take matters into their own hands and make a convenient snack made with simple ingredients, no refined sugar and void of all the artificial junk that could throw them off course.

Nate and Matt started their company with the belief that everyone has a frontier that needs to be conquered… but sometimes frontiers take unexpected turns. Months after perfecting the recipe, Nate passed away in a river-rafting accident. Struck by the tragic loss of a brother and business partner, Matt knew the best way to honor Nate was to continue the dream they once had together. So in 2014, Matt launched Frontier Snacks inspired by Nate’s passion for life, good food and adventure

Frontier Snacks is committed to crafting only the best products using the highest quality of ingredients– Frontier Bites are gluten/soy/dairy-free, non-GMO Project Verified and made without refined sugar. Made with 8-simple ingredients, Frontier Bites will help fuel your next Frontier- whatever that may be.

Your Next Frontier Awaits!

We launched Frontier Snacks inspired by our late founder's passion for life, good food and adventure. These values act as the foundation in every aspect of Frontier Snacks from our company culture, community service and quality of product.

The Change We Seek	

Everyone deserves a good-for-you snack that not only tastes great but is convenient of all of life's adventures. Frontier Snacks promises to use only the highest quality of ingredients that are good for you and good for the environment.

MyPup is a package delivery solution, reducing carbon emissions and contributing to more liveable cities since 2014. 

It’s our goal to reinvent urban last-mile logistics and make it future-proof. To ease pressure on the environment and reduce pollution, we consolidate parcels from every website and every courier service at our hubs outside city centres. From there, our trusted MyPup couriers deliver all parcels in an electric vehicle or e-cargo bike to unmanned Pick Up Points in offices, apartments, hospitals, and universities.

Because we consolidate, we reduce the number of delivery drivers in city centres. This is how we make a sustainable impact. We are the market leader in the Netherlands and are quickly growing in the UK, Ireland and Germany.

Andean Naturals was founded in 2004 with the mission of sharing quinoa with the world. Although the company’s initial plan was to sell directly to consumers, it quickly realized that there was a more pressing need for a reliable industrial link in the supply chain. Once large food companies could access a high volume, high quality supply of organic quinoa, they were be able to meet the booming demand of this soon-to-be health-food staple.
 
Andean Naturals today is a bridge between South American quinoa farmers and US food companies. It facilitates the growth of the organic and fair-trade quinoa market while improving the lives of over 4,500 small family farmers through increased income, technical assistance and sustained demand.
 
Andean Naturals has offices in Foster City-California, Sheboygan-Wisconsin, a cleaning plant in La Paz, Bolivia and a pre-shipment quality control laboratory in Lima, Peru. Together with it joint venture partner Specialty Commodities the company supplies _ of all quinoa in North America.

Organic Planet owner, Lindsay Gilmour, provides two types of services. The first is a personal chef service catering to clients with unique dietary needs, specializing in delicious and nutritious foods that nurture and restore good health. Lindsay is committed to the principle that our health and our environment are inextricably linked. In her work she uses only the highest quality ingredients, locally sourced whenever possible, avoids toxic chemicals, composts 100% of food waste, minimizes the use of non-renewable products and recycles or reuses all paper goods, glass and plastic. 
 
The second is value chain coordination, working with organizations such as Fair Food Philadelphia, Common Market Philadelphia, the PA Association for Sustainable Agriculture, and The Wallace Center at Winrock International, to provide technical assistance and resources to small-scale farmers. Since 2005 she has managed programs that have opened doors and helped family famers sell their goods to wholesale customers such as restaurants, caterers, grocery stores, schools, hospitals, and universities.

Better Life Mobile’s purpose is to keep all Australian’s connected. They recognise that having a mobile phone makes a difference to the welfare, health and social needs of the community.
 
 They work hard to reach out to their communities’ most at risk to get them on a great value mobile plan that offers one low price, no other fees or charges and some friendly people to talk to when they need to.
 
 Better Life also works directly with State and Federal Administrators, financial counsellors and welfare organisations too, to streamline the administration of accounts for those who don’t manage their own finances.
 
 Technology continues to develop and change at a rapid pace, and Australians are moving towards a mobile-only world. We’re excited by the opportunity to change lives through the connections we make and believe wholeheartedly in our purpose – to keep all Australians connected and included
 
 This is the situation Better Life Mobile sought to alleviate. They believed their communities’ most vulnerable needed to be supported in being kept connected and included. They had the most to gain from having a mobile phone, but were the ones most at risk of falling prey to expensive phone contracts and unfair tactics used by commercial Telcos.

Valli del Bitto SpA is a means of giving concrete solidarity and support to Heritage Bitto in order to preserve a cultural patrimony of the territory made up of traditions inherited from past generations, of technical capabilities, of knowledge and practices dictated by nature. It promotes Storico in the local and international markets by participating in the most important Slow Food exhibitions and in the best speciality food and wine fairs.

If we are to safeguard the traditions of Heritage cheese of Bitto valley we cannot ignore modern channels of communication and globalisation: the internet has played a key role in forming well informed consumers who look abroad for GOOD, CLEAN AND RIGHT products.
 
Food doesnÕt only represent pleasure but is becoming a real Òagricultural actÓ (C:Petrini) if it is produced respecting the environment and traditions.
 
The promotion of Storico reflects the need to rethink a model of agricultural development that is both fair and sustainable, and which favours biodiversity.

The name ÒTweegsÓ comes from the word ÒtwigsÓ, which evokes the image of the ÒnestÓ: the most eco sustainable house in nature. It was borne out from the innovative idea of developing an online platform that promotes and simplifies eco-friendly methods and solutions about building renovation.

The actors of the platform are clients, professionals, artisans and producers, both senior and junior: the client chooses a nearby professional to fulfill his/her intervention; on the other hand the professional asks producers and local artisans for help. That is working in team (Òintegrated planningÓ), in order to reduce costs and time of implementation.
 
In this way Tweegs makes the renovation of existing building heritage easier, shortens the construction supply chain and makes different professional communities get in touch. Furthermore it creates new job opportunities addressed to people who deserve a chance and simplify the spreading of eco-friendly practices and solutions. The result is a fairer and more transparent construction sector for all.

PerMicro is one of the first Italian institution to grant microcredits and disbursements. Its mission is to create employment and social inclusion through professional disbursement of microcredits, financial education and services for starting-up and supporting enterprises, with the aim of reaching the complete sustainability of its activity. PerMicro supports professionals with a good entrepreneurial idea and those with significiant financial needs (home, health, education), who are excluded from traditional credit channels because of insufficient credit history or precarious working position.

ThinkImpact is a Colorado-based social enterprise with offices in Ghana, Kenya, Rwanda and South Africa. Through our global experiential education programs we help people start something meaningful. ThinkImpact offers the Institute, Summit, Huddle and Xtreme and soon we will launch our newest digital product, Unleash. 



Ethics and integrity are at the core of our work at ThinkImpact; when we say we “ThinkImpact” we are expressing a worldview. We believe in the power of business to make positive impact in the world but only when the highest ethical standards are in the corporate DNA. We chose to become a B Corp because it provided a powerful tool to benchmark our work and to learn new ways to improve our company while adding transparency to our operation. 


The Institute is an 8-week full immersion program in Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda and South Africa attended by students from universities all over the world. Participants can earn credit through partner Universities. 


Summits are exclusive opportunities for groups that want to get a closer look at social innovation and developing economies in 8-14 days. We work with graduate schools, corporations, conference communities, enterprise incubators and you to provide on-the-ground no-nonsense, life-changing experiences in Africa. 


Xtreme is an intensive training module that empowers individuals to take action in their community, solving problems with interdisciplinary approaches. 


The Huddle is a 2-day event that brings together over 40 universities for faculty and administrators to develop experiential education in social entrepreneurship for their campus. 


Unleash is an action platform online where our curriculum, The Innovator, comes to life for individuals everywhere to answer the question: How do I start?




The Change We Seek®


We offer tools that change lives.


ThinkImpact builds offline and online programs that help people to start something meaningful. ThinkImpact constantly develops its core curriculum, The Innovator, to provide people everywhere the tools they need to engage their communities, new markets, and build teams. From this we have created the Innovation Process.


We unleash human potential.


Participants on our programs are doing things they never thought possible. The direct exposure that individuals gain from our programs is unlike anything they have ever done before – the relationships, the cultural awareness, and the process of creating solutions at the base of the pyramid and beyond.


We believe that nobody is poor.


The programs are designed to leverage local resources – rather than offer traditional aid – building market opportunities, creating jobs, and connecting people through collaboration. We work in rural villages in Africa but we don’t believe we should define the people we work with by what they lack. Rather, by focusing on opportunities and empowering individuals to start something, we envision inspiring  microenterprises that sell products and services that improve lives, creating critical new jobs along the way.

Waste To Green provides electronic waste/ ewaste recycling services to businesses, individuals and Government looking to minimize their carbon foot print through ethical, responsible and secure recycling of their old electronics and IT assets. Electronic waste constitutes only 2% of the landfills, yet it accounts for 70% of the hazardous components in the landfills. 



“Used electronics are shipped every day from the United States and other developed countries to developing countries that lack the capacity to reject imports or to appropriately handle materials”.



A company committed to diverting e-waste from landfills and unethical export to third world countries, they provide 100% assurance, accountability and transparency in handling their customer’s e-waste. Waste To Green follows e-waste recycling standards set by e-Stewards certification,  that adheres to stringent e-waste recycling practices recognized by the Basal Action Network (BAN). BAN is a global watchdog for e-waste industry, focused on confronting the global environmental justice and economic inefficiency of toxic trade and its devastating impacts.



One of the areas that Waste To Green realizes the data security risk associated with recycling old IT assets and data storage devices, hence they place heavy emphasis on securely destroying their client’s data before recycling their IT assets. They provide a complete asset report of recycled material along with certificate of recycling in addition to downstream accountability and complete transparency of their recycling processes.



“By becoming a B Corp we have formalized our commitment to preserving environment and health by making efforts to divert hazardous ewaste from landfills, preserving resources through materials recovery and above the ground mining. Our commitment to downstream accountability and complete transparency in our processes drove us towards joining the international B Corp movement."

The Change We Seek	



Waste To Green seeks to divert as much electronic waste from landfills by recycling it ethically, responsibly and in an environmentally friendly manner.

Founded in 2016 by Karla McNeil Rueda, an Honduran woman, industrial engineer, and culinary artist. Karla couldn't find all-natural and sustainably-made chocolate drinks that were up to her high standard of quality, flavor, and purity. So, she started Cru Chocolate to make them for herself and for people like her who refuse to compromise their ethics and taste for a drink.

Working closely and directly with passionate and skillful farmers allows Cru to bring the freshest, most potent, and highest-quality ingredients from the farm to their workshop in Roseville, California, where they are formulated, manufactured, and packaged into beautiful chocolate drinks, warranting only the best.

Deeply rooted in Mesoamerican cacao and chocolate heritage, Cru is empowered to re-imagine a new world of chocolate, where farmers and chocolate lovers can drink to a better future.

About Mutual Aid eXchange (MAX)

Mutual Aid eXchange (MAX) is a member-owned enterprise that provides insurance the way it should be; fair, faithful and socially responsible.  They offer a full range of competitively priced auto, homeowners, farm, business, life and related forms of insurance in most U.S. states and five Canadian provinces.  In many cases, they can match or even save you money over your current insurance.

MAX follows a set of socially responsible, spiritually-based core values that direct them to be:Spiritual and seeking guidance in all they do,Stewards of the earth and its resources,Servants in their community, andCompassionate to their members, members' families and communities.  

MAX practices their beliefs in two primary ways. The MAX Share Fund gives emergency financial help to people facing desperate circumstances beyond what insurance can provide.  MAX is a cooperative, so they report to their members not Wall Street. 

MAX was formed in the early 2000’s with a set of core beliefs that called us to be fair, faithful and socially responsible. When we learned about B Lab, we were thrilled to find a community of like-minded companies and consumers. We’re proud to join the growing list of socially responsible enterprises who share our vision of building a better world through business.  



 The Change We Seek

MAX believes in helping others regain and sustain wholeness in their lives.  Insurance is one way to help people do that.  But MAX believes that one should care beyond the contract.  Through the MAX Share Fund, they do something more to help people through desperate times.  This approach is unique in the industry. 

MAX hopes that more companies will find ways to give back, making business a greater conduit for good in the world.

Nan Tucker McEvoy did not set out to become a pioneer in the rebirth of California’s olive oil industry when she purchased a 550-acre ranch in the rolling hills of Marin County in 1990 – she simply wanted to provide her grandchildren with a chance to develop a meaningful connection to the land, but with Marin County’s strict zoning laws, Nan needed an agricultural purpose.

Inspired by her love of the assertive character of Tuscan olive oil, she met with one of Italy’s foremost experts on the subject, Maurizio Castelli. Three days later he was on the ranch (or so the story goes . . . ). Despite the obvious challenges involved in producing olive oil in Marin County, and against the advice of many, Nan imported 1000 seedlings from Tuscany. Her renegade decision-making has been a boon and a benefit to all who have discovered McEvoy Ranch and its abundance.

Nan’s infectious can-do spirit has influenced the growth of the company, the experience of its employees and the lives of its olive oil devotees. Today, McEvoy Ranch mindfully produces not only their award-winning certified organic, certified extra virgin olive oil, but also 80 Acres Body Care products, estate wines, cured olives, marmalades, organic vegetables and flowers, and hosts a full schedule of event and workshop offerings. McEvoy Ranch and 80 Acres products are available through their website and brick and mortar retails shops, by calling the ranch directly and at select retailers nationwide. 

Their company values of excellence, authenticity, sustainability, beauty, and relationships are the foundation of their approach to farming and business. These values are realized through the thoughtful stewardship of human, financial and material resources.



As a B Corp we can articulate and share our commitment to authenticity, sustainability, and building relationships within local, national and global communities. B Corp gives us the metrics to continually improve on these goals with the company and model of likeminded businesses to support us.

The Change We Seek	

Rooted in family, the land, and the values of sustainability, McEvoy Ranch aims to enrich the lives of our customers, community and employees. Through innovation and tradition, we craft our passion for food, wine, beauty, and the arts into products and experiences of unparalleled quality.

The Farm "Mãe D'Água" is a property located at the south side of the state of Minas Gerais that associates traditional agricultural practices with Natural Organic Agriculture and Agroforestry and awareness of animal welfare. Currently it produces coffee and high quality milk and it has been investing in better social and environmental practices since the beginning of its operations in 2012. It has a total of 900 hectares and directly places 42 employees in "Conceição do Rio Verde" County - with a remuneration above the average in the region - following the principles of business profitability associated with the improvements in people’s quality of life in its community. Besides the social impact, the Farm also acts to promote environmental preservation, seeking to utilize low environmental impact technologies having already recovered 200 hectares of degraded areas by planting fruit trees, native species, among others.



Acreditamos que cada negócio tem como objetivo, além da rentabilidade, melhorar a sociedade na qual está inserida, com benefícios concretos ao meio ambiente, colaboradores, consumidores e animais envolvidos, por isso optamos por fazer parte de um movimento de empresas que questiona a economia atual do lucro pelo lucro e se preocupa com seu papel na comunidade.

The Change We Seek	



A Mae d´Água se posiciona como uma Fazenda de porte médio pioneira, ao aliar o manejo convencional à práticas de baixo impacto ambiental, além de trabalhar com uma política cooperativa e respeitosa para com os colaboradores, visando seu empoderamento pessoal e ascensão econômica. Através deste modus operandi, vem servindo de exemplo para outros produtores rurais médios e grandes, demonstrando viabilidade econômica, e incluindo no rol de importância o impacto social e ambiental. Desta forma, espera-se a longo prazo contribuir para uma mudança na mentalidade de produção do agronegócio brasileiro.

The Eco Laundry Company was born from the philosophy that an industry widely known to be environmentally destructive could be changed into one that is sustainable. The company’s aim is to demonstrate that sustainability and profit can go hand in hand and push forward the new paradigm of conscious capitalism that they like to call “Happytalism”.



The Eco Laundry Company was born in Buenos Aires where the flagship store opened in early 2010 and in 2012 expanded into New York City with the launch of its Chelsea location. The company quickly gained worldwide media attention, being featured in leading publications such as Wallpaper*, Forbes, Bloomberg BusinessWeek, New York Magazine as well as extensive press coverage throughout Latin America, Asia and Europe.
 
The Company’s Founder Phillipe Christodoulou and his business partner Jean Calleja are determined to continue to push the boundaries of what Capitalism means in today's world and how it can be channeled to create meaningful change.

B Corp certification was important to us because it gave us a way to substantiate our value claims. Unfortunately many companies are misleading consumers by claiming to be ‘green’ when in fact they are simply not. We felt that it was important for our customers to feel confident that we were living up to our mission. As a young small business, it was also extremely helpful to work through the process of certification in order to learn more about how we could improve on our pledge to put people and the planet before profit.

The Change We Seek	

As a whole, the laundry and dry cleaning industry is a pretty nasty business. It churns through massive amounts of energy, huge volumes of clean drinking water, utilizes extremely toxic chemicals which are proven to be cancer causing and adds vast quantities of non biodegradable plastic to our landfills that then sit there for hundreds of years.
 
The Eco Laundry Company’s goal is to recreate the laundry industry, by breaking it down into parts and figuring out how to make each part of its business more sustainable. Their stores are fitted out using recycled and organic materials where possible. They use only non toxic, biodegradable, phosphate free, organic soaps and softeners and their dry cleaning process is both friendly to the environment and to their customers, utilizing Effective Microorganism (EM) technology to ensure that the process is as gentle and healthy as possible for all involved.
 
All returning customers are given a free organic, unbleached, recycled cotton laundry bag, which is reusable. This greatly reduces the amount of plastic waste and where plastic must be used, it is new generation fully recyclable and biodegradable.
 
The Eco Laundry Company encourages its customers to reduce their footprint in their homes by offering a water saving tool called the Water Hippo free to anyone who will commit to installing one. Their Buenos Aires store is a recycling drop off point for the local community and the company’s founder Phillipe Christodoulou works with adolescents in a foundation exploring solutions to problems around sustainability.
 
Whilst The Eco Laundry Company takes a multi-pronged approach to improving its footprint through sustainable action, it is absolutely committed to continue innovating within its industry sourcing or producing the safest and most sustainable products and updating its systems and machinery as technology advances.

New Day Films is a unique, filmmaker-run distribution company, providing award-winning films to educators, community groups, government agencies, public libraries and businesses since 1971. Democratically run by more than 150 filmmaker members, New Day delivers hundreds of titles that illuminate, challenge and inspire. New Day was initially formed because the women's movement had arrived and a group of independent filmmakers were unable to find a distributor for their feminist films—so they decided to create one. Today, New Day members sustain the ideals that inspired the company's formation in 1971 - partnership, great stories and changing the world - and curate its collection to encompass a wide range of subject areas. 

New Day has continued to deliver dynamic, provocative storytelling for more than four decades. Our members carefully select all the films in our collection. New Day titles have won an Academy Award, 9 Academy Award nominations, 4 Emmys, and hundreds of awards at prestigious film festivals. New Day films have been broadcast on PBS, HBO and other media outlets. Because our members both make and distribute their own films, New Day is equally committed to making high quality films and to finding and engaging the audiences that can most benefit from them. As the digital landscape evolves, New Day works hard to deliver its films in the formats that best suit customer needs.

Our films seek to illuminate complex issues, engage and challenge audiences, and inspire social change. As documentary filmmakers, collaboration with subjects, production teams, educators, activists and audiences is intrinsic to our work. We are proud to join forces with our B Corp colleagues, with whom we look forward to creating new synergies to advance our shared social and environmental values.

The Change We Seek	

New Day Films is a professional community of 150+ filmmakers connected to an expansive network of people and organizations that use their social issue, educational films to stimulate discussion, learning and action. New Day functions as a participatory democracy whose organizational structure and business practices embody the values promoted by its films.  With a 40-year history of being run cooperatively by the filmmakers, New Day holds the first B Corps Certification awarded to a film distribution company in the U.S. 

The mission of New Day Films is to provide media that educators, activists and businesses can use to challenge, illuminate and inspire, catalyzing debate about vital issues.  The films in New Day's collection represent a wide range of independent voices.  Their passionate, nuanced perspectives inform and engage public dialogue, and in turn contribute to more effective citizen participation in the democratic process. Collectively, New Day's films and filmmakers mobilize a diverse network of informed, active citizens striving to make a positive difference.  Joining B Corps extends the reach and power of this network exponentially, pumping up the volume on progressive voices and business practices.

RosettaBooks is the leading independent digital publisher, annually selling over 1,000,000 eBooks worldwide.

The company launched in 2001 initially with a list of 100 preeminent backlist titles. Headquartered in New York City, today the company’s 500-plus title list includes leading back and frontlist titles, original short eBook lines and original digital-only titles across a broad array of publishing categories in fiction and non fiction.

Its prominent author collections include 52 works of Winston Churchill, 35 titles by renowned science fiction author Arthur C. Clarke, 20 works by Kurt Vonnegut, 12 titles from international bestselling business author Stephen R. Covey and 18 works by Robert Graves, celebrated 20th century English poet, critic, and author of I, Claudius and Claudius, the God.  RosettaBooks also publishes eBook lines in collaboration with AARP, Harvard Health Publications and Mayo Clinic.  Publisher of ten Kindle Singles, including Ray Bradbury’s The Playground, RosettaBooks has launched nine of them to bestseller status. RosettaBooks is an Inc. 500 company, on the exclusive list of the fastest growing private companies in the United States.

I founded RosettaBooks so that millions of people worldwide would have the opportunity to read wonderful older titles digitally. As a digital company, we are by our nature committed to sustainability, so it seemed appropriate to align with the companies who have become B Corps.

The Change We Seek	

Trade publishing in the United States is a $10 billion print business – which means lots of trees.  eBooks reduce the price per book dramatically, thereby expanding readership.  eBooks exist without impacting our environment in the manner that print books do with paper, ink, printing, binding, shipping, warehousing, store presentation, and the like.  We are using technology to spread the opportunity for quality reading worldwide.

Founded in 2005 by Dr. Tegan Churcher Hoffmann, Blue Earth Consultants, LLC is a boutique consulting firm with a portfolio of over 100 projects completed for a multitude of clients in the United States and internationally. Blue Earth Consultants specializes in developing sustainable solutions to complex, multi-faceted marine and terrestrial issues. The firm works with communities, businesses, non-governmental organizations, academic institutions, and governments to provide the best ideas and consulting services that help improve resource management and sustainable practices around the world. 

We believe in the power and value of social and environmental responsibility for businesses. As a Certified B Corporation, we reinforce our commitment to upholding sustainable practices in every aspect of our business model.

Blue Earth Consultants develops robust, customized projects that ensure our clients remain on the cutting-edge of the conservation and sustainable use movements and realize outcomes that ensure benefits to coastal communities. Blue Earth Consultants’ service areas include:Monitoring and EvaluationFunding and FinancingStrategic and Business PlanningScience IntegrationNext/Best Practices

The firm has expertise and engages in development of strategic, business, and management planning; organizational effectiveness; strong governance and institutional framework design; monitoring, evaluation and learning; funding and financing planning and framework design; strategic communication approaches and outreach; and natural resource management and governance. 

Blue Earth Consultants recommends innovative and practical tools and strategies and assists in the creation of institutions, programs, and projects that realize significant returns for the environment and social welfare. Although Blue Earth Consultants works in many places around the globe, the firm has extensive expertise designing solutions for clients working in California and the U.S. West Coast, South Asia and the Pacific, and Mexico and the Wider Caribbean.
For more on Blue Earth Consultants, please visit: www.BlueEarthConsultants.com The Change We Seek

As a key partner, Blue Earth Consultants provides capacity, time, and shares resources with Coastal Quest to further solution-oriented innovations to create vibrant and resilient coastal communities and ecosystems.

The Green Smoothie Bar is 100% organic, vegan and gluten-free, serving smoothies and chef-made food in a convenient grab-and-go style. GSB focuses on packing the highest nutrition possible into every menu item, using organic whole superfoods. All smoothies have a base of kale and spinach, with whole fruits, house-made coconut milk, nuts and seeds to create delicious concoctions that make eating healthy pure joy. There are a variety of "kicker" options available to boost the nutrient value even further, such as wheatgrass, spirulina, chlorella, milk thistle and purple corn, to name a few. The chef-made food options include Bento Boxes which are filled with brightly coloured veggies, chosen for their high antioxidant content, protein-packed quinoa, and roasted red pepper hummus, and your choice of homemade sauce such as spicy peanut or almond lime. Collard green wraps with a walnut tapenade filling are another of the Bento Box options. Kale chips, protein bars, and cashew pudding parfaits with sprouted buckwheat and almond granola are some of the other menu items. Everything is made fresh daily from scratch using only whole organic foods, with no processed foods or sweeteners. 



The flagship store on James Street North, in the heart of Hamilton's art district, is run entirely by a team of chefs that are constantly working on new ideas in the kitchen. The goal is to provide the tastiest healthiest food available in the city, and educate customers on all the health benefits of the plants we use. Employees are all paid living wage after a small probation period, and the team is encouraged to share their knowledge of nutrition with each other and customers.

Since 2005, Umega Lettings has been managing residential property on behalf of its landlords for the thousands of tenants that call these properties home. It’s a big responsibility and one that the Umega team do not take lightly. Umega’s service is built on a foundation of transparency and accountability. The rights and responsibilities of landlords and tenants in the private rented sector in Scotland are in a period of constant change and renewal as Scotland adjusts to the role that private housing has to play in the housing mix. Umega excels in keeping all stakeholders up to date and ensures that they understand how to build long and happy relationship through the tenure of its tenants. These values are embodied by the hard working team and the energy and enthusiasm that they bring to work each day. Umega strives for improved services and standards, to be an outstanding place to work, to be the Best For and to have the biggest positive impact possible.

I’ve always believed in the capacity of business to make a positive impact on the world (even if our part of the world is relatively small!) and we’ve always tried to run our business in line with these values but it’s been difficult to find tangible ways of bringing this to life. The B Corp assessment is littered with tangible ways of making our business better no matter what measure you want to use. After initially completing the Quick Assessment we embarked on a 3 month journey of discussion and improvement to our business through a series of relatively small changes/adjustments that have created enormous positive changes to the culture in our company and the way we operate. We became a B Corp because undergoing the full assessment was a goal that we aimed for throughout our journey and it kept us focused with a solid outcome at the end. We honestly didn’t expect to meet the required standard at the end. It was a wonderful bonus.

The Change We Seek	

There are two areas that Umega Lettings is seeking to change. The first is in the Scottish letting industry where poor standards and bad practice are common. This usually results in tenants being exploited but there are negative consequences for all involved. The Scottish Government is legislating at the moment to try to improve the standards in the sector but this is not enough to create the change that is needed. Umega Lettings seeks to improve standards for the hundreds of thousands of people living in the private rented sector in Scotland by being a leading example of how private tenancies should be managed and facilitated.

The other area Umega seeks to change is as a small business and employer. Full time employed people spend more waking hours at work than they do at home with their nearest and dearest; a bizarre fact when you think about it. Umega is creating a place to work that can redefine the employer – employee relationship. Why can’t Monday morning be one of the best times of the week? Umega employees bring their personalities to work with them and put more into their company than they could in a traditional “job”. Umega understands that employees have a choice about where they work and how they work. Umega creates an environment where the team decides what that looks like and how it feels and the outcome of that is an incredible team and an outstanding place to work.

LRTT stands for Limited Resource Teacher Training. It was set up by a group of UK teachers back in 2011 who were passionate about creating a future where every child has access to a good education - regardless of the context they were born into. LRTT's approach was to work with schools in countries with limited resources and support teachers through training and coaching. The MadiDrop is an all-natural ceramic tablet embedded with silver, a well-known disinfectant. When placed in water, it releases silver ions that reduce pathogens such as E.coli. Silver ions remain in the container, providing on-going disinfection to prevent recontamination.

Our commitment to helping people improve their health and family circumstances is as strong as our commitment to sound business practices. We truly believe that safe water is possible for all people everywhere. Our B Corp status serves as our moral compass, ensuring that every decision we make supports healthy families and their quality of life.

The Change We Seek	

Everything at MadiDrop PBC starts with the belief that safe drinking water is imperative to human health. Yet, all over the world, people are still getting sick from their drinking water. Thousands of children die every day from water-related diseases.

MadiDrop PBC is tackling the global health crisis that is caused by contaminated drinking water. Working with humanitarian, relief and mission-based organizations as well as with individual distributors, the company provides a simple approach to address the critical number of waterborne diseases that result from drinking contaminated water. And, unlike any other technology that exists today, the MadiDrop tackles safe water storage, so that drinking water that is stored for extended periods of time remains safe to drink.

The safe drinking water dilemma can be solved. Working with partners all over the world, the company is at the forefront of the movement. What are the changes that need to happen? Families need a low-cost solution that addresses contamination in their daily water supply and stored water. They need to know about the risks of drinking contaminated water and that the things that make people sick cannot be seen in the water. Bringing together education and technology, families are empowered to take control of their daily drinking water. And, as a result, millions of people will have a sustainable safe water solution.

column3: Ned Schaub Consulting -- Social Change Strategy
column7:
About Ned Schaub Consulting

 

Ned Schaub Consulting -- Social Change Strategy (NSC-SCS) supports organizations and their leaders in their efforts to deepen their impact and achieve organization sustainability, with the ultimate goal of improving the quality of life for vulnerable populations, fostering communities that fully integrate those that are often marginalized, achieving stronger, richer communities and better life for all. It subscribes to and operates in accordance with the belief that sustainable organizations operating in environmentally sustainable systems of community can better achieve quality of life for all, while simultaneously achieving enduring ecosystems.

Across the range of its offerings tied to sustained impact and sustainable organizations, NSC-SCS facilitates and provides support during every step of the unique process it outlines for individual clients. Its consulting format is effective and cost efficient because clients play a key role at every turn, because they build and own their plans -- and because through this process they gain critical tools for adaptively managing the work that follows and for creating new plans in the future. NSC-SCS never builds the plan or comes to conclusions for its clients, but rather supports them in doing so. It works predominantly with organizations in the healthcare and social service sectors.

We became a B Certified Corporation because we believe that it is possible to bring together the best of the social sector and the best of the for-profit sector and create best-case scenarios for our communities. The B Corp model moves us closer to that, helping us live up to our own mission and practice what we are teaching.

 The Change We Seek

 

Ned Schaub Consulting – Social Change Strategy (NSC-SCS) envisions a more just and equitable world that includes full integration of those that are often marginalized, resulting in stronger, richer communities and better life for all. It seeks to impact broad communities in this direction by supporting the work of local leaders and organizations within them. NSC-SCS strives to provide cutting edge approaches and support for organizations and leaders as they articulate the impact they seek and as they craft the plans necessary to achieve it.

A Herself é uma empresa brasileira que constrói, a muitas mãos, novas realidades para as pessoas que menstruam. Criada em 2017, além de ressignificar a menstruação por meio de soluções tecnológicas – calcinhas, biquínis e acessórios menstruais –, tem entre seus objetivos a luta por equidade de gênero, dignidade menstrual e valorização das singularidades. Com a Herself Educacional, desenvolveu a Escola da menstruação (2019), que baseada na autonomia e na visão positiva sobre o corpo, já impactou a história de mais de 300 mil meninas, mulheres e pessoas que menstruam, buscando democratizar o conhecimento sobre educação menstrual. Em 2020, iniciou sua expansão para a América Latina e inaugurou, em Porto Alegre, a Casa da Menstruação – primeira loja física, mas também espaço para eventos, trocas e quebra de tabus. Atualmente, é referência nacional com o projeto Revolucione seu Ciclo, em parceria com a Secretaria de Justiça e Sistema Penal e Socioeducativo do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul, cujo objetivo é levar trabalho e renda para mulheres em situação de privação de liberdade e garantir o combate à pobreza menstrual, a partir da confecção de abosrventes tecnológicos.

VIASYN provides engineering consulting and other technology-enabled services to utility-scale renewable energy generators across the entire project lifecycle, from site evaluation to contract and interconnection agreement negotiations through to day-to-day operational monitoring and post-operational audits. In addition, VIASYN supports wholesale energy service providers that offer “green” energy programs, and also engages in innovative programs to better integrate renewable energy into the electrical grid. VIASYN is certified by the California Independent System Operator as a Scheduling Coordinator, and by the Electric Reliability Corporation of Texas as a Qualified Scheduling Entity.

VIASYN has a strong focus on environmentally responsible generation and currently counts among its generation customers - landfill methane, biomass, and wind resources. VIASYN has been a leader in providing scheduling and settlements services to "green" generators eligible for the California Participating Intermittent Resource Program and we provide expertise in the certification, operation and improvement of our client’s generation facilities.

VIASYN is a purpose-driven organization: we promote the well-being of the people, environment and economy of North America by supporting the development and integration of “green” electricity sources. We recognized in the B Corporation community a group of fellow organizations focused on improving more than just the bottom line; it was a natural step for us to become a Certified B Corp.The Change We Seek	

VIASYN’s mission is to promote the adoption of renewable energy sources in North America, working in conjunction with generation and demand clients, and the various electrical grid operators. Our services facilitate the integration of new renewable energy sources into the existing transmission and distribution infrastructure; helping developers to evaluate and assess potential new renewable projects; connecting supply with demand; and maximizing net revenues for each of our generation project clients.

VIASYN is a Qualified Reporting Entity (QRE) with the Western Regional Electricity Generation Information System (WREGIS). As a QRE, VIASYN can take responsibility for reporting your renewable energy generation for creation of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs). These RECS are tracked in the WREGIS database for use for verification of compliance with state and provincial regulatory and voluntary market programs such as requirements for the Western Region's Renewable Portfolio Standard.

RTOWN became a B Corp because we view our purpose of helping local businesses succeed as one of the main foundations on which communities can thrive. In a world where 1% of the population possesses 40% of the wealth, we believe RTOWN is a force for good in driving local consumer dollars into the smaller, local shops. Good Food For Good is an organic food company committed to making it easy for you to eat healthy while helping someone in need. Our food is made using organic ingredients and is free from allergens, refined sugar and preservatives. That’s not all, every time you buy our products, we donate money to feed someone in need. Our offering includes ketchups, BBQ sauces, fresh cooking sauces and turmeric teas. Our products are available across Canada and US and are sold under brand names Good Food For Good and Turmeric Teas.

The company was founded by Richa Gupta, a marketer and mother of a 12 year old girl. As a working mother, Richa found it very challenging to find packaged food and prepared shortcuts that met her expectations for taste and ingredient quality. Frustrated with being forced to compromise quality for convenience, Richa launched Good Foor For Good to make it easy for every one to eat well and do good. Inspired by TOMS Shoes, Richa adopted the Buy One Feed One model for her food business. Richa is proud to have made a positive difference in over 600,000 meals and is actively working on reaching her goal of feeding 1 million people every year.

Susty Party creates responsibly made, eco-friendly party supplies and compostable tableware. Parties and events generate the second largest amount of waste in the USA, just behind the construction industry! Susty Party products make parties more sustainable, and sustainability a little more fun.

How do we Choose Our Products?

At the end of the day we ask ourselves: Will this productbe good for the environment, the people who made it, and the people who will use it? We also screen our products for these specific standards.

All products must meet at least three of these attributes: renewable (made from a renewable resource; compostable (it biodegrades in 180 days); recycled (made from mostly recycled content); regulated (3rd party verifications and certifications such as Fair Trade or B Corp or Cradle to Cradle); green energy (produced by green energy); made in the USA); durable; non-toxic; artisanal producer.

And, because we don't sell products that are harmful to the environment, none of our products: contain non-recycled plastic; contain paper that is not recycled or sustainable harvested; promote a throw-away culture of waste.

Basically we try to find products that create social or environmental good. We use our standards, as well as our own sustainability ethic, philosophy and heart to guide us.

We’re proud to be a Certified B Corporation. We at Susty Party aim to create an exemplary model for a healthy, entrepreneurial, creative, and of course - fun and sustainable! - workplace. We are proud to have adopted B Corporation's strict, independent environmental and social performance standards. It's our way to ensure our values are upheld through the very DNA of our business.

The Change We Seek	

Can We Create a Movement Out of Sustainable Partying?

As human beings, we love connecting with each other.Susty Party propels forward the idea that fun human connections and a movement towards sustainability can co-exist. Our dream is to provide products for people to create magical times with each other while also spreading their good intentions to the Earth.

Can we have fun and be green? If you want to try and create a sustainable party, we hope our products will lead you in the right direction. We also have a free guide and decorative signage package to help you. As you create a fun and green party, you can also be part of something larger. As a conscious consumer you can support new systems with your buying power. Commerce is a powerful agent of change.

And, because we don't sell products that are harmful to the environment, none of our products: contain non-recycled plastic; contain paper that is not recycled or sustainable harvested; promote a throw-away culture of waste.

Basically we try to find products that create social or environmental good. We use our standards, as well as our own sustainability ethic, philosophy and heart to guide us.

CardioReady’s offering is an end-to-end solution, spanning AED selection and procurement to training to ongoing management to post-event. We are a specialist exclusively focused on the AED sector, and maintain dedicated Practice Groups that provide us with a unique ability to understand our clients' business needs. They use a patented process to provide turn-key solutions to our clients, culminating in conferment of the CardioReady Certification. Designed to optimize lifesaving potential and efficacy, and coordinated via a dedicated Relationship Manager.

In addition to its emphasis on improving safety, CardioReady's approach embeds sound risk management principles, and their CardioReady Certification Center	 affords strong local controls bolstered by real-time central / corporate visibility of compliance status. Additional peace of mind is provided by their team of medical experts who perform annual site inspections. They also recognize that compliance needs to be an easily performed routine activity - not an exercise unto itself. To put this principle into practice, they pioneered the innovative Maintenance Minder	 mobile application (available for iPhone, Android, Microsoft and Blackberry devices), enabling maintenance checks to be completed in 60 seconds via a process that is as simple as scanning a bar code.

While easy to use, AEDs do require human intervention, and training helps to generate better outcomes. They offer various training options, but oftentimes traditional training methods are impractical for enterprises with high employee turn-over. With this in mind, they developed BeReady Emergency Response Training™. Endorsed by the Heart Rhythm Society*, BeReady is a patent-pending, 100% online approach to AED/CPR training that makes it financially and logistically practical to train all employees - yielding lifesaving, employee satisfaction, and social responsibility benefits. Notably, BeReady also automates the renewal process, substantially eliminating the need for regular management of trained responder rosters.

Our company and its mission are built around elevating awareness and preparedness to reduce the death from Sudden Cardiac Arrest. Our core belief is that this change will most effectively be driven not by legislation but instead by the business world. Considering the alignment of value creation for society and the other aspects of our culture with the tenets of the B Corp community, becoming a B Corp was a very easy decision for us.

The Change We Seek	

While many people do not realize it, Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA) is the leading cause of death in the United States, taking a life every 90 seconds. SCA strikes all age brackets, and without rapid intervention, SCA is terribly lethal, as survival rates drop by roughly 10% per minute. Fortunately, Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) offer an easy and effective means of combatting SCA, and use of an AED and CPR within 3 minutes can increase the odds of survival from less than 7% to more than 70%.

CardioReady seeks change on two levels. First, the company strives to increase awareness of SCA and the lifesaving potential of CPR and AEDs. Second, CardioReady aims for the proliferation of AED/CPR use. With less than 5% of businesses having AEDs and less than 3% of the population currently trained in CPR, there is much to be gained for all of us.

Designed for laypeople to use, AEDs can be easily used by untrained school children and are very affordable. Equally, CPR is an easily apprehended skill.

To drive this change, CardioReady seeks to serve as a vocal and visible advocate across the business community, creating greater awareness. Equally, CardioReady offers a unique solution that leverages modern technology to make establishment of an AED program and training ALL of a company’s employees both easy and affordable.

Reformation is a revolutionary lifestyle brand created in 2009 by designer Yael Aflalo. Based in Los Angeles, Reformation offers stylish eco-conscious garments, proving that fast fashion and sustainability can co-exist beautifully.

Using vintage garments, deadstock materials and eco fabrics, Reformation makes beautiful styles at a fraction of the environmental impact generated by most fashion brands. With sustainability as the driving force, Reformation infuses green measures into every aspect of the brand, from a heat reflecting roof and clean energy in its factory, to recycled hangers in stores and eco-friendly packaging for at-home shipments.

Home to the first sustainable sewing factory in the U.S., Reformation designs, manufactures, photographs and ships all product under one eco-friendly roof. With boutiques in Los Angeles and New York City, and an online store at www.thereformation.com, Reformation continues to lead the movement in sustainable fashion.

We defy the status quo in the fashion industry. Pursuing B Corp certification is just another way we can challenge other apparel companies to keep up, move past compliance, and truly do the right thing for customers, employees and the environment.

The Change We Seek	

Reformation is committed to leading a sustainable revolution in the fashion industry. Its goal is to shift the industry from being one of the most polluting and wasteful enterprises on the planet, to one that has a positive impact on water, materials, and energy systems. Leading by example, Reformation opened the first sustainable sewing factory in the United States that houses all of the company’s operations including design, manufacturing, creative, and fulfillment.

Reformation products are made from repurposed vintage clothing, rescued deadstock fabrics and cellulose-based materials. All product lines help minimize fabrics in landfills and have much lower environmental footprints compared to conventional materials like cotton or polyester. Once clothing is designed and manufactured in Reformation’s sustainable LA factory, it is packaged in 100% recycled content paper mailers, which are recyclable and biodegradable. Reformation even purchases carbon offsets to help green the shipping required to get products to customers around the world.

Reformation is committed to having a transformative effect in the world, and constantly pursuing “zero waste” and “carbon neutral” goals. With sustainability as the driving force, Reformation infuses green measures into every aspect of the operations, from LED lights and clean energy in the factory, to recycled hangers and reusable totes in stores. The company limits material waste, donates fabric scrap materials, uses 100% renewable energy, and has a sustainable garden and outdoor break room.

Customers are what fuel the Reformation. They play a huge role in helping incite change and revolutionize the wasteful practices of the apparel industry. Reformation strives to educate their customers on the impact that purchasing decisions, garment care, and other lifestyle choices have on the planet, using infographics, care labels and hangtags on clothing. Reformation is committed to building awareness within the core team, too, with monthly company-wide education and volunteer events.

More Than Money ("MTM") Careers enlists the next generation to become part of the solution to the social and environmental challenges of the 21st century. A career services company, MTM Careers helps students and alums, fellowship participants and professionals "Get Clear, Get Connected and Get Hired" for well-paying social-impact opportunities that match their values. The company offers an online library of modules for individuals and CCE-accredited in-person and online training programs for university staff, mentors and coaches to use to accelerate the process of helping individuals find their next job in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), Social Enterprise, and/or Sustainable Business.



We believe strongly that corporations should not be a sanctuary from society but a tributary to society. Having one partner involved in the social responsible business movement since the late 1980s, and the other partner sculpting socially responsible career paths the past decade, we are thrilled to be able to join a tribe from which we can learn from and contribute to so that together, we can help create a world of more economic and social justice, with financial profitability a necessary and important means, but no an end onto itself. 

The Change We Seek®


We define a "good business" (and "good businessperson") as one that uplifts the human spirit and helps to alleviate poverty and suffering on our planet. Many talented college and graduate school graduates, and young professionals, want to be good businesspeople and find meaningful work that addresses a societal challenge—while still making a good living. At school, however, it is easier to be herded into on-campus recruiting for more traditional jobs, and more difficult to actively seek alternative kinds of jobs via an off-campus search. 


In addition, career services staff often have little information or resources themselves for careers that "make a difference" beyond knowing about a few non-profit organization. We wish to provide an ecosystem of the necessary resources and contacts for these intermediaries and their end users. MTM Careers video libraries make these off-campus searches easier and more effective while supporting the work of career service. In that way we channel those who want to make a difference into careers that help create a better world for all.

Enova is a social enterprise that designs, builds and operates 95 centers that offer access to education and technology based on the needs of low-income communities in Mexico. Their mission is to improve people’s academic and vocational skills through technology. 

Enova’s solution to these challenges is the Red de Innovación y Aprendizaje (RIA), or the Learning and Innovation Network. The network includes a chain of 70 educational centers that provide low-income Mexican communities with quality educational opportunities and access to information technologies. The network is expanding quickly, with 25 Digital Libraries inaugurated in 2013. Every week 3,000 individuals sign up at the RIA centers to become members. 

Enova's differentiating strategy is that in addition to providing users with access to technology, it develops the tools needed to use it effectively and incorporate the necessary elements for effective learning. The model integrates four main components: 1) access to robust IT infrastructure, 2) selection and development of relevant educational content for all ages, ranging from basic competencies to use of technology and English as a second language 3) a blended e-learning model with skilled facilitators, and 4) analysis of each student’s performance to revise and improve course content. 

We feel that it is important to be part of a group that shares our vision of having a high social impact while creating value.
