Expressyourshades was born in 2009 as a way to raise funds and awareness towards lifeline organizations who were struggling to provide in the midst of the recession. It was also born out of a need to leave the excess of Hollywood behind, however glitzy, to focus on more humane and meaningful endeavours.

Out of a real concern to minimize our footprint on the planet while increasing its inhabitants’ wellbeing, Expressyourshades decided to offer PVC-free, recyclable window shades and to donate 10% of its proceeds to a NY lifeline organization. And, four years later, offering products of exceptional quality and performance, the company does just that. The catch is, it is up to the client to get involved and pick the charity in question. It’s not so much a catch as it is an incentive. Expressyourshades allows men and women to express their attachment to the planet and their desire to see it prosper. It is a real opportunity to express one’s greener and friendlier self, a real opportunity to change the landscape, one window at a time.

When buying window treatments we might want to assess our commitment to the environment and decide if we are most concerned with indoor air quality, cost, potential risks to human health, product life cycle impact, aesthetic, or– all of the above. In the big world of sustainability, there are quite a few actions we can take to express our degree of commitment; there is no black or white, no right or wrong, just the desire to do things a bit differently. Recognizing that each individual has different resources, lifestyles, needs, tastes and so on, Expressyourshades has made its mission clear: answer to these differences, environmentally and socially.

I discovered B Corp in the very early stages of developing Expressyourshades. Right then I knew I wanted to be part of the movement because it validated my vision in a most unmistakable way: there was a better way to do business, and I wasn’t crazy for thinking so! In this day and age, there is nothing more inspiring and evolutionary than being part of a community that values the environment, people, transparency and accountability in equal measure, and uses those values to define success. That’s what I call progress.



The Change We Seek

Expressyourshades’ mission is deeply rooted in humanitarian values. So much that, had the recession not happened, the company would probably not even exist today.

By opting for a business model that truly answers to the needs of the consumers as much as to the needs of the community, Expressyourshades is saying that being environmentally-friendly doesn’t stop at home or at the office. It is saying that companies and individuals alike have a much bigger role to play before we call each other sustainable, much less “friendly”.

Expressyourshades is proud to support lifeline organizations as they are, truly, our greatest social safety net. And incidentally, someone’s second chance.

AguaClara provides the design services and technical assistance to implement its one-of-a-kind, community-scale water treatment technologies. These technologies were invented at Cornell University, and are affordable, zero-energy, and sustainable in underserved regions of the world. They are made from all locally available materials, simple to operate, and entirely powered by gravity.

AguaClara primarily designs gravity-powered water treatment plants that serve communities from semi-rural villages of 200 households to towns and urban centers of up to 50,000 people. These plants treat both high- and low-turbidity water to the highest standards of the World Health Organization (WHO) for safe drinking water. AguaClara technologies can currently only be found in Honduras and India, but the company’s vision is to provide universal access to safe water on tap.
 
AguaClara’s mission is to promote global health by designing and disseminating water treatment solutions that are socially, environmentally, and economically sustainable. They provide the services that enable their partners to implement long-lasting, high-performing technologies.

Energy Opportunities, Inc. (EO) provides technical consulting services on projects relating to energy management, efficiency and conservation, renewable energy systems, and the environmental impacts of human enterprises. They understand the synergies between building systems, which is key to optimizing energy performance, at the lowest cost. From new construction and renovations, to net zero energy and deep energy retrofits—they’ve been pushing the efficiency envelope since 1981.

As part of 7group they have developed an international reputation for leading-edge work in the fields of integrative and regenerative design and operations. The key to cost-effective green design is the practice of integrative design.  This multi-disciplinary approach mandates that all design team members participate early in the design process by focusing on ways to downsize or eliminate building systems.  Their efforts on over 100 past projects have resulted in significantly smaller HVAC systems, significantly fewer light fixtures, the elimination of perimeter heating systems, optimized HVAC system location, and other integrated solutions that have reduced both first cost and operating costs. This led to a book on the subject, The Integrative Design Guide to Green Building: Redefining the Practice of Sustainability, published by John Wiley & Sons in 2009.

We have always approached our work from an environmental perspective first and foremost, so certification as a B Corporation allows us to continue our mission of developing solutions to environmental problems even if they do not always maximize profit.  It is one thing to claim that you walk your talk but B Corp certification provides third-party verification that we really do.The Change We Seek™

Fundamentally, EO envisions a world where humans devote their enterprise toward the benefit of all life by fostering mutually beneficial exchanges and relationships between all beings. Humans need to understand that we cannot separate ourselves from the environment.  That which benefits all species provides the maximum benefit for our own species. In short we seek to change people’s hearts and minds one project, and one conversation at a time.

With that broad goal in mind, EO seeks opportunities to engage all stakeholders in the conversation and encourage them to think holistically and systemically in pursuit of synergies that produce realistic solutions.  The development of regenerative intentions is a trajectory of large and small steps in a direction.  They channel their activities in this direction and invite others to come along.

Sweet'tauk, the Montauk, NY based woman owned and operated company, was founded in 2012 by Deborah Aiza to change what is being offered to consumers by creating a bottled lemonade that is 100% fresh using fresh-squeezed and cold-pressed fruit and having less than half the sugar of any competitor. With 100% non-GMO certified ingredients, Sweet'tauk is the first lemonade brand to use the innovative pasteurization technology known as High Pressure Processing (HPP), which ensures every bottle is delicious and safe to drink and you can enjoy every ingredient as it was meant to taste –pure and refreshing.

Sweet'tauk is a multigenerational favorite that appeals to the entire family - from kids to grandparents. They developed a solid fan base originating out of Montauk's beach-surf community, extending throughout the Hamptons, into the NY Metro area.

We became a B Corp so we could instill and preserve our values into our brand and company culture. Our mission is to provide the greatest tasting, healthiest lemonades while sourcing, producing, distributing and marketing our product in a manner consistent with our Quadruple Bottom Line business model which is centered on the four Ps: People, Planet, Profit and Purpose.

Through the quality of our products and the integrity of our company, we endeavour to meet an emerging standard in the business world for managing productivity in a way that fosters authentic social responsibility and environmental awareness. Being a Certified B Corp provides the framework, accountability and transparency to help us follow our mission while growing the business.

The Change We Seek	

Sweet'tauk’s main ingredient is water. People come to Montauk year-round to be in or on the water and experience the natural beauty of this special environment. Sweet'tauk realized that more than 780 million people don't have access to safe water systems. That's why it supports non-profits that have expertise in water preservation, sanitation and hygiene to help create sustainable water systems both locally and globally.

Sweet'tauk supports the health and happiness of our planet and our community. They are committed to helping our caring community and supporting local charitable programs, including schools, which promote healthy eating habits and aid their efforts in supporting school gardening programs. Sweet'tauk says thank-you to their neighbors by helping to maintain the open spaces they all enjoy and supporting sustainability.

These two core components combine to focus Sweet'tauk on making their great tasting fresh lemonades in a manner that recognizes the responsibility they have to the planet, their people, customers, suppliers, and everyone whose lives they touch. Sweet'tauk as a business is a force for good.

This translates into five core values and goals for the company: Have a positive net effect on the environment and operate within eco-friendly values. Create and maintain mutually beneficial relationships with the suppliers and colleagues in their community and industry.Advance our mission through social entrepreneurship.Provide our customers with a high quality product made in an ethical and responsible manner. Inspire others to make great things in a good way for fun and profit.

Convinced that our nature and essence perfectly match with the B Corporation, we worked for 6 months and got 108 points of 200 in the application process. We are part of the B Corporation Net, since November 2014. 

The Change We Seek	

We consider Maggacup as the arrowhead of women and humanity empowerment, through the healthy manage and interaction with our own body. It has impact in three levels: individual, community and humanity. Individually speaking, it impacts positivily in the self-esteem, in the sexual and reproductive health, resulting in the woman²s empowerment. At the comunity level, the effect of individual empowerment, is families and insititutions empowerment; and active citizen participation bio-social-educational. And because of the preservation and restitution of the environment, we get the humanity empowerment (ex: Girl Effect, www.girleffect.org).

Magga means "way in the middle" and it is our mantra. We are a social and economic company and both aspects have the same value for us and are permanently interacting and balancing.

While the menstrual cup is starting to have the largest circulation in Argentina, most women are using pads and tampons. Argentina In a year generates 3.38 billion units in wipes and tampons. They are products with very short shelf life and are pathogenic wastes that are not treatable or recyclable by waste collection systems. They are hazardous materials because they can be infected with infectious diseases. Furthermore, the raw material for the production of wipes and pads is Kraft pulp or fluff pulp involving 60% of the weight of these methods. Produced from the monoculture of exotic trees. Which it is associated with harmful effects on soil, waterways, vegetation and native fauna. In conclusion, consumption of wipes and tampons mean consumption of the planet's resources and degradation.The INTI (National Institute of Industrial Technology) tested for health fitness of the raw material used to manufacture according to the criteria and standards of the European Pharmacopoeia.The Faculty of Pharmacy and Biochemistry of the UBA (University of Buenos Aires) conducted testings of skin irritation.The industrial design of Maggacup is patented and registered with the INPI (National Institute of Industrial Property).Maggacup is registered in the National Administration of Drugs, Food and Medical Technology (ANMAT).

The Humble Shoe Company, Inc. - dba AERA - philosophy has been built on three principles, and everything we do adheres to
them.

“Good for You”: Our shoes are beautifully designed, made by artisans in Veneto, Italy, are of the highest quality and comfort, are accessible (within the luxury market segment) and timeless.
“Good for People”: We only work with highly ethical, like-minded suppliers, who pay their employees, at the least, a living wage. We will share our success with all our employees and invest in their well-being.
“Good for the Planet”: We use high quality, vegan, eco-friendly materials and processes, as much as possible, without jeopardizing our first principle. We then scientifically measure all the environmental impacts of our shoes (through conducting LCA studies on all the shoes we make), transparently present the impacts via our website, and then work with certified third parties to offset them by 110%, thus not only reversing our environmental impacts, but actually leaving the planet better off.

AERA shoes are PETA certified Vegan and certified Carbon Negative.
column10: Certified Vegan and Carbon Negative Luxury Women's Footwear

Hepburn Wind is the owner and operator of Australia’s first community-owned wind farm. 

Hepburn Wind is located at Leonards Hill, about 100km north-west of Melbourne, just south of Daylesford Victoria. The 4.1 MW wind farm hosts two turbines called Gale and Gusto, who have been producing enough clean energy for over 2000 homes since June 2011.
 
With 2002 member shareholders, at the project’s core is the shared desire to take constructive action against climate change and in the process directly benefit the community. The project has demonstrated that, under the right conditions, communities will overwhelmingly support renewable energy and the benefits can be spread widely throughout a community.

Established in 1988, Goldfarb Financial has always emphasized Capitalism Doing Good®. We believes in Empowerment through Education. We practice this principle not just with our clients but the entire community. 

We strive to offer our clients investment options and portfolios that match their values. We believe a person’s portfolio is an important extension of their values. In an industry where success should be built on trust, we believe it’s important that our clients see not only long term financial returns, but social returns as well. That is why it’s important we develop a dialogue with each of our clients to better understand who they are and what their priorities are. Your investments can help shape the world.

Rather than limiting our clients’ options to fit a specific end goal in global sustainability, we at choose to look at companies as a whole. With inclusive screens we are able to align our clients’ values with the positive impacts companies may have on the world.

We are hoping to redefine the measure of success; how leaving a positive impact on the world should be considered when making decisions. That is why we strive to do our part in leaving a positive mark on the local community of Buffalo, NY and New Orleans, LA.

League of Extraordinary Women is an organisation that provides female entrepreneurs the power to connect, be inspired and supported by others just like them. They exist to contribute to the entrepreneurial eco-system and in particular support females on their entrepreneurial journey.

They do this by focusing on creating genuine and real connections between female entrepreneurs through their online community and face-to-face through meet ups in each state.

Ultimately they exist to connect, inspire and empower female entrepreneurs and do this through 3 pillars:League Monthly Membership. Females that are at any stage of their business life whether it be aspiring entrepreneurs, startup entrepreneurs or entrepreneurs. This membership fee allows members to connect with other female entrepreneurs through:Online Members Portal: Members are provided with a login and password to an exclusive members only portal which gives them access to resources, watch videos, peruse the business directory and share their story.Round Table Real Talk: An organised forum of 8 to 10 League Members where real talk discussions are had over a specific topic. Each participant gets 15 minutes to present a challenge and receive feedback. The aim of this round table is to provide a deeper and meaningful conversation between the female entrepreneurs involved. This is in trial in Melbourne and will be rolled out across all cities in Australia. They are currently working on building guidelines so that this is a scalable model.Face-to-Face Meet Ups: Informal meet up events occur at least every 6 weeks to bring together the female entrepreneurs in each city. These are hosted by the city’s Ambassador in each location, who is passionate about connecting women in business. Ambassadors lead The League movement in their community and organise, host and facilitate face-to-face connections. Ambassadors are empowered to find female entrepreneurs to share their stories at these meet ups.Run the World Conference: A one day conference that runs once a year to showcase 8 incredibly successful female entrepreneurs to share their story on stage with over 350 people in attendance. These conferences are recorded and uploaded to their members portal so that it can be accessed by all members.The League App: Currently in concept phase, The League is developing the world's first app that will allow female entrepreneurs across the globe to connect with each other based on location. Female entrepreneurs will be able to communicate through the app in messages and organise in-person meet ups and the Round Table Real Talk forums.

We believe that what we do impacts and inspires those around us. We are all interconnected and through our positive and purposeful values, we are able to provide women with the support throughout their entrepreneurial journey to reach their full potential.

The Change We Seek	

League of Extraordinary Women is an organisation that seeks to change the landscape of female entrepreneurship worldwide, by promoting entrepreneurship as a possibility for all females to achieve. The League does this by sparking authentic conversations that inspire growth, creativity and passion in the women they reach. By doing so, the League facilitates the cultivation of the female entrepreneur ecosystem worldwide.
column10: Online platform for Female Entrepreneurs that encourages connection

Pete and Gerry's Organic Eggs produces eggs under the Pete and Gerry's Organic, Nellie's Free Range, and Consider Pastures brands. The company is a fourth generation family farm located in the foothills of New Hampshire's White Mountains.
 
The company has a strong history of leadership in the egg industry, demonstrating for over decade that consumers demand and are will to pay more for humanely- and ethically-produced eggs from small family farms. Pete and Gerry's became America's first Certified Humane egg producer in 2003, and in 2013 the company became America's first egg producer to achieve the B Corp certification. Pete and Gerry's completed its transition to 100% Certified Humane Free-Range production in 2014.
 
Currently approximately 90% of eggs consumed in the US come from hens who live their entire life on factory farms in cramped cages. These giant egg factories are not environmentally sustainable, and have pushed most family scale-producers out of business through consolidation.
 
Pete and Gerry's Organic Eggs produces its Certified Humane Free-Range eggs on over 120 small family farms. These farms are better for the environment, their communities, and consumers. The company seeks to lead a revolution in the way we produce eggs throughout the US.
column10: Certified Humane Free Range and Organic Eggs

Mission Markets is an online electronic transactions and communications platform designed to unite impact investors with businesses and organizations that positively impact humanity and life on Earth. Mission Markets enables investors access to a regulated electronic transactions platform, associated information, communications services, impact metrics, other data, analytics and investment management tools that facilitate private capital transactions.

The founders of Mission Markets have combined their capital markets and private company finance expertise with their passion for social welfare and environmental conservation to create Mission Markets. At Mission Markets they believe that by providing impact reporting alongside financial reporting, investment dollars will flow to the projects and organizations that extract the greatest impact per dollar invested.

Mission Markets facilitates the impact investing sphere's transition from a disorganized and dispersed collection of organizations into a unified and thriving marketplace. Mission Markets makes impact investing easier, more effective, and more personal.

We at Mission Markets chose to become a B Corporation because we believe that all businesses should balance profit with purpose, contributing to the betterment of society and life on the planet. The B Corporation approach aligns a company’s mission, actions, and corporate structure with this vision. We are proud to be a part of a growing group of companies with whom we share the same vision and objectives.The Change We Seek	

Our mission is to create a marketplace that enhances the flow of sustainable investments into businesses and organizations that generate measurable social and environmental impacts, thereby improving humanity and life on Earth.

• Mission markets enhances the flow of sustainable investments by facilitating the establishment of markets, capital raising, secondary liquidity, standardized reporting, communication and information sharing, and other activities that increase funding for our listed businesses and organizations.

• Businesses and organizations that positively impact humanity and life on earth focus on products, services, clients, suppliers, and partners that solve real problems, provide double and triple bottom line value, provide real value, and increase social wealth, whether local or global, through their practices. These organizations identify objectives that transcend profits, and establish and report on concrete metrics to evaluate their impacts. By doing so, they serve as examples for other organizations to learn how to be better global citizens.

• We consider businesses and organizations that improve humanity as those that include activities that help individuals, groups, organizations, and cultures live dignified, enriched, healthy, safe, and happy lives.

• We consider businesses and organizations that improve life on Earth as those that work towards the maintenance of Earth’s ecosystem services, ecological stability, biological diversity, species richness, and natural and aesthetic beauty.

Bench Brewing Company crafts premium quality, award winning IPAs, ales, lagers, and barrel-aged sours.

Bench is located on 8-acres of farmland in Ontario’s beautiful Niagara Region. River City has offices based in Richmond and Petersburg with a third office coming to Hanover County in late 2015. River City serves individuals from across Metro Richmond and the Tri-Cities areas. With a staff of approximately 90, River City is well equipped to meet client’s needs. Each River City employee is required to meet certain standards and certifications which include a thorough background check, First Aid, CPR and Crisis Wave (a state approved restraint process). All staff meet educational and state standards for the work they do in the field. All program directors are master level clinicians with many currently under supervision to become licensed clinicians. River City was recently ranked 1st in the Healthcare & Biotechnology industry category and 13th overall on the 2014 Inner City 100 list of fastest-growing inner city businesses in the U.S. in Fortune Magazine (see article here). In December 2014, River City became a Certified B Corporation through the nonprofit B Lab.

We became a B Corp because we believe that business has a higher social purpose which was evident in the “River City Way” and how RIver City operated from inception. Many of our employees can attest to the numerous pro-bono clients we have served, assisted with housing, transported and gone above and beyond for – because we at River City truly care not only about the work we do, but also the people we serve. Becoming a B Corporation was a natural fit for River City as it allows us to be a part of another business community while also playing a part in the larger strategic plan to be the best River City that we can be.

The Change We Seek	

River City is wholeheartedly committed to the overall biological, psychological, social, and spiritual health and well-being of their clients. They focus on reducing or alleviating the emotional, mental, and behavioral distress resulting from psychiatric and substance abuse conditions. River City believes that every client they encounter is capable of achieving an improved quality of life and they work with them through the delivery of professional psychiatric and substance abuse services provided by a multidisciplinary team of mental health providers who are committed to quality care to achieve their goals.

Based out of Grass Valley, California Encanto is an eco-friendly jewelry company specializing in Tagua pieces sustainably sourced from Colombia. Monica Farbiarz founded the company in 2007 to empower herself to become economically independent while creating an ethical, conscientious business. Encanto has recently become a member of the Fair Trade Federation and a B Corporation. After establishing a strong presence in the wholesale market for seven years, the company is expanding to retail to make the products more accessible.
 
Monica works with fair trade materials which highlight the beauty found in nature. Tagua (pronounced TAG-wah) is a seed from a palm-like tree that grows in the tropical rainforests of South America. Because of its rich natural color and shiny texture, Tagua closely resembles ivory and is thus known as the vegetable ivory. The harvesting of Tagua preserves vital rainforest land and habitat while discouraging harming elephants for ivory. By purchasing Encanto's products, customers are also helping to preserve a more viable way of life for many Colombians. 
 
Encanto works closely with the supplier from the design phase all the way through production by communicating with them on a daily basis.

During one of his early morning moments of clarity, surfer and long-time yogi David Prior was inspired to create a product that would allow him to have a clear, ecological conscience. Thus was born five:am – a range of purely organic yoghurts and granolas. Over time, five:am has achieved their vision of taking organic yoghurt from a health food niche, into the mainstream, therefore making it more affordable and accessible for all.

Five:am has evolved to be a huge success story, but as a company has remained honest and true – reflecting David’s vision, beliefs and daily mantra. Every day; five:am asks its team and its consumers to “wake up, be amazing”

Five:am’s products are all organic and natural meaning they are completely free of anything nasty. All the milk used in five:am’s yoghurt range is sourced from The Organic Dairy Farmer’s Co-operative in Victoria, a group of farms dedicated to upholding the highest standards of sustainable and organic farming.

The milk travels from the happy cows, to the co-operative, and then just up the road to the bustling home of five:am in Carrum Downs, Melbourne. It is here that five:am has refined its yoghurteering technique in order to create the best-tasting yoghurt and granola in the world. And that’s just what you’ll get – organic, world’s BEST taste, made with love.

We are honoured to have achieved B Corp Certification and urge other companies to jump on board. For us, B Corp is about celebrating our culture at five:am and it encourages us to take further steps in the right direction.The Change We Seek	

David has lead the five:am team by constantly implementing a strong set of values. The five:am team focus on the following core beliefs:The work environment is a safe and welcoming placeProduct quality is King, which ensures the happiness of each and every customerTotal respect for nature and there is a constant drive to restore the environment

Five:am hopes to continually drive their passion to influence others in regards to appreciating and giving back to nature.

Five:am seeks to encourage others to embrace the five:am lifestyle & mantra. It is so easy and only takes 2 steps: wake up, be amazing!

This is about living a balanced lifestyle; loving your work – but also taking time to relax, regenerate and reflect. The five:am team & their consumers – affectionately known as five:amers – aim to set aside a slice of every day to enjoy a few moments of clarity and peace.

BacTech is an environmental technology company that applies naturally-occurring bacteria to remediate mine waste, also known as tailings.

The bacteria, harmless to both humans and the environment, work inside stainless-steel bioreactors under optimal conditions. The technology provides a "Garden of Eden" environment for the bacteria to thrive and multiply and permits them to achieve in 6 days what would normally take 20 years to occur naturally.

During this process, the bacteria are able to:Remove the source of acid generation (sulphides) and prevent future Acid Rock Drainage (ARD)Stabilize toxic elements and prevent heavy metals (such as Arsenic) from being releasedRecover valuable metals from the tailings which in turn funds the operation of the plant

The by-products created by bioleaching are benign and zero environmental damage occurs as a result. Through the selective recovery of valuable metals, bioleaching is an environmental reclamation solution that can also create a profit.



As an alternative and natural solution to mine waste remediation, we wanted to highlight our commitment to sustainability and distinguish ourselves from conventional approaches to tailings clean-ups. Becoming a B Corp helps us connect with like-minded business and offers us recognition in the impact investment community.

The Change We Seek	

The worldwide contamination caused by historic abandoned mines and tailings is so widespread that it is neither quantified nor fully evaluated. In countries with a long history of mining, the magnitude of the problem is considerable; these areas are generally laden with toxic elements that leach into the surrounding areas. The public is increasingly demanding that the governments and companies responsible address the contamination due to the negative consequences of such sites.

Unfortunately, many of these historic sites have been left behind by companies that no longer exist. Governments who have “inherited” these liabilities often lack the funds to effectively clean up all of the sites under their watch. Current practice in the industry calls for clay caps to be used on tailings to eliminate oxygen getting to the sulphides . This is a band-aid solition as the sulphides remain in the tailings, which allows for the possibility of future ARD contamination.

BacTech proposes to permanently “cure the patient” of contaminated tailings sites by removing the source of the acid, the sulphides, at NO COST to the community or government. The alternative is decades-long site monitoring and treatment costs as ARD continues to be produced.

From strategic planning to responsible event management, Takt-etik deploys an armada of expertise and skills for organizations looking to reduce their environmental impact as well as positioning themselves on the responsible business checkerboard. Through its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, it has worked with more than a hundred organizations and has classified more than 60 events with the sustainable event management provincial standard (BNQ 9700-253).


Takt-etik also seeks to positively influence its clients, partners and community by “walking the talk”. The company promotes transparency by producing its sustainability report and GHG declaration. Twice a year, all employees meet to openly discuss the strategic orientation and constantly work on finding innovative ways to assist their clients on their own sustainable path.

Qero fights against the environmental scourge of disposable cups by replacing them for reusable ones. The ultimate goal of Qero is to help provoke a cultural change by making people aware of the harmful effects of using disposable items, focusing on communication, high quality products and great service.
 
 Qero handles a 360® scope of the business, from the production of cups, washing and drying services, assessment in communication and calculation of environmental impact metrics, and finally the recycling of damaged cups (less than 1%) into other sustainable products such as portable trash cans or bike mudguards.
 
 Qero's main customers are festivals, beverage companies, artisan beer brewers, corporate and state offices, all of which have embraced the habit of reusing. In the first 4 years since its birth, the company has been able to avoid the use of 50 million disposable cups, which represent 800 tons of plastic waste and 3.000 tons of CO2 emissions.
column10: Reusable cups for all kind of occasions

Little Sun is at once an inclusive social business, a global project, and a way of connecting the world through sharing light and energy. Founded in 2012 by artist Olafur Eliasson and engineer Frederik Ottesen, Little Sun is invested in delivering clean solar products as well as raising awareness about the importance of sustainable energy for all through special projects and events around the world. The Berlin-based company’s eponymous first product, the Little Sun Original solar LED lamp, was developed to get clean, reliable, affordable light to the 1.2 billion people worldwide without access to electricity living in ‘off-grid’ areas, with a particular focus on Sub-Saharan Africa. In 2016 the second product, Little Sun Charge – a solar phone charger and lamp, was launched. It is being followed in 2017 by the Little Sun Diamond, a sparkling and beautiful smaller solar lamp.

People Against Dirty is a company made up of two brands – method and Ecover – filled with fearless thinkers, mad scientists and adventurous designers who believe in defying the status quo with innovation and optimism. They take cleaning seriously – but not themselves. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in San Francisco, method (methodhome.com) is the pioneer of premium planet-friendly and design-driven home, fabric and personal care products. Formulated with naturally derived, biodegradable ingredients, method puts the hurt on dirt without doing harm to people, creatures or the planet. Also playing an important role at People Against Dirty is Ecover (ecover.com) the revered pioneering European-based line of ecological cleaning products that has had an enormous impact on the world of cleaning – and a positive impact on the environment – since its formation in 1980.
  
People Against Dirty is in business to change business. In the same way they take the dirt out of cleaning, they strive to eliminate some of business's dirty practices. They believe their business practices and processes should be as clean as the products they make. In that spirit, People Against Dirty develop formulas and design their products to consider the past, present and future.

Food Connect is a social enterprise connecting local farmers and eaters in South East Queensland for over 13 years. They are transforming the food system taking a rights-based approach rather than seeing food as a commodity. Using a true-cost model, Food Connect returns a fair price to regenerative farmers using a unique community distribution model, reducing food miles to an average of 140km per week. Staff are engaged in democratic decision making and customers are treated to a weekly supply of healthy, whole foods from fabulous farmers and food makers.
 
Everyone in the food value chain should be rewarded fairly and treated ethically for their part in producing, processing and delivering the food we enjoy. That food should be sourced as locally as possible, thereby reducing the carbon footprint, revitalising rural and remote communities, and stimulating local economic development. Food Connect's model has been replicated in a number of locations in Australia and its relentless advocacy has helped to grow the 'Fair Food Movement' across the nation.

EcoZoom is a social enterprise dedicated to bringing ecological products to the all the world’s consumers. They believe that all people should have access to beautifully designed products that will improve their health, income and environment. EcoZoom started with improved cookstoves because they saw that as one of the biggest needs in the world. They’re the company's flagship products. But, their office in Kenya also sells solar lamps, water filters, and reusable sanitary pads to help create a more holistic healthy home solution and transform lives.
More than 3 billion people – almost half the world’s population – do not have access to modern fuels like electricity and gas. They cook with biomass, often on smoky three stone fires or inefficient, unimproved stoves and light their homes with costly and dangerous kerosene lamps. These practices result in huge impacts to people and the environment including: the death of over 4 million people a year, over 30% of monthly income being used to pay for fuel, deforestation and climate change. EcoZoom's products provide a solution and they work to make them accessible and affordable in developing countries. 

Operating a for-profit company in a space dominated by governments, NGOs and aid organizations can create some skepticism. We became a B Corp to demonstrate our high level of commitment to our social and environmental missions. We believe in the power of business to create change and think social enterprises will be instrumental in creating sustainable markets for durable goods in developing countries.The Change We Seek	

EcoZoom seeks a world where everyone’s basic needs - like cooking, lighting and water - are met in a healthy, efficient and ecofriendly way.

They first launched in 2016, with their two founders, Emilie & Deepak, packing fruit & veg in a small area in South-West London. Since then, they’ve grown all across the South-East with plans to go nationwide, bringing in even more people to eat good, do good, and stay odd.

column7: Mr. Green Africa, the first recycling company to be a Certified B Corporation on the African continent, leverages business as a force for good to realize sustainable, long-term social, environmental and economic impact through the collection, conversion and selling of post consumer plastic waste. Our technology driven plastics collection model enables waste collection at the source, integrating informal waste workers, micro-entrepreneurs and consumers into our formal value chain, increasing the amount of post-consumer plastic waste Mr. Green Africa collects and providing stakeholders the chance to earn a fair, predictable and transparent income and benefits. Our world class processing equipment, housed at our factory in Nairobi Kenya, allows Mr. Green Africa to convert locally collected plastic waste into high-quality post consumer recyclates (PCR) and sell it as a substitute to imported virgin plastics at competitive rates. To close the loop, Mr. Green Africa works closely with brand owners and third party plastics manufactures to develop and execute three-way off take agreements for high quality PCR, helping FMCGs and others realize their sustainable packaging goals by accessing ethically sourced, locally produced PCR.

Pour le Monde's name says it all (For the World). They're about educating and providing consumers alternatives to synthetic perfumes, which can be unhealthy for the environment and ourselves.
 
Pour le Monde was created by Wendi Berger, a self-confessed perfume junkie and former fashion and beauty magazine executive. During her pregnancy, she was advised by her doctor to eliminate her beloved perfumes due to the chemicals in them and the unknown effects they may have on her unborn child. She was shocked to discover the health risks tied to the conventional perfumes that she loved. Studies show that petrochemicals in fragrances—particularly synthetic musk—are endocrine disruptors. Traces of fragrance ingredients have been found in breast tissue, breast milk, and aquatic life.
 
Yet, when Wendi attempted to hunt down a natural scent that suited her, she came up empty. None of the available fragrances rivaled her favorites, nor did they offer a truly natural option. Surprisingly, they still contained a small percentage of synthetic ingredients that could prove harmful. Eyeing a hole in the marketplace, she embarked on a long journey to create the Pour le Monde collection, the only certified 100% natural fine fragrances on the market.

The milkround’s back with a vengeance! Supermarkets have commoditised food and wrapped it in plastic, but Modern Milkman's app and return and reuse packaging give users convenience with a conscience at the push of a button. Eliminating waste and pollution calls for businesses to give back what they put in, and work together to create a brighter, greener future, in which collecting, washing and reusing packaging is the norm. Modern Milkman began as a local milkround in Colne, Lancashire, with four friends and a beat-up old van that barely passed its MOT. Fast forward a few years and it's now a network of British dairies, independent suppliers and thousands of brew-sipping treat-lovers, working together to reduce waste across the UK. Modern Milkman is a Certified B Corporation working to prevent plastic from polluting our planet, one bottle and doorstep at a time. Earthbound Farm, a unit of Danone North America, is one of North America’s heritage organic brands and one of the largest growers of organic produce. Founded in 1984 on 2½-acres in Carmel Valley, California by Drew & Myra Goodman, Earthbound Farm grew from that small local farm to become one of the first large scale organic vegetable farms by partnering with third-generation conventional farmers who converted land and learned to farm organically while bringing efficient farming practices to organic farming. It is a company built on the social, economic, and environmental benefits of organic.

Fulfilling its mission to cultivate a healthier world through organic food and farming, Earthbound Farm been a catalyst for positive change by converting thousands of acres from conventional chemical farming to organic farming practices that protect the air, water and food supply; by making organic produce more affordable and accessible in supermarkets across North America; and by making its clamshell packages from 100% Post-Consumer Recycled PET (PCR PET). By making its packages from PCR PET, Earthbound Farm creates a market for recycled beverage bottles, keeping about 40 million pounds of plastic out of landfills every year.

Earthbound Farm is a subsidiary of Danone North America, also a Certified B Corp. To learn more about Danone North America's B Corp Certification, please visit their B Impact Report by searching them in the B Corp Directory bar below.

Laudex is a Mexican student-lending business that supports bottom of the pyramid to middle-income individuals reach and accomplish university or graduate studies. All of Laudex loans are structured to optimize the student’s repayment capability, both during studies and after graduation.  The requirements, credit analysis and legal documents of all of our products are designed to assure a solid portfolio and an economically sustainable business model.


We decided to become a B-Corp because we believe that Mexico’s future rests upon its youth education, a skilled populace is vital to overcome poverty. Beyond any doubt education plays a pivotal role in the development and progress of any country.


Laudex differs from other student-loan business by offering students and their families, college loans based on flexible tuition schemes with minimum monthly payments. By 2025, it is projected that Laudex would have supported more than 8,000 young students in Mexico accomplish university or graduate studies.




The Change We Seek®


Laudex provides loans to university and graduate students so they may obtain a quality higher education regardless of their economic background. Mexico’s university enrollment, at roughly 28%, is at an unacceptably low level due to very limited public university capacity and a disproportionate un-affordability of quality private universities. Through student financing, Laudex is contributing to bridge this critical economic gap and create higher educational opportunities for young Mexicans.

Terra Genesis International works with companies in a way that they didn't realize they needed. At the source of what TGI does are the Principles of Regeneration that guide the team to work in a way that aims at capacity building for all stakeholders, not just finite deliverables.
 
 The TGI team grew out of the ecological agriculture field and realized that systemic change in agriculture was more likely to come through supply systems rather than through the development of individual farmers. It was this thinking that has guided the company to now work with some of the top natural products companies to help transform the way they do business and specifically to understand their relationship to their supply in a whole new way.
 
 The process of engaging with supply in a way that uplifts the whole leads the system to strengthen in ways that, among other things, sequesters more carbon into our soils, strengthens our communities, reconnects consumers to the source of their products, and empowers farmers to innovate.

Sorriso e Salute is one of the first Clinic for Biological & Holistic Dentistry and Integrated Medicine in the world to receive the B Corp certificate. 
 
The Clinic is located in Italy, minutes away from Venice and was founded by Doctor Raimondo Pische, President of AIOB (International association of biological dentistry). 
 
The Clinic mission is: Òto improve our patientÕs overall health, while serving as a force for well-being and improvement for our collaborators, suppliers, local community and environmentÓ.
 
Sorriso e Salute is strongly committed to operate in the highest respect of the human body, by banishing the use of mercury in dental fillings, as well as following a strict procedure to guarantee its safest removal for intoxicated patients, by using bio-compatible materials and by running a metal free supply chain. The Clinic believes that only one medicine exists: Òthe one that curesÓ and so approaches its patients with a Holistic mind-set, implying that teeth and organism are deeply interconnected and hence an aching tooth can be a signal that something else in our body needs attention, and vice versa.

SavinGreen was established to demonstrate that adopting the principles of "people, planet, profits"_, a commercial business model could be created to enable all Australians to be involved in contributing to environmental sustainability, simply by making a conscious choice about where services they use everyday are obtained from. Their model is not reliant on government legislation, is simple, understandable, and achieved without additional charge to, or excessive investment of time by their clients.
 
 SavinGreen captures the power of consumerism via their "Tree Planting Policy." This directly ties the action and decision of our consumers to the planting of trees, not to company profit. Based on the terms of this Policy, SavinGreen makes voluntary contributions to Carbon Neutral, an Australian Profit for Purpose Company based in W.A, specializing in native biodiversity reforestation. The impact of this activity extends well beyond simply planting trees: it impacts positively on the native fauna, the local community and our climate. Through this model SavinGreen has been responsible for the planting of over 50,000 trees and is a Platinum Supporter of Carbon Neutral.

In 1983, two young marine biologists borrowed $500 from their families and planted oyster seed on a five-acre lease in Tomales Bay, CA. They began with the aim of growing the highest quality, local Pacific oysters for San Francisco’s half-shell market. This hands-on commitment to quality remains a core value of the business today.
 
With a mission to grow, shuck and serve an exceptional oyster experience – and have fun doing it – Hog Island Oyster Co. has built namesake restaurants in San Francisco and Napa and an outdoor oyster bar, picnic tables, and retail shop at their farm in Marshall, on Tomales Bay. Known for an unusually large number of long-term employees -- aka the Hog Island Family -- the company has created a culture of people who care about their communities, their environments and the customers they serve. They call this their ‘Bay to Bar’ philosophy –every step, and every person, plays an equally important role in setting and meeting the company’s high standards for great food and great service.
 
Hog Island Oyster Co. currently leases one hundred and sixty acres in Tomales Bay, CA and sells over 5 million oysters, Manila clams and mussels per year.

Gardener’s Supply is 100% employee-owned and was founded in 1983 by a handful of enthusiastic Vermont gardeners. Today, the company serves millions of gardeners nationwide and is known for its’ award-winning gardening products. Though the company has grown, it remains passionately committed to help people experience the joys of gardening in harmony with nature.
 
When visiting Gardener’s at its corporate headquarters and retail store in Burlington’s Intervale, it’s hard to believe that what is now beautiful gardens, farms and trails was formerly a landfill. In 1986, Gardener’s Supply spearheaded an Intervale clean-up effort to restore the Intervale – 700 acres of bottomland within the city limits of Burlington, Vermont – to its agricultural roots and feed Burlington.
 
Gardener's Supply actively promotes gardening as an important way for people to make the world a better place. The company donates 8% of profits to support programs and organizations that are using gardening to improve the quality of people's lives and the health of our environment. The company provides garden grants across the U.S. and in Vermont that focus on gardening and hunger-relief supporting many community gardens, urban farms and workplace gardens.

Snoqualmie Ice Cream is a family-owned company that makes super-premium, natural and organic craft ice cream in Snohomish, Washington. The ice cream is made with extra cream, lots of eggs and very little air, creating the most rich and velvety treat.
 
 They stand firm in only using simple ingredients from the Pacific Northwest, including USDA Organic-certified grass-fed milk and cream, eggs and berries. Everything they make is vat-pasteurized to slow cook the ingredients without scorching the cream and allowing each flavor to have its own unique recipe.
 
 Snoqualmie believes in the power of sustainability. They purposely designed their property with rain gardens, bio-swales and pervious concrete to completely eliminate runoff. Their solar panels, compressor waste heat recovery, LED sensor lighting and energy efficient equipment has allowed them to significantly reduce their energy usage.

Green House Data is a VMware vCloud powered partner, SSAE 16 Type II and HIPAA compliant, as well as an EPA Green Power Partner. In addition to passing on cost savings achieved through energy efficiency, the company offers 24/7/365 live customer support and a 100% uptime SLA.

Green House Data strives to build innovative IT business value for every client, every single day. They are passionate stewards of customer data and systems, balancing high availability with high performance, security, and service. Avocado is redefining what it means to be a sustainable, ethical brand. Their vision is as urgent as it is aspirational—a world united by sustainability and social responsibility. They make eco-luxury, organic certified mattresses and bedding. Avocado practices radical transparency and a “farm-to-bedroom” approach; they co-own a latex farm, factory, and wool collective in India—from where they source and process raw materials. Mattresses are then handcrafted in a Los Angeles factory that they also own. Their materials, factory and finished products are GOTS/GOLS organic certified. Their mattresses are also GREENGUARD Gold certified for low emissions, MADE SAFE® certified, and have achieved STANDARD 100 by OEKO-TEX® for both human and ecological safety. As a Climate Neutral® Certified business, Avocado is the world’s first mattress brand to achieve negative carbon emissions across its entire business scope. As long standing members of 1% for the Planet, one percent of all revenue is donated to environmental nonprofit members on an annual basis.

Harrogate Water is super proud to carry the baton for today’s generation and future generations, in providing natural source water for all to enjoy from the beautiful spa town of Harrogate. The business is at the heart of the community; a centre of manufacturing excellence, quality employment and training, balancing performance with environmental sustainability and social engagement.
The story begins in 1571 when the town’s unique waters were discovered by the physician to Queen Elizabeth; the town later became the first British spa and Harrogate water was bottled in 1740, becoming the original British bottled water. 
Today, Harrogate Spring is celebrated for its history and heritage, provenance and taste, the official water of Royal Ascot and the Royal Albert Hall and the water of choice for British Airways and Hilton Hotels. It’s the No1 British premium bottled water and ‘out of home’ water brand. 
With each step to improve performance and environmental efficiency, Harrogate Water seeks to give something back. This ethos was behind the launch of Thirsty Planet water. To date, more than £2.3 million has been raised for charity partner Pump Aid, providing clean water, improved sanitation and sustainable job creation for communities in sub-Saharan Africa.

Door to Door Organics is an online grocer that delivers fresh, high-quality organic produce and natural groceries directly to homes, offices, and schools throughout Colorado, Chicago, Kansas City, and Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware. The company partners with farmers who are dedicated stewards of the land and use USDA-certified organic practices that are healthier for both animals and people, better for the soil, and reduce carbon emissions. Door to Door Organics’s shop-by-recipe and meal planning tools make it simple to eat delicious local, seasonal food that supports health, the communities it serves, and the environment.

Our mission is to bring more Good Food -- food that positively impacts health, communities, and the environment -- to more people in a sustainable way. Beyond the sourcing of our products and our delivery and packing practices, we make every effort to ensure all aspects of our business are run with the environment and corporate responsibility in mind. We’re constantly seeking ways to innovate, set new standards for excellence, and wow our customers, so becoming a B Corporation will help hold us to a higher level of accountability.

The Change We Seek	

Good Food sounds so simple, but it can be difficult to find in today’s complex food system. That’s why Door to Door Organics strives to be the country’s Good Food advocate. When selecting the freshest, highest quality organic and natural, local and seasonal foods they can deliver, the company weighs many different attributes. Here are examples of questions they ask:

• Does this food support local family farms and the community?

• What distance will this food travel from the farm to a customer’s doorstep?

• Were the animals that produced this food humanely raised?

• Is this grocery item as minimally processed as possible?

Door to Door Organics is dedicated to these principles and believes that in achieving them, the company will make a positive impact on our food system, make people healthier, connect communities, grow local economies, and inspire people to eat Good Food.

Synapse is a paper-free, virtual company that organizes businesses in groups around local nonprofits for the purpose of stimulating connections, collaborations and contributions both between the business members and between them and the nonprofits we partner with.

Each group is called a "Hub" and each Hub is partnered with a nonprofit. Hubs can contain up to 20 members total. Our Hub meetings are either weekly or bi-weekly and follow a carefully developed agenda that lets everyone at the table talk about who they are, what they do, how they do it, and why they do it, plus their personal passions, family, hobbies and so on.

This is followed with a brainstorming session where questions, ideas, connections, comments and so on from the individual comments can be shared and expanded upon. The result is that nonprofits gain valuable ambassadors for their cause as well as volunteers, board members, donations and connections. Business members learn and grow, make useful connections and collaborate with and refer business and ideas to their Hub-mates. The result of all of this is economic and community development that strengthens the business and nonprofit community locally

Since we founded this company, we have practiced the kind of behaviors that typically identify B corps - so we felt that if we became certified, then we could better promote the idea of B corp status to all of our business members by 'walking the walk.'

The Change We Seek	

That the connections, collaborations and contributions that small to medium sized businesses can make with one another and the nonprofit community can be facilitated and maximized to the fullest degree using the Synapse system of networking.

Parque del Recuerdo is the first cemetery in Chile that utilizes a novel concept of landscaping in their services. Over the past 40 years, Parque del Recuerdo has helped families cope with the loss of a loved one. They are committed to provide professional support to those who need it. In the past five years, they have carried out the only existing study about Chilean culture and death. The results have been shared in the community, and they have addressed their strategies based on the needs of individuals, diversifying, for example rites and memorial services. 
 
Since its creation, Parque del Recuerdo has become a popular green space in Santiago- which is one of the world's top ten polluted cities. The gardens are one of the many attractions to the cemetery where you can find every kind of flora and fauna. Parque del Recuerdo spans over 452.2 acres, and it is one of the few resting places for migratory birds.

Manawa means heart and that's what drives us - Honey from the Heart. 
Manawa Honey NZ was founded by the Tuhoe Tuawhenua Trust in Ruatāhuna at the Heart of Māui's Fish (North Island of New Zealand), to sustain our people with jobs and good health, and to keep bees for what they do for our place and this planet. 

The Tūhoe Tuawhenua Trust has a 100-year vision of “Kua tau te iwi me te whenua (People and the natural world thriving harmony)”. Thus, Manawa Honey is ultimately about the development of our people and the enrichment of our forests. 

We specialise in native tree honeys from the untouched forests of Te Urewera - homeland of our tribe, Tūhoe. Our exquisite honeys include Mānuka, Rewarewa, Tāwari, Pua-ā-Tāne - bounty of the God of the Forest.

With our deep expertise at both the front lines and strategic sides of sustainability, we understand its multifaceted nature requires a diversity of perspectives. Carbon Credit Capital (CCC) is a carbon offset management firm. CCC specializes in linking international and local partners to high-quality carbon emission reduction projects in developing and domestic markets. CCC works to reduce carbon emissions, provide climate education, and achieve sustainability goals with corporations, non-profits, small businesses, and universities.
 
CCC is also a wide disseminator of knowledge through print and media. Olivia Fussell, CCC’s managing director, is also a frequent speaker on carbon and clean energy markets.
 
 In 2015, CCC began the Carbon Neutral Checkout™, an opportunity for firms to go completely carbon-neutral at little to no cost. CCC calculates a firm’s carbon footprint associated with the numerous supply-chain stages and offers offsets to neutralize the footprint. The cost is passed on to the end customers and there are no additional costs to the company.
 
Carbon Credit Capital’s (CCC) mission is dedicated to combating climate change and helping businesses and individuals mitigate carbon emissions. Unlike big corporations, CCC recognizes that not every individual, institution, or business has the necessary acumen or resources to make meaningful impact.

Born out of that deep, human desire to leave a legacy, Measure Meant’s journey began in 2017 with the goal of empowering businesses to participate in the hard work of literally saving the world.  
 
Saving the world can be overwhelming—and so is implementing any kind of change at scale. We’ve learned this firsthand through our collective experience advocating for sustainability within organizations large and small. We’ve also found that the greatest heroes have guides who will champion their efforts until the mission is complete. They have a Yoda, a Gandalf, or a Leslie Knope.  
 
Since our inception, we’ve had the opportunity to guide clients of all sizes through some incredible transformations, from a local winery seeking B Corp certification to a national chocolate company committed to sustainability throughout its supply chain. We’ve been able to consistently identify areas of impact and implement lasting change, providing the insight, expertise, and capacity required for the task at hand—everything you need to accomplish world-saving impact.

Culinary Collective is an import and distribution company specializing in gourmet cultural foods that embody and promote their native culture and traditions. They work with small family and community companies that take pride in producing all natural foods using methods and recipes passed down through the generations.
 
All products are completely natural and free of preservatives or colorants. Organic certification is pursued whenever feasible. Products and ingredients are sourced using fair sourcing criteria to ensure that farmers and producers receive a fair price and that no communities are exploited in the trade process. We select our products to promote local traditions and food cultures.

A&R Solar is a team of smart, environmentally conscious specialists who design and install solar energy systems for homeowners, businesses, and government agencies. The company was founded in 2007 as an employee owned venture in Seattle, Washington. As one of the first contractors dedicated to solar installations in Washington State, A&R Solar empowers its customers by helping them take their energy futures into their own hands while minimizing their carbon footprints. 
 
 We started A&R Solar with the idea of changing the way business was done in the world. We wanted to build a business structure that focused on respect for our employees, our customers, our community, and our planet. We believe that by aligning our personal values with our business, we will achieve incredible results.
 
A&R Solar conducts business on a Triple Bottom Line model, measuring success by the social, environmental, and economic impacts it makes. By delivering solar energy solutions to homes and businesses, its activities are slowing the destructive effects of climate change. And at the same time, its customers are gaining energy independence while supporting a local, green economy.

Almaciguera is a consultant company that started in 2012 in Puerto Varas, Chile. Almaciguera develops social responsibility programs and shared values with companies in Chile. They help to generate training, communication and integration strategies with the community, taking into account the large number of productive enterprises in the region and the impact generated in neighboring communities.
 
Almaciguera also developed RED WOMAN SMEs, the largest active network of trade links and business training for women entrepreneurs and businesswomen in southern Chile. They began this work three years ago, connecting regional entrepreneurs together with business training programs and bringing SMEs with financing programs to new markets, thereby decreasing gaps for women in the entrepreneurship field (DIB).

column7: BlueDot (formerly known as BioDiaspora) develops risk assessment technology that enables global leaders to accurately predict and anticipate how emerging infectious disease threats will spread around the world. This capability was scientifically validated during the 2009 H1N1 influenza pandemic and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. BlueDot technology is extensively used by United States Centers for Disease Control, World Health Organization, Public Health Agency of Canada, and other leading institutions that seek to mitigate against the health and economic risks of infectious diseases. BlueDot technology is an advanced web-based enterprise solution that has an integrated live stream of global epidemic intelligence from worldwide infectious disease surveillance systems and contextualizes these threats by integrating an extensive number of datasets pertaining to human and animal populations, climate, health system environments, economic conditions, and many other factors. BlueDot users can conduct in-depth analysis of the continuously evolving architecture of the global airline transportation network and the origins, travel routes, and destinations of more than two billion passengers who pass through it every year.

The Products is a social enterprise that is a response to the lack of innovative, effective and accessible furniture to children and young people with physical disabilities, contemplating on the same product function, performance, beauty, autonomy and security.



The Products' main solutions are Ciranda, a chair that allows all physical disabled children 1-6 years old to sit on the floor and play with others as an equal, and the first Inclusive School Desk based on the principles of universal design. Innovative, both products enable people with disabilities to fully exercise their citizenship - in all, this audience consists of 3 million children and young people in Brazil (IBGE, 2010).



The scarce equipment available in the market so far are heavily associated with the idea of "sickness", they are also costly and not very efficient. Ineffective products, such as these, end up causing a social handicap, mainly in the first years of childhood for handiCapable children, when inclusion is most importance in their formation as a citizen.



One of the main challenges of the 21st century is to create new ways of undertaking, which means changing old habits to embrace the new, the daring, the innovative, and the committed to the action. Means do not aim to profit at the expense of issues related to the social, environmental and economic ills that plague the society from the very beginning we try to be present by those who somehow believe in this form of activity. 



Becoming a Certificated B Corp proves our commitments, it was recognized worldwide and finally uses parameters and metrics that we believe are fundamental for our type of business. Working in the certification process itself is an opportunity to enhance our operating model showing points that we need to grow, rethink and give us the opportunity to enhance a better governance process.

The Change We Seek	



The Products seeks to improve society through an innovative and profitable business model aimed at greater equality of opportunities. They are providing products for the inclusion of physically disabled children, so that in the future they may be inserted productively in the community with all their rights and obligations. Creating innovative technologies and generating a stream of innovations that aim to reduce social inequality for a part of the population that until recently depended solely on society is the purpose of their business.

The Honest Company is a leading lifestyle brand whose mission is to inspire and empower people to live a healthy life.

The Honest Company was started by a mom and a dad who, like many modern parents, had become increasingly concerned about poorly regulated products laden with questionable chemical ingredients. But, the alternatives they found were often expensive, inaccessible, bland, or ineffective.

In response to this clear need in the marketplace, they created The Honest Company to ensure that parents have access to non-toxic, eco-friendly, beautiful family products that don’t break the bank. Honest diapers, cleaning, feeding and personal care products are designed with delight in mind, and never contain harmful or toxic ingredients.

As a social enterprise and mission-driven company, the” Social Goodness” (CSR) platform aims to build healthy, safe families by investing in the whole development of children ages 0-3 and supporting young people in pursuit of their dreams.

The Honest Company is on a mission to make the healthy and safe choices, the accessible choices for all families.

One of the core goals of The Honest Company is to create a happy, healthy future for today's children and families. We are very proud be an active member of the B Corp community of like-minded organizations who are dedicated to making a profound difference in community, safeguarding people & the planet, and making efforts to be better businesses.

The Change We Seek	

The Honest Company was born out of the desire to provide not only effective, but also unquestionably safe, eco-friendly, beautiful, convenient, and affordable products to homes everywhere. We believe that every baby deserves the best we can create for them.

We strive to embody all of the qualities in a brand we hold dear – savvy style, sustainability, and extraordinary service & convenience all wrapped in a passion for social goodness, tied with a bow of integrity and sprinkled with a little cheeky fun.

We hope to simplify the lives of parents and bring more delight to every day. Our dream is to re-define the "family brand" and create something that's better for all families, everywhere.

We’re committed to helping families, and to do that, we feel strongly that we need to think sustainably. Without our health, without our planet – we have nothing. It's serious business and we're in the business of making it better. Since our inception we've tried to re-think how to create a business that promotes health and sustainability.

We are committed to operating with integrity & transparency, and with humble honesty, as we strive to always create better, do better, and be better.

Downsize Managers was primarily born out of the need to help people downsize by repurposing and recycling their personal belongings through local online auctions and donating to local charities.  
The key to their approach lies in understanding how people and objects are connected, how one thing can be the bridge to another thing. This has enabled them to create an ecosystem for people and things in transition in a caring way.  Downsize Managers is now full circle in that they reduce waste by finding new homes for gently used items, at the same time building a local community by hiring locally underserved individuals who are in turn seeing the benefits of building a network with local charities and agencies in need and giving back.  Downsize Managers contributes to the good of the world and strives to do good business by creating meaningful work for people and things in transition in a way that is socially responsible and environmentally sustainable. It’s not just a job, it’s a calling.

Cometech is specialized in the development of Cardio Protection programs; they help every day to save lives with our Automated External Defibrillators that allow to rescue a victim of a sudden cardiac arrest while awaiting the arrival of emergency vehicles.
 
Cometech tries to reduce the victims of cardiac arrest forming the public about CPR and installing defibrillators.
 
Cometech has created an internal division called "SAVE your LIFE" with the aim of spreading the culture of preventing sudden cardiac arrest (CA). To do this, they created a network of points of AED emergency, in order to reduce the delay time of intervention and thus increase the survival rate of people suffering from sudden cardiac arrest.
 
 "SAVE your LIFE" explains, in a simple but effective way, what is stunting Rate, the technique of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and the use of the AED to create a social conscience that face overcoming fears, the insecurity and indifference on these matters.

As a team, Bond&Devick’s objective is to help clients reach their long-term goals and dreams. They aim to be your primary retirement planning resource by helping you arrange your financial affairs in the most efficient and effective way. They are unique in that they use Goals-Based Planning to measure progress toward achieving your goals. Since their firm’s establishment in 1982, they have been proud to help many clients plan for and reach their dreams.

Xinca generates work for people who are in a state of social vulnerability through shoemaking, while respecting their commitment to sustainability and the environment. The purpose of Xinca is to make footwear with all recycled materials. The sole in their shoes is made out of the rubber taken from used tires, which are a threat to the environment. For the upper part of trainers they re-use fabric taken from pants, work uniforms or textile discard in general.

In the productive process, Xinca offers job opportunities to people who, for different reasons, cannot have a formal job. Xinca provides these workers with the input materials so that they can bring them home, glue the pieces together and cut them out so that Xinca can finish the product in the factory.

We became a B Corp because we believe in impact. We pursue social and environmental changes using the same methods and techniques of a conventional company. 

The Change We Seek	

Xinca wants to be more than just shoes. They do business in a different manner, with social and environmental commitment. Without betraying their values and enjoy while they do what they like. Xinca dreams of a better world and will do their part.

Stumptown Coffee Roasters is a roaster, wholesaler and retailer of specialty coffee, founded and headquartered in Portland, Oregon.

Stumptown was started with the goal of doing things differently, with a vision that’s always been a little left-of-center, and with the focus squarely on quality. 

They source the best coffees in the world and strive to maintain transparent, quality-based relationships with their farmers along the way. From plant to portafilter, they pay homage to these folks through their own fervent attention to detail at every step, quality control in their cupping labs, meticulous roasting profiles and extensive barista education. 

They are committed to the well-being of everyone they work with, from the farmers and the communities they live in, to their employees and communities here in the States. They value their relationships with their customers, growers, and each other. With roastery facilities in four cities, several cafes, and fantastic wholesale partnerships around the country, there’s a lot to be proud of here.
column10: Responsibly sourced coffee and cold brew. Employee-driven culture.  Hospitality focused.

FLOOW2 is the first B2B online Sharing Marketplace. On FLOOW2.com, businesses from all around the world can share their assets amongst each other.

When a businesses has equipment, services, facilities or personnel available, they can rent out, sell or lend it to other organizations via our platform to generate additional turnover while acting more sustainably conscious and social.

If a businesses is in need of equipment, services, facilities or personnel, they can also use our website to rent, buy or borrow from fellow businesses and save costs while also acting in a more sustainable and social way.

We became a B Corp because we would like to show that change is here in the form of the new economy. This new economy will thrive because of radical innovations such as our platform, that creates mutliple new values for every business.
