Six Degree People are seen as ‘chief connectors’ that empower people and organisations across their global community to accelerate their own purposeful growth journeys. Over the past two decades they've worked at the nexus where global corporations, sustainable business and disruptive not for profits overlap. Every day they make ‘right person-right time' connections to clients to help them unblock major challenges and identify opportunities to innovate products, services and business models. The connections Six Degree People make: create or validate vision; shape strategy; take action; and measure impact.

Six Degree People’ services include:shaping advisory boards and innovation hubs,finding and attracting senior executives,matching senior executives with mentors,organising and planning discovery road trips for senior leadership,creating collaboration partnerships and new business opportunities.

The natural progression of our own purposeful growth journey helped us find B-Corporation as the most complementary global community to our own. They enable us to collaborate with organisations that we know share similar values, and we understand the power of building a movement together that will accelerate purposeful growth. We strongly believe in the power of collaboration and in the energy that comes from being part of an environment which will help us grow the business without compromising on our values.The Change We Seek	

The world is experiencing unparalleled global challenges because economic growth has come at great societal and environmental cost. Six Degree People are part of driving the systemic change required to move to a new economic paradigm of vibrant, resourceful and sustainable economies that function for the benefit of everyone.

Six Degree People believe in an abundance business culture that will make purposeful growth the ‘new norm’ and create outstanding opportunities to innovate products, services and business models that far out-perform existing ‘business as usual’ approaches. Six Degree People believe there is a clear business case as to why growth should be decoupled from natural resource constraints, and in doing so - how we then create a future where growth creates a net benefit to our natural resources and society.

Onda Orgánica offers clothes made with organic cotton and fair work conditions in the Cordoba province of Argentina. Through their garments, the brand seeks to create awareness about the environmental and social situation in Argentina and to offer an ethical consumerism option. The use of organic cotton in garments avoids not only environmental contamination, but also water pollution. Onda Orgánica also cares about the health of workers and families that live near the crops. 

By producing their clothes in in responsible workshops, Onda Orgánica contributes to social justice by avoiding child labor, slave labor, and human trafficking.

By becoming a B Corp, we hope to connect with other people sharing our same ideology, to share experiences and challenges that exist in the market, and to build future alliances. We are ready to be a real B Corp ambassador through future presentations and events. It will be a pleasure to share knowledge and help to boost action with other B Corps and build a sustainable synergy.The Change We Seek	

Onda Orgánica tries to help solve two main issues:

1. Environmental issues: In the Cordoba Province alone, 50 million liters of glyphosate are used annually. This toxic weedkiller not only pollutes the environment, but also causes diseases like cancer in workers and their families.
2. Social issues: Almost 80% of the textile industry uses clandestine workshops for their production. Also, in 2013 unemployment reached 7.2%, which means there are almost 3 million unemployed people in Argentina.

Onda Orgánica feels very proud of:Offering garments with ecological and social values.Being an activist company in society and trying to plant the sustainability seed in other people’s minds.

Tulip Winery is the largest boutique winery in Israel and combines the production of high quality wine with social responsibility. Located on the grounds of Kfar Tikva (Village of hope): A home and community for adults with developmental, cognitive and emotional disabilities; Tulip Winery provides inclusive employment opportunities to adults with disabilities while producing internationally acclaimed boutique wines.

We become a B Corp to follow our vision of social entrepreneurship and to inspire others to do the same – because "You can label wines but you can't label people."

The Change We Seek	

Tulip Winery is committed to creating a corporate environment that supports their community by producing the best possible product and at the same time providing employment for adults with disabilities.

Tulip winery is situated on a hilltop in Northern Israel’s Jezreel Valley on the grounds of a small village called Kfar Tikva: The Village of Hope. Kfar Tikva’s mission is to enable its 200+ residents with special needs to fulfill their potential and live a full and happy life. Tulip Winery helps Kfar Tikva achieve its mission by employing residents of the village in the production of Tulip wines, encouraging community involvement and promoting joint activities. Kfar Tikva residents who are employees of Tulip Winery take an active part in harvesting the grapes, bottling and packaging of the wine and welcoming and receiving guests at the Tulip Winery Visitor Center. The successful synthesis of Kfar Tikva’s mission with Tulip Winery's desire to produce quality wine has created an exciting model for the wine industry; employing adults with special needs and providing the opportunity for inclusion in the mainstream workforce.

Tulip Winery also partners with The Make- A Wish Foundation, in Israel, and has produced a private label wine series of Tulip wines just for them. Fifty percent of the profit from the gift packages containing the Make A Wish Foundation wines are donated to the Foundation.

Creativity and attention to every detail of the manufacturing process and constant emphasis on providing quality at a reasonable price, has made Tulip Winery an industry leader and the largest boutique winery in Israel. Tulip wines have spirit, soul, bouquet and flavor like no other wine: "Because you cannot compete with a dream."

B-Green is an environmental agency based in Argentina with local and global coverage, which works with companies, governments and the community, in the development and implementation of innovative actions that result in environmental and social benefits. 

We became B Corp because we believe in an economy where equality and inclusion can prevail, and where the ultimate goal is not the benefit of the few at the expense of poverty for many. We found in this system a great environment for companies with community purposes, where they can grow and spread this message to the world by demonstrating that it is possible.

The implementation is done across different areas of management involved in the processes: institutional relationships, human resources and marketing; designing together customized solutions tailored to each target.

We focus in helping forward-thinking organizations become sustainable leaders of the present, injecting sustainability into the company³s DNA through new implementations focused on people.

This can be achieved through different tools, including: environmental best practices programs, workshops and training sessions for executives, public massive campaigns, sustainable BTL communication, design of carbon neutral events, etc.


 The Change We Seek™

B-Green seeks to increase awareness about the rational use of natural resources and environmental care, to improve people’s quality of life. 

Through the development of new ideas that solve the needs of companies and governments as well as consumers, B-Green aims to shorten the gap between the private and the community interests.

Thus, all the gears of society may work towards personal benefits, while sharing a new goal: To improve quality of life for current and future generations.

Wild Nutrition is committed to creating Food-Grown supplements to empower human health. Right from the start they wanted to do it differently. To create products with purpose, backed by science, and using natural ingredients of exceptional quality. Their guiding principles are to support a holistic approach to health, to affect tangible change - and challenge the wellness industry. It was an uncompromising vision - and it remains so today.

Today Wild Nutrition is stocked in 52 countries around the world, with a team committed to driving wellness on a global scale. As the community grows, so does the vision. Now, more than ever, Wild Nutrition is committed to supporting the planet: from environmentally-conscious packaging, to business initiatives that instill respect for the natural world. After all, nature is in our DNA: it’s our inspiration, the seed that sparks change, and the foundation for our formulas that have helped people of all ages to live life in balance.

Approximately 1.5% of the Western world's population lives with a speech disability caused by a variety of medical conditions such as CP, ALS, Down's syndrome and Parkinson's, impairments that make it difficult for people to communicate clearly. At Voiceitt, we have made a promise to the community of those with speech impairments that we will provide them with our Talkitt solution. The speech disabled population has shown strong interest in our product, preferring to have a sleek and easily transportable solution such as the Talkitt application which can be downloaded to a tablet or smart phone or used on a wearable, as opposed to other bulky stigmatizing products, thereby allowing greater social integration and inclusion.

Establishing a technological Start-up is very challenging as it requires large amounts of funding before having a product ready for market. A social-tech Start-up is ever more challenging as most conventional investors avoid investing in a company that develops a solution for people with disabilities because they see this a niche market, not catering to the entire population at large. Becoming a B Corp will enable us the accessibility to reach out and share our goals with those investors who are looking for a double impact company to connect with.

The Change We Seek	

One day, Voiceitt will receive a letter or a video of a young child who the world had given up on and thought would never speak. And those who will watch the video showing how Voiceitt's hard work and commitment has finally changed the lives of those who struggle to communicate. And when reading or watching in amazement, hearing the gratitude and witnessing the testimony of their family and friends, thanking Voicett for helping their loved one speak, then and only then, Voiceitt will know that they have made a difference and reached their goals.

This is a exciting period where the development in technology has the potential to break down the gaps between people with disabilities and society, and help them communicate freely. Voiceitt solutions will play a major role in helping to dramatically improve the quality of life of people with speech, motor and cognitive disabilities. The company plans to become the leading standard solution, facilitating the integration in mobile devices, wearables, IOT, smart cars and homes.

Falcon & Singer P.C. provides relationship-based quality services for business owners and individuals. They work with owners of privately held businesses, including women and minority business owners and owners of socially responsible enterprises, in a wide range of industries, providing outsourced general counsel services, Business Life Cycle Planning	 (an integrated planning technique for business owners) and traditional transactional services, such as setting up entities, negotiating and drafting agreements, acquisitions and immigration. They work with individuals with special needs in the areas of planning and guardianship and with individuals generally in the area of trusts and estates (including estate planning, the preparation of Wills and trusts and the probate and administration of estates).

The firm’s approach to practice reflects its belief in the importance of recognizing and serving our multiple stakeholders. Falcon & Singer recognizes that clients want their lawyer to be a pro-active, creative resource. That involves a holistic approach to client service, helping to develop creative opportunities and options, functioning as part of a client’s team, and working collaboratively to ensure clients understand – in plain English rather than legalese – their options and to help guide them to decisions. For employees, serving their needs means creating opportunities and flexible work environments, particularly for working mothers. For the firm’s community, it means active community service, helping in particular to educate their special needs community, improve their business community and pursue numerous charitable projects. For the environment, it means, among other things, making substantial efforts in a paper-driven industry to reduce the use of paper and being a part of the Westchester Green Business Challenge.

The firm has offices in New York and New Jersey. It has a peer review rating of AV Preeminent	 Peer Review rating from Martindale Hubbell	, which is their highest rating for legal ability and ethical standards (www.martindale.com/ratings).

Our mission is to practice law at the highest quality and ethical levels in a manner which benefits our clients, empowers our employees, supports our communities and minimizes our environmental impact. We became a B Corp because those are the same values that power the B Corp community. B Corp certification provides us with a third party set of standards by which we can assess our progress in meeting those goals and which help guide us in our internal decision-making.The Change We Seek	

In the way that Falcon & Singer defines their mission and works to fulfill it, they endeavor to lead by example and to inspire others to set similar goals and act with integrity, honesty and respect for others. As examples:

• In their work with clients, they endeavor to create long term relationships that involve educating their clients and developing their role as part of the client's team out of respect for the fact that the decisions to be implemented are the client's, not the firm's.

• In their work with underserved communities (e.g., individuals with special needs and women and minority business owners), they strive to provide high quality holistic legal services to their clients and free education to individuals and organizations who are members of those communities.

• With their employees, they try to provide employment opportunities and training to individuals who might not otherwise have such opportunities. As examples,• They have for many years employed mothers with young children, utilizing flexible schedules and creatively defined work flow methods to fit with a mother’s other responsibilities.• They created an internship program within the firm for a high school student with special needs and, in partnership with the Northern New Jersey Rotary Clubs, created and implemented a program to engage other businesses to do the same.

• With the environment, in a paper driven industry, they endeavor to substantially reduce their consumption of paper. Much of their work is now performed electronically. In addition, they use the back sides of printed pages for notes and drafts, use two sided printing where possible and limit the number of printed documents.

R World Energy Solutions, originally established as Eco Energy, specialized in energy efficient lighting for small and mid-sized businesses. The successful venture in energy efficiency led to other energy conservation products and services; and that’s how in 2010 R World Energy Solutions (RWES) was born. RWES is a full service sales and engineering energy firm headquartered in King of Prussia, PA. They assist clients with understanding where and how much energy is consumed within their organization. From there, they help them in reducing energy consumption with state of the art conservation products by providing powerful financing alternatives. This in turn leads to significant cost reductions with measurable ROI.

RWES has Certified Energy Managers (CEM) and Certified Sustainable Development Professionals (CSDP) whose focus is to work with both sales consultants and clients. RWES’ engineers are tasked to evaluate the latest products and technologies for energy conservation in order to maintain RWES’ leadership status in the energy efficiency sector. This due diligence is the reason RWES stays on the leading edge within the energy conservation industry.

Along with RWES’ energy consulting practice, they have a top-notch professional sales organization fully knowledgeable within the energy conservation sector. Their sales professionals sell either vertically (focused on specific industries), or geographically. RWES has helped clients save hundreds of thousands of dollars a year, while making the world a greener place.

We became a B Corporation because we believe in creating a more sustainable environment and giving back in the process. Our mission is to create a greener world one business at a time; and this certification will ensure that we stay focused on our mission while keeping all people, the planet, and profit in mind.

The Change We Seek	

RWES advises clients acting on their financial and environmental sustainability concerns; thus, enabling these leaders in the communities they serve to preserve our nation’s natural resources. They do this by not only working with businesses, but also volunteering and educating local organizations and entities in various sustainable and energy efficient practices. RWES works with a local university educating students and organizations on the power of energy efficiency. They are currently involved in a yearlong volunteer project assisting a student organization with a lighting audit and proposal in regards to efficiency upgrades.

RWES addresses their clients’ needs by delivering the latest energy conservation technologies, ensuring that the best possible solution for the client and the environment are being utilized. They make these projects a financial reality for their clients by providing unique and powerful financing options, in hopes that energy conservation becomes second nature and future generations will still enjoy the beauties of our planet. RWES’ values are at the center of every decision and interaction. These values are focus, teamwork, professionalism, trust and respect; and they apply to our employees, partners, suppliers, and our clients.

H.U.M.A.N. (Helping Unite Mankind And Nutrition) Healthy Vending is a socially responsible franchisor of healthy vending machine businesses focused on increasing access to healthier foods and drinks by way of eco-friendly and high-tech vending machines that vend better-for-you foods and drinks, including fresh fruit and locally-sourced products. HUMAN's overarching vision is to “make healthy food more convenient than junk food.”

We are incredibly proud to become a Certified B Corporation since this ensures that our commitment to solving social and environmental problems is at the core of everything we do and literally specified in our by-laws. Rarely do the vending industry and sustainability go hand-in-hand, but we’re proud to push the envelope. We think B Corporations are the wave of the future: businesses measuring their success by the amount of good they do in the world and we couldn’t be happier about this.



Founded in 2008 by Sean Kelly and Andy Mackensen, HUMAN Healthy Vending has not only revolutionized the vending industry, it has also created a viable business model for over 150 franchisees across the nation, Puerto Rico and Canada. HUMAN Healthy Vending has machines placed in over 1,200 schools, hospitals, and other locations across North America.

HUMAN donates 10% of its profits to promote improved nutrition and entrepreneurial education in underserved schools via its charity HUMAN Everywhere.The Change We Seek	

At HUMAN Healthy Vending, our mission is to make healthy food more convenient than junk-food through the placement of 100% healthy and interactive vending machines in schools, hospitals, gyms and corporate locations across the globe. We consider ourselves disruptors of the $42B vending industry that, for decades, has been peddling junk food to children and adults alike. 



We have innovated a new model for “instant” nutrition that does not just profit consumers’ health, but also profits the location financially. For example, Tomball High School in Tomball, TX, removed its junk food vending machines, replaced them with HUMAN Healthy Vending machines and doubled vending commissions while also slashing energy costs by more than eighty percent. This resulted in over $10,000 in increased earnings and savings for the school. With 90% of U.S. schools having vending machines on campus, and children consuming 19-50% of their daily food intake at school, we feel it is our duty to ensure that there are healthful food and beverage options for children on campus.

Our responsibility to our franchisees, our employees, our community, and to the environment is paramount to our success. That’s why we’re building a network of like-minded social entrepreneurs around the world who take our mission (“to make healthy food more convenient than junk food”) to heart and are actively bringing positive change to their communities. 

 

Written on every healthy vending machine wrap, you’ll see that we put our money where our figurative mouth is: we donate 10% of our proceeds to promote improved nutrition and entrepreneurial education in underserved schools via our charity, HUMAN Everywhere.

Caos! comunicação & design is a creative studio that develops solutions in the areas of multiplatform communication and information design, in the search for results that can facilitate and broaden the range of transforming ideas and actions. With 10 years of experience in the market and relying on a multidisciplinary team, caos! has created complex projects for major brands, from strategy to implementation, always using design as a tool that allow the comprehension of the whole, not losing attention to details.

Believing in construction of networks, in exchange and in experience as promoters of knowledge, in the open source as an important mindset for transformation, caos! has been implementing actions and promoting ideas through their own projects. BRIO 2013, a national award for digital projects. Convescote, an open event of talks that happens every month with more than 70 editions held. Engenhoca, a lab for experimentation where the following projects where developed: galeria caos!, cromatográfico, B facts, egotweet and video:sprints.

In order to guide and evaluate it’s projects, caos! defined the following positive impact drivers: sustainability, transformation and legacy. These drivers translate objectively the focus and purpose of the studio and help to guide and review processes and objectives. Each driver is assessed according to the following criteria: reach, impact and duration. This creates metrics that can be compared over time and generates information that can be shared clearly.

Through the B Corp community, we found a network of people and companies that share ideas, ideals and values which have driven us for many years. It also brings new perspectives and practices to our own way of acting.

The Change We Seek	

In a world where mass culture and global marketing create desires and subjectivities, where information is treated as a commodity and people as variables in algorithms, caos! believe in design as a promoter of a human-centered vision. Collaboration can contribute to building more truthful, responsible and transparent practices. In the quest to be one of the agents of this new movement, the studio seeks, through the establishment of interdependent local networks, to participate in and promote actions aligned with the ideas of new education, maker culture, open source, new production and distribution arrangements and organisms. Skin Care for Athletes is the only organic & natural skin care line designed specifically for athletes and the athletically inclined. Athletes sweat more, spend more time in the sun, and shower more often than a typical person; they need products that restore essential nutrients and help prevent dry, cracked skin, acne breakouts, and even infections. Their products naturally cleanse and moisturize your skin without the use of drying or harmful chemicals, and the instances of catching and spreading Staph infections or Athletes Foot are diminished by their organic germ fighting ingredients.

Offering total body care, the Tri-Body Collection contains the: 3-in-1 Tri-Body Wash, Tri-Body Moisturizing Spray and the Tri-Facial Serum. The Tri-Body Collection has anti-fungal/anti-bacterial properties; all are sulfate, petrochemical, paraben and phthalate-free and never tested on animals. They also offer the Tri-Body Collection Travel Set and the Tri-Facial Collection Travel Set. The line was developed by a late-blooming endurance athlete and certified holistic aromatherapist that has competed in 5ks, full and half-marathons, a sprint triathlon and a half-Ironman triathlon.

The newest P.A.R. line will help an athlete to Prepare, Achieve and Recover from their trainings and events. The P.A.R. line works synergistically and holistically during each phase of their training, event and recovery utilizing the best natural and organic ingredients. The P.A.R. line focuses on an athletes three main areas of performance-physical, mental and energy, providing products for each focus.

We became a B Corp to join with like-minded companies that believe in social and environmental responsibility and to demonstrate our commitment to our community, employees, consumers, environment and suppliers.

The Change We Seek	

They seek to educate and hydrate the skin of athletes, health and fitness enthusiasts and anyone who's "Got Skin" on the benefits of organic and natural skin care by providing a total body care line of organic products.

• They do not test any of their products on animals. They have committments from their suppliers that none of them test the raw ingredients that they purchase from them on animals. Their products do not contain any animal products or any animal by-products.

• They use PET bottles for their products, all of which are easily recycled. Shipping materials are made from 100% recycled materials. They do not add any chemicals, sudsing agents, colorants or man-made fragrances to any of their products. Not only is this healthier for your skin and body but none of the "run-off" from the use of their products will enter the environment via the sinks, showers, etc. Because their products are all natural, use of their products outside will not harm the environment. None of their suppliers utilize chemicals in the raw ingredients that they purchase from them.

No One Without was founded in 2010 when Gaston Javurek took a group of high school students to Skid Row. Expecting life change for the boys, he was blown away by the life changing experience he would have. He wanted to start a company that would give back in a positive way. He began making t-shirts and searching for a solid giving plan. In 2011, he met Kelli Dunavant who would help him formulate the business plan of No One Without and become his Founding Chief Operating Officer. In April of 2012, No One Without simplified their business model from 5 non-profit organizations to one mission for clean water.

No One Without is a For Purpose fashion brand. Through fashion, No One Without partners with Thirst Relief International to bring clean water to people around the globe. Your purchase provides one person with clean water for 25 years. One At A Time.

The bio-sand filter mimics the earth’s natural filtration process by utilizing layers of soil. The simple technology provides a long term, sustainable and maintenance free economical solution to drinking water in developing countries. Each bio-sand filter provides 20 people with clean drinking water for 25 years.

No One Without sought out the B Corp certification in order to provide irrefutable proof that the change we are seeking to make is trustworthy. B Corporation is the highest standard for socially responsible business. No One Without desires to provide our customers with not only satisfaction but also peace of mind.

The Change We Seek™

Bio-Sand filters make a way for so many communities to have clean water. Community members are in turn trained to troubleshoot any problems and maintenance education.  Not only do they have access to clean water, they are sustaining/maintaining the filters on their own. Equipping people to help themselves is of utmost importance to No One Without. No One Without lives to serve others but we also want to educate people. Education is the springboard for movement. 

They always want to give to where the most need is. They never allocate where they feel like the money should go, or what they think they might want to do. No One Without asks Thirst Relief International where there is most need at that moment. They have provided filters in Rwanda, Uganda, Cameroon, Tanzania, Kenya and Brazil. They give according to the knowledge and expertise of Thirst Relief International. The beauty of working with partners that are on the ground is that they know far better than they do what is best for the communities they work with. They have full community reports, photos of people and scenery and names of community members that comment on what clean water means to them. They pass all this information on to No One Without as well. We are able to keep customers in the circle as to where their contributions went and what it means to the families.  

No One Without seeks to:

-Provide Clean Water Across The Globe

-Educate People 

-Give Where The Most Need Is

Green April is a strategy consulting firm with a focus on sustainability. Their clients see sustainability as core to their business and have it embedded their strategy; responsible towards stakeholders, society and the environment. With in-depth knowledge on the technical, strategical and financial aspects of sustainability, Green April helps to develop creative business models, substantiate this with sound business cases and support their clients to make this work.

Green April works in four sectors: renewable energy, food & feed, built environment and mobility and companies Green April worked for are leading in their industry; energy producers, feed & food producers, traders, network providers and many others.

Green April develops sustainability strategies, brings KPIs actions and monitoring in place, manages sustainability programs, develops business cases and projects, structures finance and executes projects.

Green April is based in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

We believe community action can create change and we have to practice what we preach.

The Change We Seek	

The transition towards a sustainably society is not only inevitable, it’s the biggest business opportunity in a generation. The business case is often hard to make however and markets are often immature. But the belief of consumers, employees and employers in the value of sustainability in the corporate environment is growing; people want to buy from, work for and identify oneself with companies with pronounced ethical values. This will drive the business environment to strengthen people and planet ambitions next to being profitable. Green April wants to be at the forefront on this change and assist companies to create value from it.

It’s the mission of Green April to build a business environment of companies that are responsible towards its customers, employees, the environment and society; to build ‘better business’. Green April assists clients to identify, substantiate and execute sustainable business opportunities with a down-to-earth approach, a focus on the bottom-line and with in-depth expertise on the subject.

MAONO was founded with the simple mission to produce high-quality goods at affordable prices. Why continue to pay extraordinary prices for clothing and accessories, only making the rich richer? The industry is controlled by a few luxury brands that keep their prices high, raking in huge profits. By working with our in-house designers and partnering with some of the same factories of your favorite designer brands, MAONO is able to produce superior-quality goods at revolutionary pricing. 

We at MAONO adhere to a strict code of lifestyle ethics, and sometimes that means coming up with a new way of thinking. Our fabrics are sourced from every corner of the world, bringing you some of the finest materials available. Selling our products exclusively through our website and select pop-up locations enables us to keep costs down and transfer those savings to you -- and a lower cost means there’s more room to give back.

Fashion with a cause 

Idealistic and full of heart, we believe that we should do good for others while taking care of ourselves. Forging ahead with the belief that everyone has a right to luxury, we’re outfitting the movers, shakers, and influencers of the world at a fraction of the cost. By kicking the middleman out of the process and selling directly to you, we can donate 5% of our profits to organizations that make our communities better. We truly believe that fashion can change the world.

Why Washington, D.C.? 

MAONO was launched in Washington D.C. due to the area’s unique cultural blend of fashion and power. The District is a playground for some of the world’s most influential minds, working together to create lasting change. What then could be more appropriate than outfitting the power-players to make a good impression, all while allowing them the opportunity to bring up a new generation of game changers? By shopping with MAONO, you’re making a direct financial contribution to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Washington and providing our youth with the support and guidance they need to succeed.

Being a B Corporation allows MAONO to join a group that represents our values and helps support our commitments to our customers, our employees, the environment and the community. We hope that we can provide an example of how all businesses should act and the B Corp model will ensure that we are living up to our own mission to change the world.



The Change we Seek

BE THE MOVEMENT

Idealistic and full of heart, we believe that we should
do good for others while taking care of ourselves.

ENVIRONMENT

Here at MAONO, we strive for an ethical approach to business. With the knowledge

that we can’t care for each other without caring for the environment, we only use
chemical-free materials and source leathers from cruelty-free suppliers.

FOR OUR CUSTOMERS There’s nothing we hate more than being ignored. Here at MAONO, we understand there would be no us without a you! That’s why providing exceptional service is our top priority. While you’re busy changing the world, we’ll be here to keep you looking sharp and feeling valuable.

COMMUNITY

MAONO is dedicated to giving back to the community. From volunteering at a local food kitchen (Capital Area Food Bank), to partnering with the Boys and Girls Clubs of Greater Washington, we believe that we are a reflection of our surroundings. We at MAONO would like to challenge you to be the movement and join us in
fostering positive change in the world.

OUR TEAM 

We can’t do good for others if our team members aren’t happy. That’s why we strive to create an environment that fosters creativity and promotes inclusion. Comprised of a global generation of optimists and idealists, the MAONO enterprise understands that cultivating personal and professional growth is a privilege.

Three SistaÕs was established in 2011 by Janet Guthrie and Stuart Wright and commenced operations in May 2012. Stuart & Janet have extensive backgrounds within housing and homelessness and Indigenous Health and identified the need to put back into the community due to what appeared to be decades of failure in the homelessness space in Cairns.
 
 Three SistaÕs purchased the management rights to a rundown budget resort,with the aim of converting the 68 unit facility into a holistic and culturally appropriate short- medium accommodation facility for families and individuals within the homelessness stream. Three SistaÕs has two arms Ð asocial enterprise and a registered non-profit foundation.
 
 The mission statement of Three SistaÕs is to contribute to the long term well-being of socially disadvantaged and Indigenous people living in the homelessness stream in the Cairns and Cape York regions by improving health and living standards, accommodation and employment opportunities. This holistic model aims to broker access to health and social services in order to provide a dedicated model of support that empowers individuals and families to re- enter the broader community in a meaningful way under a private model of investment partnering with government in models of social equity.

Everyone has a right to high-quality information. And each individual should be able to express his or her opinion. Anytime. Anywhere. But how do you reach people living in remote parts of the world? TTC reaches them with mobile solutions that share and collect information. To improve social projects, services and products worldwide. And make a difference in people’s lives.

Mobile phones play an important role in day-to-day communication. For example, over 80% of people in Africa now have access to a mobile phone. TTC runs social marketing campaigns, collects data, and measures impact in emerging markets. At this moment they work in more than 16 countries across five continents. Mobile technology is a very important medium for making a connection. That’s why TTC uses mobile technology to connect organizations with their hard-to-reach target group.

We believe that business has a higher social purpose beyond simply profit. The B Corp assessment gives us a framework to measure our success against rigorous values and responsible practices as we scale as a company. 

The Change We Seek	

In 2008, TTC was at the forefront of the revolutionary growth of mobile communications in emerging markets, and they still are today. TTC are pioneers in using mobile phone technology to achieve social change. They – as partners of development bodies, NGOs, private companies, governments and other global organizations – are proud to help people to empower themselves; to free themselves from continuous dependence on foreign aid. Using mobile devices, TTC collects and provides real-time and accurate information, in a way that is relevant and meaningful, to people in developing countries all over the world.

TTC facilitates dialogue between (development) organizations and their audiences. In every project, partners and clients value how they always seek to add value by creatively developing ways to support organizations in achieving their goals.

GreenFox offers cost-saving and sustainable (lighting) solutions. GreenFox creates work for people with a distance to the labourmarket. Their specialists are active in sustainable lighting and also in (repeatable) technical installation work, large inventories and social return. GreenFox works with several social work shelters and WerkgeversServicepunten throughout The Netherlands.
 
 GreenFox creates new business models. For example, with Eneco, GreenFox creates jobs that are paid by the energy reduction of lighting. GreenFox renovates existing luminaries for clients of Eneco. Eneco invests in the renovation and gets a part of the energy reduction for a couple of years. A win-win-win. The customers of Eneco get, without investing, energy efficient lighting and reduce their energy consumption. Eneco gives their customers the opportunity to reduce energy and GreenFox creates jobs for people with a distance to the labourmarket by educating people to renovate existing luminaries.
 
 GreenFox helps companies with social return obligations. In The Netherlands a company that wins a public tender is obligated to create one or several jobs for people with a distance to the labourmarket for 5% of total som of to the tender. GreenFox helps companies to select the work for their specialist.

Greenlink has an extensive experience of projects in Africa ranging from countries in West to the East of the continent. Greenlink's expanding base of office locations ensures direct local support for all their customers.

Kitts’ mission is to be your favorite every day underwear! Even better, for each pair sold Kitts donates a pair to those in need, filling a major gap in clothing donations.

Charities who rely on donated clothes can’t accept used underwear, and very few people think to buy and donate new pairs. Most tend to think of the bigger items that people need - food, shelter and the larger items of clothing - but underwear is really important too.

Dignity comes from a lot of places and having basic hygiene and cleanliness is one source that’s often taken for granted. Imagine you had to wear the same underwear for a week or go without: how would that affect your life and how you feel about yourself? Underwear is a tiny thing with a big impact.

This is why Kitts pledges to donate a pair of new underwear to charity for every pair sold, offering a simple yet essential way for everyone to feel comfortable and secure. Such a small gesture of love and care can help brighten someone’s day and restore a little dignity, the foundation of building a better life.

FEEL GOOD IN THEM. FEEL GOOD ABOUT THEM.

Becoming a B Corp is one way to express our commitment to pioneering a better way to do business. We strongly believe that business can create value for all of society and the planet, not just shareholders. Inspired and motivated by fellow B Corps we aim to join the movement redefining success in business.

The Change We Seek	

The mission of Kitts is twofold. First, Kitts aims to make it a little easier for those in need to access the basic necessities. As mentioned above, since it can’t be donated used, underwear is often forgotten. But, it’s an essential item of clothing. Having good and clean underwear is just part of basic dignity and no one should have to go without. This is why Kitts is committed to donating a new pair of underwear to charity for every pair sold.

Second, Kitts aims to make awesome underwear that customers love and want to wear every day. To do this, the social and environmental all aspects of production are carefully considered. For fabric, Kitts uses only sustainable raw fibres that require no pesticides or artificial irrigation - protecting and saving our precious water resources! These fabrics also happen to be the softest, most luxurious feeling fabrics around. They are also certified with OEKO-TEX Standard 100 testing for harmful substances. Kitts are also produced according to the principles of BSCI, the Business Social Compliance Initiative and Kitts works only with those that comply with the BSCI Code of Conduct or other internationally recognized labour standards.

Kitts aims to make underwear of the highest quality, according to the highest standards of environmental and social responsibility possible.  Along with donating a pair to charity for every pair sold, Kitts hopes to show that the apparel business can done in an ethical and responsible way and to inspire others to find creative ways to solve problems they see in their own community. Because sometimes the smallest things can have a big impact.
Thread Publishing does not exist to tell stories for the sake of telling nice stories; they tell stories to support organisations with purpose that are making a genuine difference in some way.

Organizations, people and athletes cramp when the primary focus is shifted purely to results. Many executives, entrepreneurs and managers have to deal with this phenomenon daily: the bottom-line results determine the rhythm of the day.
 
 The fact that large studies consistently show that 70 to 80% of employees is disengaged from their work – on top of the massive depletion of natural resources and destroying of ecosystems by organizations – fuels the question if we have reached the limits of our current organizational models.
 
 Actimpact guides leadership teams on their journey towards an organization that would be approved by the future. It’s time to act.

Tendril delivers personalized energy experiences for consumers around the world. Pioneering energy providers that want to establish a competitive advantage rely on Tendril's software and solutions to better acquire, engage and activate their customers. To do this Tendril employs the latest in energy science and data analytics to unveil a complete understanding of the individual consumer, including their unique needs and propensities to act. With this granular understanding they help their customers unlock the true value of energy interactions.



We have always sought to integrate and align a greater social good into our business and B Corp represented a way for us to institutionalize that commitment fully. Being a B Corp has also given us a framework from which to measure our performance with the objective to become an even better organization for our employees, stakeholders, community and environment.

The Change We Seek	



Tendril seeks to make consumers more aware of their energy use so they can take better control of their energy footprint. By enabling the transparency and relevancy of energy data, Tendril helps create a world in which energy is personal, sustainable and optimal both today and into the future.

In 2004 serial entrepreneur Ben Sayers started to notice a growing demand for VoIP products and realized that there was one distinct problem; there was nowhere to buy them from.

In August of that year, VoIPSupply.com was launched to serve the niche VoIP market and ironically the website featured more networking equipment than VoIP equipment. That unbalanced product catalog may not have been 100% true to their namesake but it did foreshadow the company’s eventual tagline, “Everything you need for VoIP,” and their belief in providing the best and most complete customer experience.

VoIP Supply is more than just a website and more than just VoIP. VoIP Supply is a diverse team of talented people passionate about IP technologies that are dedicated to educating customers first instead of just simply selling them stuff. VoIP Supply can design communication solutions for customers through VoIP, Video Conferencing, Unified Communications, IP Surveillance, installation services, and equipment buyback and recycling.

Becoming a B Corp gives VoIP Supply a clear roadmap to continue doing well so that we can do good. It’s a great feeling to know that in addition to being successful at work by solving problems for customers, completing tasks, and earning a paycheck that we’re also helping the community with every successful order we process.


 The Change We Seek™

VoIP Supply wants to be the opposite of most other online technology resellers who focus solely on offering the lowest price and selling what’s most profitable for them, and not what’s best for the customer.  The difference VoIP Supply is trying to make is doing a tremendous amount of education and offering real value and support to customers.  VoIP Supply loves helping customers and its employees love coming to work in a creative, fun, and dynamic culture which ensures that their customers will enjoy their experience as well.

VoIP Supply’s purpose is to provide a place of uncovering, teaching and developing leaders. A place where entrepreneurial leaders gain access; the ability to learn, grow and leverage a core business infrastructure that will allow them to execute on their ideas while driving the company towards the achievement of its greater goal.

Our business, people, products and services all revolve around maintaining and living up to our core values:Get Goosed (teamwork)Go Beyond the Bottom Line (the greater good)Mom's Calling (customer first)Be a Very Hungry Caterpillar (embrace change)No Donkeys! (positive family spirit)

VoIP Supply’s open door policy allows employees to freely share concerns and ideas.  A weekly intra-office newsletter and weekly huddles on “The Lawn” provide casual forums to keep everyone engaged and up to date on where the company is heading.

It is our belief that it is not what we do, but what differences we make that defines who we are. We have made community involvement a part of what we do, so that we can make a profound impact locally through the donation of our time, talents and money to charitable organizations in the Western New York area.

When is the last time you heard a CEO ask an interview question like this; “Who is Kip?” From the smiling faces, to the frequent company events, to the fact that you can make a mistake and celebrate the fact that you tried to do the right thing, VoIP Supply is a melting pot, a diverse set of people and principles that puts the focus on serving our customers (both internal and external). Everyone contributes above and beyond to accomplish our purpose.

The most exciting thing to happen in running since Forrest Gump broke his braces...The Impact Marathon Series is now live in 5 countries: Nepal, Malawi, Guatemala, Colombia & Kenya.
 
Participants travel from all over the globe, representing nations, charities & corporates to spend a week in Impact Marathon's Athletes' Village (think stunning campsites overlooking the Himalayas). From there, each day, they head out to visit and work at the exact projects they have fundraised for - Impact Marathon Series' mission is to create a real emotional link between fundraising and the impact. During this time participants will see, feel and understand the difference they can make in the lives of others. Each night, they share a beer and relax in the Sunset Bar and share the stories, ideas and lessons from the day.
 
On the final day, they run! A tough, super challenging trail race where the goal is not to race a personal best, but to run as a community; with others, for others. It's about the uniting power of running as the people you have worked alongside all week, many will be racing for the first time, feeling the empowerment that comes from running.

Luftman, Heck & Associates (founded 2003) is a community law firm which helps individuals and families find solutions to complex and personal circumstances. They focus their practice on helping people with both criminal and traffic defense matters and consumer finance law. When times are most tough, Luftman, Heck & Associates provides guidance and peace of mind.

The majority of legal services the firm provides are developed specifically to benefit individuals and families who are economically less fortunate, in need and are either underserved or not served at all by legal professionals. More than two thirds of Luftman, Heck & Associates' clientele is made up of individuals from low-income or insolvent households. The law firm takes pride in the ability to help people in struggling communities get back on their feet after financial hardships have knocked them down.

Unscrupulous business practices during the first decade of this century have been very difficult on the average family. The variations of mortgage deception and fraud, debt collection practices and countless breeds of companies exploiting individuals harmed by these practices prompted Luftman, Heck & Associates to take a full-on aggressive approach to protect these threatened communities.  Luftman, Heck & Associates has been one of very few firms to stand up for those who have lost money to illegally operating and unlicensed financial corporations working in the states of Ohio and California.

We became a B Corp for the opportunity to continue learning new ways in which we can expand our social and environmental impact through networking with other like-minded (and better) companies.The Change We Seek	

Luftman, Heck & Associates believes that the community deserves quality representation and support, regardless of an economically challenging environment. They seek to help individuals in low-income households rise above the hard times in their lives and create a powerful new beginning. The firm passionately strives to positively impact their neighbors and the communities served through effecting social changes for the betterment of all, while being attentive stewards of the environment in which they live and work.

GreenCitizen is on a mission to provide convenient, affordable and responsible ways for individuals and organizations to recycle obsolete, surplus, broken or unwanted electronics. Globally, electronics comprise the fastest growing waste stream, with 50 million tons of electronics discarded annually of which less that 20% is recycled. In the US, of the electronics supposedly recycled, 80% are shipped abroad and dumped on countries lacking appropriate environmental regulations to deal with it safely. GreenCitizen was founded in 2005 to confront the electronic waste stream holistically; finding systemic solutions to both household and business e-waste. GreenCitizen’s growing network of eco-centers, embedded in commercial centers, make it easy for individuals and businesses to drop off unwanted electronics and learn about the electronic waste crisis. GreenCitizen also picks up unwanted electronics from buildings and businesses in order to ensure that they are reused or recycled securely and responsibly without being shipped abroad. In its eight years of existence, GreenCitizen has served over 15,000 businesses, 150,000 individuals and responsibly reused or recycled over 12 million pounds of e-waste.

Ecologic Designs works with organizations to manufacture OEM, Private Label and Co-Branded consumer products made from their waste materials or materials they’ve previously reclaimed. This process of “upcycling” reduces landfill waste and creates valuable eco-friendly products worthy of conversation about resourcefulness. Working with the customer closely, Ecologic Designs is able to help companies have a triple bottom line approach to their marketing and promotional product purchases.

Over the years Ecologic Designs has worked with companies like Nike, AT&T, Whole Foods, REI, Container Store, Associated Press, Patagonia, New Belgium Brewery, White Wave Foods and many more taking their old banners, billboards or other durable waste streams then transforming them into unique backpacks, messenger bags, tote bags, wallets, portfolios, note book covers, etc. Other materials upcycled into custom branded products include bike tubes, wetsuits, garments, post-industrial packaging and more. This process extends the marketing message of their banners or other materials by giving them a second life as functional product placed directly in the hands of their customers. These customers then love to show off and talk about their unique product made from salvaged materials.

JustNeem provides high-quality body care products. The Neem tree, native to India, has been used in skin care for centuries and is known for its anti-bacterial, anti-fungal, and anti-viral properties. All of JustNeem's soaps, bath salts, and shaving soaps are made with the finest cosmetic grade raw materials and contain Neem and other natural ingredients that help sustain and help heal the skin. All products are handmade in small batches and wrapped and labeled individually.

JustNeem is committed to sharing the benefits of Neem with West Africa. They purchase all of their Neem raw material from Mauritania, West Africa, using existing Neem trees and paying a fair market price for labor and goods. This helps create jobs and generates income for families living with few resources. Their goal is to keep your skin healthy while at the same time improve the lives of people in West Africa.

The values advanced by B Lab and B Corporations are ones that are important to us and also to our stakeholders. By becoming a B Corporation, we are better able to broadcast our commitment to those values and hopefully set an example of social and environmental responsibility in our community.

The Change We Seek	

We believe that all human beings have the right to support themselves and their families through work.

We are partnering with like-minded NGOs (non-governmental organizations) that work with villagers in Mauritania, West Africa, to discover local resources and to establish economic opportunities for the local people. One of these resources, the Neem tree, can be used to generate income for families simply by planting the tree and selling its leaves and fruit. It has the additional benefit of giving shade in a hot desert climate and offering its medicinal benefits to the tree owner’s family. In collaboration with local NGOs, we help create jobs centered around this tree. With proceeds from our soap sales, we fund the planting of Neem trees in neighborhoods surrounding Nouakchott.

Blue Hill Partners is an energy services company that provides specialty energy efficiency retrofits as a fully funded, turnkey service. The Company partners with best-in-class technology, engineering and construction partners. They fund and manage the entire process: assessment, design, engineering, installation, and commissioning. Blue Hill also monitors and maintains the equipment and covers the labor and equipment costs of any product failure over the term of the service agreement. The Company provides user-friendly reports and analysis to support the client’s operations and sustainability reporting objectives. Clients have no out of pocket costs for the retrofits, and pay a service fee to Blue Hill over the service term for the efficiency, maintenance, and monitoring services. These payments are based on the actual energy savings of the upgrades – so Blue Hill is only successful when the projected savings are achieved. The cost of the new energy bill plus Blue Hill’s services fee is typically less than the client’s pre-retrofit energy bill. Blue Hill’s goal is to make it easy and efficient to be energy efficient. Blue Hill currently offers two specialty solutions: outdoor lighting retrofits and science building ventilation upgrades.

The Company partners with best-in-class technology, engineering and construction partners. They fund and manage the entire process: assessment, design, engineering, installation, and commissioning. Blue Hill also monitors and maintains the equipment and covers the labor and equipment costs of any product failure over the term of the service agreement. The Company provides user-friendly reports and analysis to support the client’s operations and sustainability reporting objectives. Clients have no out of pocket costs for the retrofits, and pay a service fee to Blue Hill over the service term for the efficiency, maintenance, and monitoring services. These payments are based on the actual energy savings of the upgrades – so Blue Hill is only successful when the projected savings are achieved. The cost of the new energy bill plus Blue Hill’s services fee is typically less than the client’s pre-retrofit energy bill. Blue Hill’s goal is to make it easy and efficient to be energy efficient. Blue Hill currently offers two specialty solutions: outdoor lighting retrofits and science building ventilation upgrades.

MyDomino's mission is to create 1 billion actions toward a clean energy future.

Everyone wants clean energy, air, and water. The technology for that is available today. But where do you start? Can you afford it? Do you have to make lifestyle sacrifices? This confusion keeps people from taking action.

That’s why MyDomino was founded. They cut through the confusion and make it easy for anyone to live more sustainably -- while lowering their bills. They provide useful information and guidance on the latest in clean energy living, product reviews and comparisons, and tips on saving energy and money.

Through consultation and personalized recommendations, they also help people take actions from picking the right LED light bulbs for their home to getting solar quotes to finding an electric car, and more.

An innovative company perk, MyDomino helps employees in a meaningful way -- allowing them to not only save time and money but also participate in a bigger cause. Their employee benefit helps a company enhance its CSR goals by showing a commitment to its employees and to a cleaner environment. They help companies go beyond greening their workplace and truly make a significant impact.

We became a B Corp because we want our mission of creating 1 billion clean-energy actions to drive all that we do. It's important to us to provide a meaningful benefit to people and the planet. As a B Corp, we’re proud to work for the public good of preserving a healthy planet for our children and for future generations.

The Change We Seek	

MyDomino believes that changing the world's energy sources from dirty fossil fuels to clean renewable energy will have a substantial, positive impact on the climate for people now and in the future.

How do we make this happen? Through the power of individuals and communities across the globe to come together and make a huge impact -- starting with small actions.

You might think you’re not doing much if you replace a light bulb. But if 60 people switch to LEDs, that’s like taking 25 cars off the road for a year. If just 25 people go solar, that’s like planting 97,000 trees -- or 400 football fields’ worth.

All the clean energy actions you take, no matter how small, add up. Together, we can create an epic MyDomino Effect.

Union Kitchen exists to grow and promote small businesses. For communities to be diverse, exciting, prosperous places, local businesses need to thrive and local entrepreneurs need to fulfill their passions. And that is where Union Kitchen comes in. Union Kitchen is building a platform and a megaphone for small businesses by providing a low-cost, low-risk, full-service kitchen for local businesses to grow and establish their operations. Union Kitchen eliminates the need for small businesses to take on debt, purchase expensive equipment, sign a long-term lease, or take many of the other risks that business owners have come to expect as the norm for starting a business.

Union Kitchen isn’t just about the dollar bottom line. The true bottom line is the world we wake up to each morning. Development can be an opportunity for locals to put a stamp on the city or an opportunity for large-scale developers and others to take advantage of the soaring real estate market to make themselves a buck (or, more likely, a few million). Union Kitchen is one piece of the effort to sculpt the future of community. A future that is grown organically, from within, to promote businesses, to create unique cultural identity, and to establish communities that we want to wake up to each morning.

We became a B Corp because we believe in the power of small business to drive sustainable community development and wanted to make a commitment to maximizing our social and environmental impact. We are excited to have a baseline assessment of our performance and pursue changes to strengthen our social and environmental impacts.

 

The Change We Seek	

 

Union Kitchen is sculpting the future of our community by making sure that local residents can find gainful employment with local businesses, that grocery shelves are stocked with locally made products, and by creating opportunities for small businesses to succeed without having to take on insurmountable debt and risk.

Kabrita is America’s first line of gentle goat milk foods for toddlers. Launched in 2014, Kabrita is uniquely privileged to offer a naturally easy to digest solution for children with cow milk sensitivity with its Goat Milk Formula and Goat Milk Yogurt and Fruit. Kabrita provides the highest standard of goat milk nourishment for children, and inspires parents and health care professionals with expert nutrition education.

All Kabrita ingredients are non-GMO and carefully chosen for their role in supporting healthy childhood development, as well as their sustainability and environmental footprint.



Kabrita is committed to a safer, healthier world for children, and to helping parents make choices for their families through education and dialogue. As part of this mandate, Kabrita is dedicated to 100% transparency and invites parents to explore what goes into making Kabrita gentle goat milk foods from farm to table.



We’re starting as we mean to go on – entrenching and articulating our commitment to children’s health and the planet from day one by becoming B Corp certified. Becoming a B Corp allows us to benchmark our environmental and social impact, evaluating every business decision we make with this top of mind and striving to make innovative choices that will further influence our positive impact on children and the world.The Change We Seek	

At its heart, Kabrita exists to support parents with great food they can trust and education to help them make nutrition decisions with confidence and joy. To accomplish this, parents need companies that are transparent about their business practices and ingredients, and give them the straight goods when it comes to discussions about products, parenting and nutrition.

Kabrita operates under the belief that, armed with clear information, parents are more likely to support companies that strive to do better for the environment and society. By joining the ranks of B Corps encouraging consumers to vote with their wallets, Kabrita hopes to influence other businesses to follow suit and examine their own practices.

Kabrita seeks to support all parents in their efforts to nourish their families and has an ongoing program to distribute Kabrita to families in need through our partnerships with community agencies and non-profit organizations. Through their own content and educational partners, Kabrita seeks to widen parents’ exposure to information that will keep their families healthy and happy and help them protect the environment.

Outcomes for Children’s vision is to make a positive and lasting difference for vulnerable children, families and communities. It’s mission is to provide solutions for individuals and organisations that help them achieve and its specific focus is upon developing and implementing Social Impact Bond and large payment by results social care solutions to address some of society’s most difficult problems for these beneficiaries. 




Outcomes for Children has been operating a Social Impact Bond contract with Birmingham City Council since the summer of 2015 to appropriately transition children in care from residential to foster care, safely bring them back into Birmingham communities, and improve their overall life trajectories. A similar contract has just commenced with Cardiff City Council. Outcomes for Children is a social enterprise within the Core Assets Group, who are a UK based founder owned international children’s social care organisation.



The independent certification and the rigorous standards applied for Outcomes for Children to gain accreditation as a B Corp evidence to our commissioners, the beneficiaries we work with, and a broader set of stakeholders that we are a mission driven enterprise, that we act in ways true our vision, and that we are committed to delivering social impact. This is invaluable when operating in a sector dealing with some of the most vulnerable people in our society.

The Change We Seek	



Outcomes for Children is continually seeking to improve outcomes for vulnerable children, families and communities, and continually exploring different ways to achieve this. Debates in the field of social care services can often become unproductively polarised and caricatured around public sector versus charity versus commercial sector provision and hinder collaboration to maximise social impact. The B Corp certification helps cut through to the characteristics of organisations that do make a difference and so will help move the debate on, and help parties identify suitable 'impact' collaboration partners.

Nova Sun Power has evolved from humble beginnings. In 1975, Robert MacKean received a "150 in 1 Electronic Projects Kit" form his father. It ignited a long-term passion for the power of renewable energy.

Almost two decades later, soaring energy prices in 1996 motivated him to find a better way to power his home. As an electrician, he knew he had the skills and knowledge to provide his family with energy security and save money. He contacted a supplier of solar modules in Ontario and purchased enough equipment to service his home as well as the homes of a few of his friends.

Today, Nova Sun Power is growing and thriving as a leader in renewable energy, sourcing the best systems for customers to ensure quality and durability over time.

From modest roots, we have become a company determined to be a part of the solution for our families, our communities and our planet. As a triple bottom line company (People. Planet. Profit.), we want to be part of a globally sustainable energy solution. 

The Change We Seek	

What began as a desire to lower energy costs in the summer of 1996 has become Nova Sun Power's call to action. Nova Sun Power doesn't just install renewable energy and solar systems; they actually reduce the long-term costs of energy to their clients while making positive environmental change. It’s a renewable energy uprising!

Corporations sometimes struggle to see beyond the bottom line. Nonprofit organizations occasionally need help presenting their business case to funders. The Communications Refinery, PBC, helps bridge such gaps for a wide range of organizations seeking to make a positive impact on the communities they serve through effective messaging, communication efforts and strategic development. Based at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, the firm works with local, regional and national clients.



On the corporate front, The Communications Refinery provides business consulting services for benefit corporations, fellow B Corps and other purpose-driven companies, with a focus on strategic thinking, message development and communicating achievements through vehicles such as annual benefit reports. It also serves the responsible investing community, helping develop messaging and content that resonates with individuals and institutions interested in investments that incorporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors or impact investments.



On the nonprofit front, The Communications Refinery offers grant writing and research expertise that eases the burden on busy executive directors and development directors who must tap valuable grant making sources for funding. From private foundations to public resources, the firm explores grant possibilities, assesses the opportunities and delivers grant applications tailored to each situation.



B Corp Certification reinforces our belief that businesses can thrive with more than a singular focus on shareholders, and nonprofits can prosper when their compelling story is shared effectively. As we dug deeper into the B Assessment, we also determined that it provides a solid framework for running a smart business rooted in accountability.

The Change We Seek	



There are many companies and nonprofits looking to achieve great things while doing what's right. The Communications Refinery helps them get there.



Fulfilling a purpose is just as viable for a corporation as it is for a nonprofit, and stakeholders matter for all kinds of organizations looking to enjoy a long and fruitful existence.

Close to half of the energy produced on this planet is used for heating and cooling and still most of it is generated by burning fossil fuels. That makes the vision of Thermaflex absolutely clear:



“Minimize the waste of energy and maximize the use of renewables.”



Thermaflex is a leading provider of smart, and sustainable distribution solutions for thermal energy. Our by nature inspired design for efficiency, durability and recyclability demands a minimum of resources for maximum benefit in respect to energy, economy, environment and quality of life. Thermaflex works closely together with its stakeholders to develop new innovations that meet the needs of today, and tomorrow.



Starting out in 1976 in the Netherlands, this family-run business has grown to be an international player with 5 production facilities and 16 sales and support offices worldwide, making a positive impact in over 45 countries worldwide. 



In Poland, Thermaflex started in 1992 as the first company in the Polish market in polyolefine-based solutions for the installation industry. Starting as a sales and distribution office, the highly successful market entry quickly saw the construction of a production plant in Żarów, near Wroclaw. Since 2008, Thermaflex North-East Europe has especially grown as a key player in this insulation market.



 Global threats such as climate change, resource scarcity and ecosystem health are our long term strategy drivers. We act on that strong passion through safe, recyclable and future-proof solutions together with our stakeholders. To be a B-corp means that we can better convey those values and inspire others to follow suit by using business as a force for good, and leave a positive social, and environmental impact. 

The Change We Seek	



 In the early days, thermal energy production and consumption were highly localized, based on local needs, available resources, limited technology and lower levels of comfort. With the discovery of fossil fuels this all changed dramatically. Yet it has now become very clear this shift is far from sustainable, nor equitable. 



Today the world increasingly strives for improving energy efficiency as well as searching of renewable alternatives. That is driving the development of both production and use of energy. Yet as energy sources diversify, provisions once again becoming more and more localized. In theory, everyone has the choice to become an energy supplier. Yet, whether on individual or community level, it is vital that the available capacities and fluctuating demands can be collectivized and well connected.



 In co-creation with its stakeholders, Thermaflex looks for smart energy solutions, gradually building for a common future and flexibly adapting to new circumstances and challenges. From generating ideas, through testing of prototypes to successful implementation. Thermaflex’ ‘high-energy’ team across the globe attaches a great deal of importance to working together to co-create substantial progress in this regard. 



 With Cradle to Cradle-certified components, Thermaflex North-East Europe is on a journey to fully recycle its products and only make use of safe, reliable and sustainable materials.

Winner of the SBN's Triple Bottom Line award, Mugshots is a socially conscious café with an extensive fair-trade drink menu and a local food menu consisting of soups, salads, sandwiches, yoghurt, and granola made with free-range & organic ingredients, bought from local farmers whenever possible.

Mugshots uses only fair-trade, organic coffee, and supports sustainable agriculture and local farmers. By doing so, they not only support the local economy, but also reduce fuel use associated with shipping. Mugshots received "Best of Philly" by Philadelphia Magazine and was voted the City's Best Coffeehouse by AOL City Guide.

Mugshots became a Founding B Corporation because we are committed to making sustainability an integral part of our business.The Change We Seek	

Mugshots is committed to making a positive contribution to our community by being mindful of the environment and our neighbors, both local and global, in all our actions. We aim to set an example in practicing a triple bottom line philosophy for other businesses in our community. We also seek to raise awareness around fair trade, the local food movement, and conservation.

• Working with Equal Exchange, we are able to offer only fair-trade, organic coffee at a reasonable price. Buying fair-trade certified coffee supports farmers by guaranteeing a fair price for their crops, prohibiting forced or exploitative child labor, providing credit to farmers at low rates, promoting sustainable farming methods, encouraging long-term business relationships, and organizing farmers into democratic cooperatives.

• We select our other suppliers based upon their business ethics and a shared commitment to the “triple bottom line,” a commitment to people, to profit, and to the planet. To reduce food waste, we send our juice pulp and coffee grounds to Green Meadow Farms for chicken feed and composting. In turn, we purchase a variety of food items from Green Meadow Farms, including seasonal, organic fruits and vegetables, eggs, which come from cage-free vegetarian-fed hens, bacon and ham which come from humanely-raised pigs, and free-range, all natural smoked turkey breast. Our milk comes from Lancaster Farm Fresh Cooperative.

• In addition to composting, we recycle paper, cardboard, plastic, aluminum and glass. We purchase our cleaning products from Green Village, a local supplier of environmentally-friendly cleaning solutions. Finally, a portion of our electricity is supplied by wind energy, a renewable source of energy with no fuel and no pollution.
