BOULD is an experiential education company, making green buildings available and accessible to ALL. We partner with affordable housing builders, like Habitat for Humanity, to transform building projects into green ‘learning laboratories’ for career development professionals and students. Equipping the next generation of professionals with the skills and experience to launch green careers, while simultaneously building affordable green homes for low-income families!


Impact was the sole driver behind BOULD, as our Team worked to develop our content and educational platform -- we were hell-bent on making green building easy for affordable housing builders and young professionals! And it was around that drive toward impact, that we developed a business model that made that impact sustainable. Now, with the B Corp Certification, we have the backing that our impact is real and can objectively convey that our our customers and delivery partners.



The Change We Seek®


BOULD has created an entry-level hands-on experiential education program that provides professionals and students with the hand-on, real world building experiences necessary to launch green careers. The program consists of 50 hours of training on a 4-month building project – where participants will get access to: design and planning meetings, green research and documentation, performance inspections, and even rolling-up their sleeves and building on-site! Upon program completion, graduates are qualified for LEED Accreditation, a credential that 71% of decision makers recognize as a necessity in the green building industry.


And the projects the participants work on? Habitat for Humanity affordable homes in their community! We're partnering with the 1,500 Habitat affiliates across the US to transform their building projects into these green "learning laboratories." The program was built specifically to plug into existing Habitat for Humanity affiliates and latches on to their existing building schedule.


In exchange for program facilitation, BOULD supports Habitat financially and in the green management of affordable, LEED-certified green homes for Habitat's low-income families. These green homes will save families $50,000 over 30 years in saved utilities and reduce CO2 emissions by 66%.

EPOCH PI provides independent, strategic advice to purpose-driven and culture-rich companies regarding raising debt and equity capital for growth and on mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, ESOPs, recapitalizations or selling a business. Identifying the best strategic option given the mission and vision of the company, as well as the best financial or strategic partner, requires a new approach. EPOCH uses proprietary culture tools to give insights into the parties’ alignment around values and mission and then uses corporate structure and thorough integration planning to address areas of concern. Financial terms are critically important, but evaluating the alignment of values, structuring the transaction to protect them, and creating a thoughtful integration plan are key to a transaction’s longer-term success.
 
EPOCH believes transaction success should be measured two or three years after the transaction closes, not simply because it did close. An ideal transaction creates shared success for multiple stakeholders (investors, employees, suppliers, customers, community). Success should be measured by asking whether it delivered the intended goals and whether it safeguarded the company’s mission and values.

WattElse Solar is an Australian energy company that provides solar energy solutions to help their customers achieve simple and smart energy freedom. The company grew out of a non-proﬁt community initiative that the founders established after they discovered how expensive and confusing it was to get solar for the homes. By the time they had organised the installation of 220 solar PV installations in their small regional Queensland community, it was clear they had hit on a gap in the market. Social Asset Measurements Inc. (SAM), incorporated in May 2011, is a consulting and software company that helps organizations measure, manage, and demonstrate their social impact. SAM has been twice-funded by the National Research Council of Canada via the Industrial Research Assistance Program for our work in developing the Social Return Intelligence Suite (SRI). The SRI provides on-demand reports for Social Return on Investment (SROI) and outcomes, hosts the largest global database of indicators and financial proxies (monetary approximations of the value created by interventions), and provides SROI and outcomes benchmarking. The company has developed core expertise in large-scale rigorous and credible frameworks that has been used for government reporting, financing, and internal stakeholder engagement (i.e. volunteers, staff, participants). Our clients are some of the country’s largest non-profit organizations and foundations.

Social Asset Measurements (SAM) is committed to advancing the social, environmental, and economic impact of our clients. Given this objective, and our belief that companies can provide both economic and social benefits, we decided to become a B Corp to solidify our commitment to improving social and environmental outcomes.

The Change We Seek	

Social Asset Measurements (SAM) strives to increase the capacity of its clients to enable them to easily and effectively analyze their programs. This is achieved through developing and implementing customized software services which clients can use to track and manage data related to their impact. In addition, SAM provides consulting services to assist organizations in developing impact measurement frameworks which the clients can use on an ongoing basis.

SAM recognizes that developing and implementing impact measurement frameworks can be a labour intensive exercise and that some organizations lack the internal capacity to develop these frameworks. To address this knowledge gap SAM seeks to assist clients in 1) developing measurement frameworks, 2) providing advice to grant making and on the ground organizations about gathering data and utilizing the frameworks, and, 3) reducing the administrative burden by providing automated software services.

As a result of delivering these products and services, organizations are positioned to understand how their programs create change and where there are service gaps and opportunities for improvement. This knowledge enables organizations to develop more effective programs and more clearly explain their impact to the public.

Creator of NobleHour® and Collaboratory®; community engagement software for the greater good.

That’s when the idea for NobleHour was born.

Over the years NobleHour has helped thousands of schools, nonprofits, and businesses across the nation connect volunteers with opportunities. It has also helped volunteers track, log, and verify those hours.

In 2014, TreeTop Commons LLC was created as the parent company to NobleHour. TreeTop Commons developed Collaboratory in collaboration with The University of North Carolina at Greensboro. The UNC Greensboro Institute for Community and Economic Engagement created an online database to organize and report their data from hundreds of community engagement and public service activities and relationships. Collaboratory builds off of UNCG’s experience to create a national database to further the understanding practice, and scholarship of community engagement.

The Organic Media Network is a global media company solely dedicated to educating and inspiring the public on healthy living, green solutions, and sustainability. Its primary vehicle is the national talk radio program An Organic Conversation and its online media platform offering interviews, video tutorials, blogs, recipes, DIY tips, and more. 

Topics include organic food production, tips for a healthy lifestyle on a budget, gardening, holistic nutrition, natural pet care, renewable energies, waste reduction, genetic engineering, social justice issues, instructions for making homemade non-toxic cleaners and beauty products, and observations about what makes life sacred.

The Organic Media Network and its programs are positive and inviting, dedicated to creating a language of possibility. The work of the Organic Media Network is to promote conscious decisions and experiences, believing in the power of inspired and educated individuals as the greatest change agents for creating a healthier world.



We believe that sustainable change happens through people, community, and the right commerce. The community of Certified B Corporations is creating a world where products and services help shape a standard of business that is based on transparency and responsibility which directly and immediately influences the quality of our lives now and for generations to come. Being B Corp Certified means seeing business as a cultural exchange, an opportunity to educate, a chance to make the world a better place by offering alternatives for the daily vote with each dollar being spent – values the Organic Media Network completely aligns with.The Change We Seek	

The Organic Media Network seeks to change the current conversation. 

By curating touching and inspiring stories from eco-savvy people all over the world, they highlight the intrinsic human qualities of dedication, beauty, and goodness that we all have in common. 

By sharing the whole story of a company, product, and its ingredients, they help people understand the full lifecycle of their purchases and the responsibility for all of our decisions.

By encouraging community engagement through online dialogue, they bridge isolation and are cultivating a language of possibility and empowerment, spoken with the voice of each individual listener.

Adjacent Consulting’s work focuses on three key processes:

First: Adjacent helps you build emotionally agile teams and develop emotionally agile leaders. All relationships, including those related to business, are based on emotional connections. Whether you; like someone, want to follow someone, believe in someone, or want to do business with someone, your motivations are directly linked to how you feel about that person. Strategy creates the structure of business, but it’s emotional intelligence that binds the structure together in an effective and meaningful way.

Second: Adjacent helps you become clear about your purpose. Daniel Pink, the author of Drive, states that we are motivated by three things; autonomy, mastery, and purpose. If the “why” of your business is fuzzy, they facilitate team sessions to bring your horizon line into sharp focus. From there, we work with your team to make sure every function, role and goal is aligned with that purpose. They help you create seamless alignment throughout your team so that everyone knows why and how they contribute to the overall purpose of the company.

Third: Adjacent helps you craft business strategies that achieve the optimal balance between people, planet and profit  — the triple bottom line. Every business invests their resources based on the values they hold dear. Some companies are primarily motivated by profit and pursue a business plan that uses their resources to maximize profit. Maintaining good paying jobs for their employees primarily motivates other companies. These companies devote their resources to keeping and rewarding staff. Whatever your industry or purpose, every company arrives at a unique balance between the competing priorities of people, planet and profit. We help you arrive at your unique balance.

Like B Lab, our foundation is in redefining business success.  At Adjacent we dream of a leadership surge that allows organizations to form and effectively pursue triple bottom line goals.  We gain great energy working with people aligned with this dream.

   The Change We Seek	

Adjacent Consulting's contribution to change lies in building capacity for purpose-driven organizations. They develop shared vision and culture for leaders and teams. Adjacent Consulting gets to the heart of what really matters to you by focusing on the skills and strategies that lead to meaningful, successful workplace relationships.

CafeGive Social is a social and mobile applications and cause marketing solutions company, whose platform and services empower companies and nonprofits to build effective social media campaigns around causes and community engagement. CafeGive Social provides companies with the tools they need to drive corporate philanthropy, and create deeper, more meaningful connections with customers around the issues and causes that matter to them. Using CafeGive Social’s platform, companies and nonprofits can raise funds and awareness for a cause, inspire and reward employee engagement and volunteerism, promote corporate giving campaigns, and develop a stronger competitive advantage through cause marketing.



CafeGive Social helps organizations and teams of all sizes create winning cause marketing campaigns. Their platform and solutions make it easy for socially responsible organizations to create branded social media campaigns. Whether building awareness, driving community engagement, or raising money for a cause; CafeGive Social will help find the right social media, mobile or web solution. They can also help you customize amazing Facebook pages and social messaging around your cause campaign. 

Managed and supported on their hosted solution, no code is needed to launch effective cause-related campaigns. CafeGive Social’s marketing platform and suite of apps (see www.cafegive.com/apps) includes pre-configured templates with a DIY dashboard that enables organizations of any size to easily upload logos, links, and copy to launch a fully-branded campaign in a matter of hours. Social Analytics tools allow marketers to identify campaign trends and anomalies, while measuring number of visits, likes, donations, and percent of goal met--everything businesses and nonprofits need to tell their cause stories, share their social goodness, or raise more money. 

To find out more or to request a demo, visit www.cafegive.com and connect with CafeGive Social on Facebook.

CafeGive Social aims to “walk the talk” by finding new ways to build social and environmental stewardship into its mission and business practices through employee engagement and volunteerism, strategic collaboration, and technological innovation. Such on-going sustainable practices make CafeGive Social well-positioned to help meet the cause-related marketing needs of businesses and nonprofits, and empower companies to launch effective cause marketing campaigns that serve the greater good as well as their bottom line.

The 3p Community is a diverse group of businesspeople, from social entrepreneurs to corporate executives, MBA students to consultants, each dedicated to using the power of business for good.

Founded in 1932, Oregon Cherry Growers (OCG) is a grower-owned cooperative of family farms located in Oregon’s bountiful Willamette Valley and pristine Columbia River Gorge, where families have been farming for generations. What began with 700 fruit tree “rootings” brought to Oregon by covered wagon in 1847 now encompasses more than 2,500 acres of orchards and fruit cultivation.

Managed by a board of grower-owners, OCG employs more than 400 staff at its processing facilities in Salem and The Dalles, Oregon, and processes an average of 25,000 to 30,000 tons of cherries annually, making it one of the largest producers and processors of sweet cherries in the world.

From fresh table cherries to maraschino, dried, frozen, glacé and blended cherries, to fruit products made with strawberries and blueberries, the cooperative has earned an international reputation for its top quality fruit. Its fresh and processed fruit is sold to consumers, restaurants, bakeries, confectioners, and food manufacturers around the world.

OCG sells its retail maraschino cherries and dried fruits under the Royal Harvest™ brand, all products of which are non-GMO Project verified, Fairtrade	 certified, made with 100% natural ingredients, and never contain artificial colors, flavors or preservatives. Royal Harvest™ products are now sold at www.amazon.com and select retailers.

Stewardship – we’ve been entrusted to continue the legacy of our organization for current and future stakeholders. By becoming a certified B Corp, we can become part of a larger community to support other like-minded businesses that share a similar vision for our planet, our communities, and each other. We are proud to be one of the country’s first agricultural cooperatives that are B Corp Certified.

The Change We Seek	

Oregon Cherry Grower’s purpose is to sustain the family farms of its co-op members and help preserve a way of life for future generations that speaks to its core values. As such, they are committed to Sustainability in every aspect of their business; nurturing a culture of safety and respect with its employees, and offering robust training programs to foster career growth and prosperity, engaging in community events to ensure a healthy place to live, work and play, providing safe, quality foods to its customers, and embracing environmentally responsible practices throughout its operations such as introducing natural methods for pest control, deploying water conservation practices, reducing waste through composting and mulching practices, and enhancing wildlife habitat.

As a Certified B Corp, Oregon Cherry Growers is proud to join a community of like-minded businesses that desire to make a positive, sustainable change for the world.

2b design is an award-winning company which transforms architectural salvage from conflict zones and other reclaimed materials into high end home décor. Currently the company operates out of Beirut, Lebanon and Cambridge, MA, USA. 2b design trains and employs directly and indirectly marginalized and disabled men and women to enable them to become world class artisans and enjoy a dignified living.  The company involves in its work people of diverse backgrounds to promote reconciliation. Its flagship brand is called Beyt which means House or Home in semitic languages. 2b design is often referred to as Beyt by 2b design. 

The company mission is to restore the unseen beauty of the broken. It includes 4 focus areas:  people, broken heritage, broken environment, broken relationships. 

2b design's creations can be found in Europe, the Middle East,  Japan and the US sold through a network of retailers or directly to customers. The products include lamps, tables, candelabras and other home decor made out of 18th, 19th c and early 20th century elements from destroyed houses in Syria, Egypt and Lebanon. Lampshades and cushions are handmade out of 18th or 19th c. linen, vintage ethnic fabrics and other fabric remnants.  Overall about 90% of the contents of each handcrafted item comes from recycled and repurposed raw materials. Since the creation of the business 100% of the workers who make the products have been recruited from marginalized backgrounds. 



Our concept of impact includes not only what we do directly but also through collaboration with other like minded individuals and organizations.  As a result becoming part of the B Corp community was a logical outcome of our desire to further expand our scope of collaboration and belong to a movement with high standards. We work in the US and in the Middle East where we are a Founding B Corp in Lebanon,  as such we hope to inspire other Middle Eastern companies to join the community and work for positive change in a region which badly needs it.

The Change We Seek	

Having started in a conflict torn region before replicating its model to the US 2b design strives to build a business that can be a powerful inspiration for change. The company aims to show that broken pieces of heritage or discarded materials can be transformed into elements of great beauty. It seeks to transform people who have been broken in their dignity, body, spirit or who come from disadvantaged backgrounds into talented individuals who contribute to a better world. 2b design wants to turn broken relationships between individuals of diverse faith, ethnic and cultural backgrounds into lasting bonds where differences build peace not create conflict.

PLUSfoam is committed to "saving the planet...one product at a time™." Using its proprietary, 100% recyclable compounds, PLUSfoam makes materials and components for manufacturers of branded consumer goods. PLUSfoam often outperforms the materials they are intended to replace such as traditional foams, plastics and rubber. 
 
The environmental mission at PLUSfoam has two components. The first occurs at the factory level. When other companies decide to use the material, PLUSfoam works with their factories to turn post-manufacturing scrap into valuable material once again. PLUSfoam’s unique chemistry and process ability allow the material to be recycled continuously with nominal degradation and without adding any additional agents.
 
The second component occurs at the consumer level. PLUSfoam makes it easy for end-users to send post-consumer goods back for recycling. This is a cornerstone of PLUSfoam’s business model. PLUSfoam brand partners actively participate in the reclaim effort by incentivizing their consumers to recycle their used goods with PLUSfoam by offering them a discount off of their next purchase. PLUSfoam operates reclaim facilities in the US, Canada, Europe, China, Korea and Japan where consumers can return any products made with PLUSfoam.

Simply Gum is the only 100% natural, premium chewing gum in the United States. Unlike regular chewing gum, which is filled with artificial flavors, preservatives, and synthetics, Simply Gum features only six all-natural ingredients. At the Simply Gum kitchen in New York, these ingredients are handcrafted into the highest quality gum on the market.  The result is a totally natural, biodegradable gum that is better for you and the planet. 

Simply gum was born out of the belief that consumers have a right to know what is going into their products. Our mission is to be transparent, honest, and responsible in everything that we do. We chose to become a B Corp in order to formally hold ourselves accountable to this mission. 



 The Change We Seek	

Conventional gum brands hide up to 80 synthetic ingredients in the catch-all term "gum base" on their labels. These ingredients include the same components of plastic bottles, rubber tires, and white glue. And although there are a few gums in the US market claiming to be "natural," none of them are actually 100% natural.

Simply Gum’s goal is to make a better chew based on the principles of transparency and honesty. A gum that is made from all natural ingredients.  One that is better for your bodies and the planet.  One that tells the truth and makes you feel better about yourself for chewing it.

It all started with one question: “Where does our food come from?” Amidst the rise of the ‘farm-to-table movement’, Localize realized something was missing – the retail shelf.
 
 Localize provides software, services, and expertise to manage local and specialty products in retail stores. They specialize in combining geo-tag location data with other important social attributes of food products, including certifications and verified claims. They provide software tools for retailers to manage portfolios of products specific to individual stores; and their system allows them to create tailored shelf labels to share information with shoppers. Information that is transparent, and relevant.
 
Their mission is provide value and insight throughout the supply chain and to empower shoppers with information behind the products they buy. They are constantly adapting to meet market needs and provide tools to support local food ecosystems, grow the market for innovative and amazing food producers - and most importantly, make sure that transparent and reliable information is available to shoppers when they make purchase decisions.

Make a Stand didn't start as a product. It started as a promise—in the heart of a little girl. One year ago, then eight year-old Vivienne Harr saw a photo of two boys, roughly her age, with giant rocks strapped to their heads. She learned that they were modern-day slaves. She thought slavery ended with Abraham Lincoln. She was wrong. She decided to do something about it. She set up a local lemonade stand every day to make a stand against child slavery. After 173 straight days, at the age of 8, she reached her goal and donated over $100,000 for Not for Sale, liberating hundreds of enslaved children in the process. The world watched in wonderment. That moment became a movement—and made a company. 

When she reached her $100,000 goal, Vivienne's parents said: "You did it, honey. You're done." Vivienne responded: "Is child slavery done? Then, I'm not done." The Little Lemonpreneur decided to "bottle the hope." Make a Stand Lemon-aid is now sold in grocery stores across the West Coast. It is a certified organic, Fair-Trade, nonGMO lemonade that is refreshing and contains less sugar than most lemonades.



Make a Stand’s brand promise is: “When you buy a bottle, we help a child. Together, we can end child slavery." Therefore, they created an immediate line between your purchase and impact on this issue. Five percent of all gross sales (5% of every bottle) go to 6 organizations helping end child slavery: Free the Slaves, UNICEF, Nepal Youth Foundation, Not For Sale, the International Programme on the Elimination of Child Labor, and GEMS. 

"Certified B Corporations are leading a global movement to redefine success in business" — and that resonated with us. Our 9-year-old founder put it best: "Make a Stand is not a business. It's a ‘giveness,’ a business in the business of giving.” Make a Stand is out to redefine success in business and we are immensely proud to be a B Corp.

The Change We Seek	

Make a Stand has an unwavering fidelity to its 9-year-old founder's dream of ending child slavery in this lifetime.

OneRoof, Inc. is a Berkeley California-based social enterprise company with extensive prior experience in delivering IT-enabled communications (e.g. Internet access, computer literacy, job skills, transportation ticketing and insurance services) to rural communities in India and Mexico.

OneRoof provides free software to effectively manage commercial public access computing in Internet cafes with its popular CyberCafePro	 software -- in nearly every country of the world.

The company’s gift of ’OneRoof by TechSoup’ to TechSoup Global (the world’s leading distributor of software to non-profits and NGO’s) is now available from them for managing government-supported Internet access in Telecentres and libraries across the globe.

As a B Corporation, OneRoof now helps enable inexpensive access to the Internet and computer literacy -- both critical for diminishing poverty and social inequality.The Change We Seek	

OneRoof supports the belief that Internet access should be a Universal Right and facilitated for people of all walks of life.

OneRoof’s CyberCafePro software helps bridge the digital divide by directly supporting the sustainability of commercial public access computing locations. For-profit locations have a better chance to stay open using effective management tools such as CyberCafePro.

Non-profit organizations can now more successfully seek continued public funding by presenting reliable social metrics about the people they serve that are provided via cloud-based reporting features that are unique to OneRoof by TechSoup.

OneRoof, Inc. is a global social enterprise with the dual goals to 'Do Good' and 'Do Well' – a double bottom line that we believe possible and by which we measure our success.
column10: Free Software to Manage Public Access Computing Locations

India’s first certified B corp, eKutir started in 2009 with a vision to provide equal opportunities and sustainable development to people at the “bottom of the pyramid.” It has created a first of its kind, integrated, data-driven platform to empower poor smallholders and create new jobs in rural communities. Originally operational in India, today the company is active in Nepal and Haiti. eKutir’s 74,000 farmers, with the help of over 400 micro-entrepreneurs, have seen average yields and income increased, while cutting operating costs. 

Independent assessments of eKutir’s social impact have also demonstrated improvements in gender equality. The ICT platform has since been applied to a larger variety of industries, including water, sanitation and food furthering its reach and impacting more than 100,000 lives in the rural markets. 

Since its incorporation in 2009, eKutir has set- up multiple subsidiary social enterprises to augment the model’s growth across food, agriculture, and sanitation, and in the process has received awards, capital and support from Facebook, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Government of India, World Bank, Inter-American Development Bank, and the UN, among others.

SCS Global Services is a pioneer and leader in third party certification and validation of environmental, sustainability, stewardship, life-cycle assessment, and food quality and safety claims. Founded in the San Francisco bay area in 1984, its aim is to help companies achieve the highest level of environmental performance and social accountability. SCS evaluates companies for compliance with standards such as the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC), Marine Stewardship Council (MSC), USDA Organic, BIFMA level, Veriflora, Safe Quality Food (SQF), British Retail Consortium (BRC), Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) and many more. Companies trust SCS to audit and certify their accomplishments in greenhouse gas offsets, organic and sustainable agricultural production, food processing and handling, responsible forest management, responsible fisheries management, energy generation, green building, product manufacturing, and supply chain management.

Since our founding in 1984, SCS has always been driven by the mission of advancing sound environmental and social business practices through the development and application of strong ecolabeling standards. By becoming B Corp certified, we are delighted to join a community of businesses dedicated to the path of sustainability, and hope to inspire others to adopt sustainability practices as a core component of their mission and success strategies.

The Change We Seek	

SCS is driving constructive change in the public and private sectors based on principles of sound environmental science and social accountability. SCS is accomplishing this goal in three ways: 1) by helping companies develop better products through greater understanding of the environmental and social benefits and trade-offs; 2) by providing decision-makers (companies, government policy makers, industry professionals and consumers) with reliable information about products, services and systems; and 3) by supporting the development of leadership standards that guide environmental and social performance toward long-term sustainability goals.

Invested Development is an impact investment management firm. ID’s mission is to reduce poverty in emerging markets through risk capital investments in innovative alternative energy and mobile technology startups. To achieve its mission, ID invests in seed- and early-stage, for-profit social enterprises that provide radically affordable technology solutions to the world’s underserved markets. 


ID’s focus on mobile technology and alternative energy is laser sharp. Within these sectors, ID provides equity investments (through the BSP Fund) and working capital (through the Impact Factoring Fund) to early-stage technology companies committed to serving the world’s poorest citizens. Investments and subsequent portfolio management are designed with the context of emerging markets in mind. Privy to the unique challenges that social enterprise startups face, ID also provides customized investor services, including program design and market insight. 



Through our initiatives, we are trying to catalyze the potential of impact investing and social entrepreneurship as a solution to global poverty. We became a B Corp to support and collaborate with like-minded investors and entrepreneurs also trying to use the power of business for public benefit. 

  

The Change We Seek®


Invested Development believes that innovative technology can contribute to the reduction of global poverty. Despite real progress and impact, decades of international aid and donor-supported programs have left nearly 1.5 billion people in abject poverty. ID recognizes the need to merge the heart of the social sector with the efficiency of the free market to finish what they started. 


As an industry, conservative estimates suggest impact investing will be between a $400 billion and $1 trillion industry by the end of the decade. The missing ingredients in impact investing are seed and working capital. Unlike the traditional technology sector, impact investing does not have hordes of prosperous industry veterans to catalyze investment with their keen industry knowledge, deep pockets, and extensive rolodex. ID combines its industry knowledge, network, and financial resources to catalyze the next innovative explosion and generate strong social and financial returns.

Little Bean Sprout is an environmentally sustainable online children’s apparel boutique and new retail concept. Customers who purchase from the site can buy brand new current season items and gently used items from previous seasons, and when their children have outgrown the apparel, they can sell the garments back for 5% cash or 15% store credit.  If the garments do not meet Little Bean Sprout quality control for resale, Little Bean Sprout assesses whether items are still useable for donation and if not, works with textile recyclers to ensure garments do not meet a fate in the landfill.  Customers enjoy eco-friendly collections as well as finely made clothing intended to last use after use.  

We firmly believe that corporations must embrace the people, planet and profit model of business. But it's not enough to say it; we have to act it. And we saw that being a Certified BCorporation would enable us to hold ourselves accountable to this model through its rigorous assessment process and system of measurement.  We are excited to be a part of this dynamic and growing community who share our values and see the importance of conscious capitalism.  

The Change We Seek	

Estimates suggest that approximately 2.2B pounds of textile waste related to kids' clothes ends up in landfills annually. And that's just from kids clothes. Little Bean Sprout aims to transform this waste by allowing customers to purchase new and used items, and then sell back when they're done. When an item is sold back it will either meet quality control for resale in the used section, be eligible for donation, or be sent to textile recyclers for processing ensuring that garments are kept out of our landfills. In fact, for every 12-15 garments reused per annum, approximately 5 pounds of textile waste is kept out of landfills. Across the population of children ages 0-11, that equates to over 244.5M pounds per annum kept out of our landfill system just by reusing garments. Little Bean Sprout is driven to close the loop on retail waste by educating it's community of customers, enabling them to choose to reduce waste in their purchasing practices, and giving them the option to remove garments from the system in a sustainable manner. Of course, all this plus the convenience and fun of shopping online.

The Green Engineer, Inc is a sustainable design consulting firm specializing in energy efficient and sustainable solutions for the built environment. Founded in 2005 by Christopher Schaffner, the firm currently has a staff of twenty-five, with twenty LEED-accredited professionals. The Green Engineer sees sustainability as a core goal shared by all design team members and stakeholders. 
 
 The Green Engineer Inc practices Integrative Design, a whole system approach, which looks at diverse connections in buildings and explores their inter-relationships. Their practice uses tools such as energy and daylight modeling and life-cycle assessment of materials, to analyze project performance and inform decision-making. They provide guidance in determining appropriate sustainable design measures for each project. The Green Engineer firm consists of both Project Managers and Building Performance Analysts, which enable them to mange a LEED project from start to finish. They also consult for non-LEED clients, including affordable housing agencies and other non-profit developers. The Green Engineer, Inc is a member of the U.S. Green Building Council, has adopted the Architecture 2030 Challenge, and is an Energy Star partner.

therethere is about “pride of place.” That place where you feel connected—your hometown, new town, or anywhere your memories live. With the help of local artists, the company has worked to create expressions of the local everyday to help deepen your connections to this place. For each shirt that is purchased, therethere donates a portion of the proceeds to local organizations working to strengthen your community. You see, every time you put this on, you’re helping to create a there, there.

We became a Certified B Corp because we believe businesses should be sustainable and accountable. We hope that in our work we create products that people love, while still being attentive to our effect on the communities and environment around us.

The Change We Seek	

Almost everyone wears screen printed t-shirts. It’s a very simple tool that people use to communicate their passions and eccentricities. At the same time, graphic tees have become a mass-produced, commercial product. Therethere tries to put the meaning back into the shirt, to enable people to engage in conscious, rather than conspicuous, consumption, celebrate the local, and connect to their communities, wherever they might be.

With Good Reasons, LLC is a small company dedicated to providing healthy, wholesome granolas and gluten-free snacks in a conscious way. It strives to protect the Earth, contribute to the local economy, and support social justice through its business practices. It's snacks and granolas are made in small batches to keep them fresh. They are made using whole foods, with less sweetener than most competing products and no chemical additives. With Good Reasons also uses fair-trade, local, and organic ingredients when available.

Recently, the company invested in solar panels which now provide all of the energy needs for the kitchen. The solar panels also charge the plug-in hybrid vehicle used for company transportation. With Good Reasons continues to do research to provide the healthiest snack products it can in the best non- toxic packaging materials. The company is committed to being part of the solution to creating a better world.

I started the company with deep consideration for all the principles that B Corps represent. This was before I even knew about B Corps. When I learned of them I thought it was important to join an organization that so closely aligns with the founding principles of With Good Reasons. These company goals are now verified by an outside source. And we at With Good Reasons can now stand united with others to create a brighter future for all. I think valuable change starts on the local level and I want to be a part of the movement to make that change.

The Change We Seek	

With Good Reasons seeks a world where business practices support well being for all life on this planet. They seek to have their food produced in a way that shows consideration for the whole of humanity and the whole person. This means they bake for the health and well being of their customers. It also means With Good Reasons wants to do their best to source their ingredients in a way that supports the health and well being of the communities that provide these ingredients. They hope by example they can encourage others to do the same.

Green Rising Marketing is a full-service strategy house that serves innovators and change-makers. They solve problems and think in systems, often using unorthodox, irreverent, or serendipitous methods to inform their work. They ask challenging questions, make unusual comparisons, and turn over rocks that may seem useless to others.

Green Rising strategizes with a marketing lens and focuses on long-term quantifiable results. Their work is extremely varied and includes consultation, strategic planning, branding (logo creation, websites, marketing collateral), public relations and experiential marketing to reach the environmentally-conscious consumer and increase profits for clients.

We believe that companies have a responsibility to make EVERY purchasing decision clear and honest. Third-party certifications like B Corp Certification are making this a reality. We want this to spread like wildfire.

The Change We Seek	

Right now, doing the right thing isn’t easy. There are greenwashers and pinkwashers and people who’d rather make a buck than build a relationship. People are being intentionally confused and misinformed on a daily basis, and even the good options are buried in the noise.

Green Rising exists to fuel movements—to activate people to serve a balanced world.

Green Rising wants to create a world where socially conscious becomes socially subconscious. Where, choices are easy, and scouring labels at the store is a thing of the past. A world where hidden manipulation is a criminal act, and people can make a living by doing good.

Centscere empowers donors to give a few cents to their favorite cause every time they Tweet on Twitter, post on Facebook or click ‘Like’. In addition, Centscere offers analytic and digital marketing services for nonprofit organizations. The company operates from New York City, but funds projects worldwide.

We became a B Corp because we’re devoted to creating transparency and relentlessly pursuing social goals as we simplify giving, one cent at a time.

The Change We Seek	

Centscere’s overall mission has three components: to make giving easily accessible to each and every person; to create an effortless donation process; and to deepen engagement between nonprofit organizations and their online audiences.

Centscere supports solutions to societal and environmental challenges -- global and local. A member of the Alliance To End Hunger, the Centscere team is especially committed to meeting the basic needs of every human. They understand however, that fulfilling such needs is multifaceted and complex. So Centscere supports animal welfare – essential to the lives of Southeast Asian farmers and American suburbanites alike. It supports ocean conservation – crucial to preserving food supply, reducing coastal pollution, and maintaining temperate weather patterns. It supports shelter over every person’s head, universal civil liberties, and the right to a live a long, happy life. It supports whatever solutions our donors believe will make a difference.

The Centscere team works closely with its nonprofit partners to establish and achieve clear goals. By delivering information in a manner that’s compelling and easily understood, Centscere helps them generate more gifts, especially from new donors engaged on social network. Centscere reduces fundraising costs while increasing the charitable pot, enabling nonprofits to devote more of their resources to solving society’s problems. Ultimately, Centscere aims to eliminate all barriers between those who provide funds and those who put those funds to work. On one hand, Centscere unscrambles complex global and local issues, transforming the work of nonprofits into lucid, accessible stories. On the other, it provides a platform that seamlessly enables any person to donate anywhere, anytime.

GO Box is the first and only reusable takeout container service offering customers a way to get their meal in an environmentally friendly, reusable alternative to the single-use disposable container. With a mission of "doing away with throw away," GO Box makes sustainable eating fast, easy, and convenient for people who eat on the go.

Customers subscribe to GO Box for unlimited use. After downloading the GO Box mobile app, they use the app when ordering food to get their meal in a reusable, durable takeout container. When they’re done with their food, they return the container to a nearby drop site, using the app to scan and return their GO Box. Then they’re ready to use GO Box again.

GO Box picks up the used containers, has them washed in a commercial kitchen, and returns them clean to vendors — all by bicycle!

We are a mission-driven business working to do away with throw away. We became a B Corp to amplify this mission while joining a community of businesses with similar values.

The Change We Seek	

Throwaway packaging litters oceans, piles up in landfills, and contributes greenhouse gases to the atmosphere. Every day in the U.S., millions of people get meals "to go" in single-use disposable clamshells or boxes. These containers require resources to produce, are used for a very short amount of time, and then end their short lives filling up landfills. In downtown Portland alone, food cart customers use and throw away about 60,000 disposable containers every month.

The problem, of course, isn’t takeout — it’s the lack of options available to people who eat out regularly but want to reduce their environmental footprint. GO Box gives people a fast, easy, and convenient alternative to singe-use disposables so they don’t have to worry about burdening our landfills when they grab a bite to eat.

Since launching, GO Box has prevented the use of over 100,000 disposable containers. They hope to spread their mission of doing away with throw away to cities across the U.S. and Canada, making it easier for everyone to make a sustainable choice when getting their food to-go.

By leading by example, we hope to encourage many of the excellent businesses in Staffordshire which have the B Corp values at their heart, to look to seek recognition too.The Change We Seek

Founded in 2012, Kina‘ole is a solar finance company that focuses on providing low-cost, solar energy to homeowners, business owners and non-profits throughout the United States. The Kina‘ole team is led by a group of solar professionals who work to ensure that the process of going solar is a seamless and positive experience for the customers’ transition to low cost, efficient clean energy.

Kina'ole strives to benefit their customers, their community and their environment and are excited to be one of the few B Corporations in the US that are leading the country's shift to clean, renewable energy.

We believe that today's business can be profitable while also being good corporate citizens. We believe that we can and should all strive to do good and deliver significant benefits to our customers, our communities and our environment. B Corporations stand for this and we hope that our commitment will spur others to follow.

The Change We Seek	

Kina'ole believes that their country needs to be the global leader in the shift to renewable energy and our goal is to lead this change. They push every day to deliver solar electricity for less than the cost for conventional sources and will continue to innovate and strive to see solar on every rooftop.

Zero to Go provides zero waste event services for events big and small in the NY metro area, reducing the footprint of events through careful planning, logistics and education. Zero to Go incorporates education into the work they do: their team of educators stand behind the compost, recycling and landfill bins and explain what items go into each one. One of Zero to Go's most successful events brought 4500 people to a craft beer festival where they only had 8 bags of landfill and 120 bags of compostables.
 
In addition, Zero to Go provides a bike-powered food waste pickup service in their home base of Beacon, NY. Food waste is the single largest and least recovered waste stream in the US, and the EPA estimates that 40% of what's in our waste stream is compostable. In our county, 65% of waste is incinerated and the rest landfilled. Zero to Go is working to divert food waste from the city of Beacon's waste stream to create compost, a profitable material that can be used to grow food, create jobs, and generate revenue. In this way, waste becomes a resource that everyone can profit from, and keep those profits within the community.
 
Reducing solid waste volume and increasing composting and recycling is an environmental and a financial good, and core to Zero to Go's mission.

A small company, owned and operated by friends Lauren Lilly and Jody Rollins.   Yellow 108 is named after the color code for a bright sunny yellow, inspiring curiosity and cheer.  The mission based brand was built to conserve resources by creating high quality, accessories and home wares made from salvaged and recycled materials.  Yellow 108 promotes its mission as a form of sustainability for the environmental, economical and social benefits combined.  Salvaged = Saved is the mantra. 



This is how...Salvaged materials = Limited edition production quantities and minimal waste manufacturingNo dyes = Reduced water consumption and water pollution Localized manufacturing = Products are made in the same country as they are salvaged to minimize shipping cost and pollutionCreativity = Positive alternatives to traditional methodsGreat People = Long term, trusting business and customers partnerships build a strong foundation for sustainable growth

This is why...
Founded in 2010, Yellow 108 has saved around 20 tons of material from landfills.  The mission to salvage must be implemented due to the alarming fact that in the U.S. alone the EPA estimates that textile waste occupies nearly 5% of all landfill space.  With an ever expanding network of friends, employees and vendors, the Yellow 108 company has grown to inspire artists, create jobs and increase salvaging trends in manufacturing around the world.



The certification from B Corp adds a level of responsibility and integrity that holds us accountable for the commitment we have to our mission and high ethical business standards.   The B Corp community is guaranteed to be a positive influence and we are honored to work alongside such a distinguished collective of sustainable companies.

The Change We Seek	

Yellow 108 seeks change rooted in community involvement.  By sharing the mission through example, it will offer the global community creative insight on how to be active participants in building a more sustainable world. The aim is to make 'Salvaged=Saved' as important as 'Recycle' in everyday life.

Institute B is a mission-based company that believes what’s good for the world is good for business. Rising Springs Inc. is a natural spring water company that stewards a unique geothermal source in the Sawtooth National Forest in south central Idaho. 

Rising Springs launched its first product, a natural mineral supplement (NMS), in November 2017. Rising Springs NMS is comprised of 100% geothermal spring water from the source. As an NMS, the product can be packaged straight from the source with zero processing of any kind – preserving the water’s beneficial minerals and high pH (9.4). Rising Springs contains ZERO contaminants (modern pollution or contaminants) to parts per quadrillion (PPQ).

Rising Springs is packaged in an environmentally-friendly low carbon footprint bag-in-box and is sold direct to consumers via the company’s website, www.risingspringssource.com, and in limited retail locations. Rising Springs will begin offering glass in 2020.

Rising Springs is packaged at the source with no drilling or pumping of the source – It is a free flowing spring. The water is collected in a source house, and the water flows by gravity, through stainless steel pipes, to the plant a few feet away from the source.

TriLibrium breaks the mold of Certified Public Accounting firms. The accounting profession is full of people who prepare tax returns, audit financial statements, project cash flow and otherwise account for the financial bottom line. Where conventional firms see those services as the sum total of their business, they view them as a starting point towards building sustainable communities. You notice the difference immediately in their name: TriLibrium is a synthesis of triple bottom line and equilibrium. “Triple bottom line” captures their commitment to the mutually supportive values—people, planet, profit—that distinguish a sustainable business. “Equilibrium” refers to their commitment to establish balance among the three bottom lines in all that they do for their clients and as a firm.

Inherent in their name is the promise of a different relationship than you’ve experienced with other accounting firms. Honest relationships define TriLibrium. You don’t treat your business, organization or life as a numbers game. And neither will they. In a triple-bottom-line world, numbers rarely tell the whole story or serve as an adequate guide for making decisions or measuring performance.

TriLibrium became a B Corporation to insure that the values of sustainability were baked into the firm's DNA. B Corporation offers a benchmark towards excellence and holds organizations accountable while providing guidance towards sustainable communities through holistic business practices.The Change We Seek	

TriLibrium's mission is to help businesses, organizations, and individuals succeed across the triple-bottom line: People, Planet, and Profit.

An economy exists to meet human needs. At TriLibrium, we’re contributing to an economy and building a business that works for all. For us, it all begins with honest relationships. It’s what our clients experience in the integrity and professionalism we bring to our engagements. It’s what our community sees in the passion we bring to our work as volunteers. And it’s what we share here at TriLibrium as we create the all-time best workplace.

Success at the expense of the environment doesn’t count. It’s as simple as that. That’s why we purchase 100% renewable energy for our offices. We offset 150% of our greenhouse gas emissions including employee travel. All of our sourcing and purchasing decisions take into account the vendor’s environmental (and social) policies and practices. And we recycle everything that can reasonably be recycled here in Portland.

As a CPA firm, we never need to be reminded of the importance of money; whether generating profits for businesses, helping individuals save on taxes or maximizing funds for nonprofits. Helping our clients reach their financial goals is at the heart of our business, tax and financial advice and services. We also value profits at TriLibrium. But making and spending them in support of a sustainable future matters even more.

ecojot is more than an eco-friendly stationery company; they are committed to giving back one journal at a time. Created in 2007, Ecojot designs and creates green stationery products that are printed and made in Canada. All paper and board used is 100% post-consumer recycled - no trees are cut down to make their products. The paper is acid free and processed chlorine free, and all inks and glues are vegetable based. The mill where the notebooks are made is even powered by biogas harnessed from a nearby landfill.

We became a B Corp because we believe that we are a different type of business. We believe that business can play a role in the positive transformation of society and we are happy to embrace this idea.

The Change We Seek	

The GIVE program started in 2010 and was done to show our support for materials that can help kids become literate. Many children cannot attend school because they lack basic school supplies and we donate pens and notebooks to kids in some of the poorest countries on earth. In 2013 ecojot worked with schools in Haiti, St Lucia and Grenada. To date ecojot has given over 240,000 notebooks and pens to children in need around the world.

CAP Global is a wholly owned subsidiary of Napo Pharmaceuticals. Napo is committed to the development and commercialization of novel, branded pharmaceuticals to global populations through the establishment of local partnerships.

Napo Pharmaceuticals is a privately held pharmaceutical company based in San Francisco, California. Napo's lead drug candidate, CROFELEMER, is under development for gastrointestinal indications, in persons living with HIV/AIDS. In addition to CROFELEMER, Napo has identified NP-500, a product for insulin-resistant diseases of Type II diabetes and Syndrome X. The company has a library of approximately 2,300 medicinal plants, all of which are available for screening for research and developmental purposes.

CAP Global became a B Corp to allow Napo to embrace and communicate in a legal manner to our shareholders and other business partners the importance of considering the interests of all stakeholders when evaluating various strategic business opportunities.The Change We Seek™

CAP Global’s mission is to accelerate the development of CROFELEMER for pediatric populations in the treatment of multiple diarrheal diseases and to provide these drugs cost-effectively to relief organizations in the developing world. CROFELEMER is a novel pharmaceutical agent derived from raw plant material, which CAP Global sustainably harvests from rain forest areas. CAP Global employs fair trade work practices in all local businesses established to supply the plant material. They have a long-standing commitment to provide benefit sharing to all rain forest populations in recognition of their intellectual contribution to the study of medicinal plants.

• Napo is conducting a Phase 3 clinical trial (ADVENT) to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of a new therapy with the investigational agentCROFELEMER, for the treatment of diarrhea in patients with HIV infection.

• Napo and Direct Relief International ("DRI") of Santa Barbara, California have allied in a novel for- profit/not-for-profit effort to provide a development stage pharmaceutical product to pediatric populations in disaster situations and resource-constrained geographies, termed the Crofelemer Access Program ("CAP"). As part of the CAP, Napo has committed to sustainably provide CROFELEMER to DRI, for distribution to developing countries where cholera and other gastro-intestinal diseases are most prevalent.

In addition to CROFELEMER, Napo has identified NP-500, a product for insulin-resistant diseases of Type II diabetes and Syndrome X. The company has a library of approximately 2,300 medicinal plants, all of which are available for screening for research and developmental purposes.

CAP Global became a B Corp to allow Napo to embrace and communicate in a legal manner to our shareholders and other business partners the importance of considering the interests of all stakeholders when evaluating various strategic business opportunities.The Change We Seek™

CAP Global’s mission is to accelerate the development of CROFELEMER for pediatric populations in the treatment of multiple diarrheal diseases and to provide these drugs cost-effectively to relief organizations in the developing world. CROFELEMER is a novel pharmaceutical agent derived from raw plant material, which CAP Global sustainably harvests from rain forest areas. CAP Global employs fair trade work practices in all local businesses established to supply the plant material. They have a long-standing commitment to provide benefit sharing to all rain forest populations in recognition of their intellectual contribution to the study of medicinal plants.

• Napo is conducting a Phase 3 clinical trial (ADVENT) to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of a new therapy with the investigational agentCROFELEMER, for the treatment of diarrhea in patients with HIV infection.

• Napo and Direct Relief International ("DRI") of Santa Barbara, California have allied in a novel for- profit/not-for-profit effort to provide a development stage pharmaceutical product to pediatric populations in disaster situations and resource-constrained geographies, termed the Crofelemer Access Program ("CAP"). As part of the CAP, Napo has committed to sustainably provide CROFELEMER to DRI, for distribution to developing countries where cholera and other gastro-intestinal diseases are most prevalent.

Mobile Accord, founded in 2005, is the leading enterprise mobile platform provider dedicated to driving social change through the mobile phone. Mobile Accord works on mobile-social initiatives to change the world for the better.

In 2007, the Mobile Accord team founded the text giving channel and launched mGive, the leading mobile donation platform in the Unites States. The mGive program remains the foremost source of domestic mobile donations for leading nonprofit organizations. mGive processes 85% of all mobile donations in the U.S. and has partnered with nonprofits on over 10,000 mobile campaigns.

Deployed in countries in Africa and Central Asia, the service gives organizations access to GeoPoll’s proprietary user database which enables surveying of millions of people targeted by location and demographics. GeoPoll allows close to real time surveying, providing organizations the information they need, when they need it.

We became a B Corp because we feel that commercial entities such as ourselves, who aspire to change the world through social impact, should be recognized for their efforts and have a platform that provides the means for engaging and networking with similar organizations.

Abroad, Mobile Accord seeks to facilitate open communications by building and implementing innovative mobile solutions through the GeoPoll service. Domestically, mGive, a subsidiary of Mobile Accord, provides nonprofit mobile solutions designed to facilitate donor engagement and fundraising through text messages.

Springleaf Strategies is a marketing and sustainability consulting firm focused on helping businesses grow through planning and implementation of strategic business initiatives.

Springleaf Strategies specializes in sustainability-focused marketing for companies in the green building industry, municipalities, and firms in the renewable energy and natural resource conservation sectors. The company also works with companies interested in developing a roadmap for incorporating the fundamentals of environmental stewardship,economic strength, and community into daily operations.

Founded by Evelyn Contre, Springleaf Strategies provides a full array of services for marketing strategy and communication planning. All of its services are designed to help you develop a communication plan that aligns your business objectives with your commitment to sustainability.

Springleaf Strategies is committed to making a positive impact in the business community and providing leadership by evaluating its own operations to reduce its carbon footprint, conserve resources, reduce waste, support local businesses, give back to the community through time and resource donations, and provide opportunities for employees.

Springleaf Strategies’ mission is to improve the performance of businesses and organizations by integrating the fundamentals of environmental stewardship and social responsibility into day-to-day operations. Springleaf Strategies became a B Corporation to synthesize and communicate its commitment to the environment, its community, and building a successful business. The company believes the values of being a B Corporation are key components to 21st century leadership and preserving the long-term health and attractiveness of its company.

DO GOOD Real Estate was founded on a simple belief that they can create a real estate brokerage firm that really matters. DO GOOD is a socially minded real estate firm based in Wilmington, NC that donates 10% of sales commissions to local charities and nonprofits of their clients choosing. The name "Do Good" conjures up a sense of feeling good because it's not just a catchy name - it's tied to a unique value proposition based on "Creating Tomorrows Community" by combining quality real estate services with fundraising and charity.

We became a B Corp because it's too easy for any company to just claim they are trustworthy, but by becoming a certified B Corp we are proving it to our clients and our community.The Change We Seek	

Do Good Real Estate is about more than just selling homes or donation money; it's a mindset. It's about creating a socially minded business that attracts clients who feel the same way we do about giving something back. It's about making other people feel good about themselves, while helping other people in the community. They believe that their homes are not islands. They are deeply rooted in the community that surrounds them. They believe they can make that community better by inspiring others to "DO GOOD".

The Corps is a collaborative of accomplished agencies, firms and freelancers who come together because they want to use their talents to build a better world. Ideaction's clients include companies and causes doing good.  If you have a project that aims to make a positive social impact, Ideaction Corps can help. 

Ideaction Corps Mission: Ideaction Corps make the world better by connecting inspiring ideas for change to passionate talent that can execute, and expectional professionals to paid work with purpose. 

Ideaction Corp's business model means their bench of expertise is wide and deep.  Corps members' services include communications and messaging, corporate and nonprofit partnership development, digital media amplification, government relations and advocacy, impact and outcomes measurement, market research, public and media relations, sponsorship and philanthropic strategy, visual storytelling, web design and much more. 

We became a B Corporation because Ideaction Corps believes that doing good is not about your tax-exempt status, but about your purpose and your impact. The line between “non-profit” and “for-profit” is increasingly blurred, and we think that is a good thing. The magic happens when people come together around a shared vision and use their passion and talents to make a difference.The Change We Seek	

A social change enterprise, Ideaction Corps works exclusively with partners that pursue positive social impact. By helping clients create, amplify and implement strategic social-change initiatives, we’re using power of business to solve social and environmental problems.

Ideaction’s unique business model means that we are not only helping solve social problems, we are helping other businesses solve them too. By providing a platform for collaboration on projects and access to work that has meaning, Ideaction’s Corps members are able to channel their talents towared projects that make a difference and collaborate around a shared vision with others doing the same.

Green Home offers thousands of trusted products for home and business from compostable goods to organic mattresses and offers sound advice for living green every day. More than just about the environment – Green Home is about healthy simple choices. Every product is tagged with one or more top ten green attributes that include: Health Conscious, Organic, USA Made, Sustainable, Non-Toxic, Compostable, Energy Efficient, Water Conserving, Socially Conscious, and Recycled/Upcycled. The Green Home Team takes the time to listen to their customers’ needs and truly cares about the people and products they represent.

Green Home’s mission is simple: green the home, green the planet. Greenhome.com is the all-in-one online store and resource center for green living and green business. Making a difference since 1999, Greenhome.com makes it easy to green first what matters most. Whether the change is looking to live a healthier, simple life, or to become a more sustainable business owner, Green Home starts in our own backyards, literally, by effortlessly shifting to sustainable consumption habits. 

Green Home became a B Corp because it is what comes naturally to us and has since 1999. We feel every product we sell improves and supports the sustainable community we are trying to grow and being a B Corp allows us to prove we proudly walk the walk and talk the talk.

The Change We Seek	

The real power to make change lies with our everyday choices, and starts at home. Greenhome.com truly believes that positive change can happen with simple adjustments to everyday habits. Choosing a non-toxic cleaner and compostable trash bag doesn’t disrupt the flow, but improve it. These changes affect everyone around us; ourselves, our family, our community, and our environment. Green first what matters most.

Greenhome.com is committed to selling only proven green products in a wide variety of categories including, but of course not limited to, solar LED lighting, compostable clear cups, recycled plastic toys, and sustainable yoga mats. Personal attention is given to everyone who is ready to make the change to better themselves, their business, and the environment around us.  Change is not just about preserving the environment, but is about the people and community we support and Greenhome.com is proud to be one of the original pioneers of this movement.

Incite Directives works with businesses and building owners to integrate sustainability into the cultural cloth of their organizations, beginning with facilities and operations. The firm designs and executes a customized mix of energy audits, certifications and marketing messages which allow businesses to meet their sustainability goals. Incite specializes in developing a comprehensive sustainability strategy that helps clients green their operations, improve their market position, and save costs in the long and short run.

We became a B Corp to walk the talk! Every day we help our clients become more responsible corporate citizens. What better way is there for us to illustrate interdependence and environmental responsibility than as a B Corp? We believe in helping all companies find ways to improve, starting with their built environments, and we aim to show our clients that less really can be more.The Change We Seek	

In a perfect world, businesses and buildings would make a positive impact on the natural environment. Incite strives towards this vision by helping companies weave sustainability into their day-to-day operations with a customized strategy of retrofits, certifications, and marketing messages. Incite also works to foster good stewardship by improving the efficiency of commercial buildings and business operations. This creates a win-win situation for businesses and their clients, reducing ecological footprints and generating more harmony in the world.

The Big Idea Cooperative is a a bookstore and cafe owned by eight worker-owners in Pittsburgh, PA. The Big Idea provides literature that is multicultural, women-positive, queer-positive, class-conscious, anti-militaristic,and that promotes a sustainable world and community. It is a cooperatively owned and operated, not-for-profit, non-capitalist establishment. Founded in 2001 as an S-Corporation and only a bookstore, the group recently became an LLC, formed a worker-owned cooperative, and opened a cafe in late 2011. The new changes have brought exciting success and new opportunities, and the B Corporation certification shows The Big Idea's members and community that we are committed to social, environmental and economic justice.

We became a B Corporation to show our members and community that we are serious about our commitment to social, economic and environmental justice--so much so, that we wrote it into our operating agreement and hold ourselves accountable to B Corporation principles. We are excited to be one of Pittsburgh's very first B Corporations and to help set the trend for socially just business practices locally and globally.

             The Change We Seek	

The Big Idea seeks to provide members of the Pittsburgh community with a safe, welcoming space for all individuals to explore radical and alternative ideas. Our cafe sources ethically and locally produced products and all of our cafe offerings are vegan, fair-trade and organic as often as possible. The Big Idea partners with several community organizations, such as Book 'Em, a books-to-prisoners project, and Building New Hope, a nonprofit that works with cooperative coffee farms in Central America. We regularly host community meetings and actively seek input from our members to guide our efforts and growth.

Emory Knoll Farms, dba “Green Roof Plants”, is a long-standing leader in the green roof industry (since 1998), providing the highest quality in plants, knowledge, and service for green roof projects across the U.S. and around the world. Our nursery is located on 150 acres of conservation farmland in Maryland, on the East Coast of the U.S. We have provided plants for over 1,000 green roof projects, totaling hundreds of acres of planted roofs. As green roof specialists, we are active in green roof plant research and maintain several test roofs at our nursery. We are constantly acquiring and studying new varieties of plants, and collaborate on green roof research projects at educational institutions and nurseries in North and South America, Europe, Asia, and Australia. Our plugs are propagated in custom-blended growing medium that we developed specifically for use in green roof installations, mapping it to the air-filled porosity in green roof growing substrate. As a result, our plugs integrate faster, become established more quickly, and have increased longevity once on the roof.

Our diverse selection of plants is the product of many years of solid horticultural experience, both in greenhouses and on green roofs. Over time, we have evaluated over 1,500 species for their viability in green roof installations, selecting the strongest species that are best suited to the challenging environmental conditions found on a green roof. We keep over 100 different green roof species and cultivars in our regular inventory, including succulents, groundcovers, perennials, and North American Natives. We regularly inventory over 2 million plants, ready for shipping each season. We are the innovators of the most frequently specified Green Roof Mixed Flats, and we carry a variety of mixed flat blends for different geographic regions and design applications. Our carefully chosen plant palettes excel at creating biodiversity on the green roof, including providing vital habitat for pollinators. We are a preferred green roof grower for custom and contract work, and ship nationwide. We consistently hear from our customers that our level of service is the highest in the industry.

Our knowledgeable staff provides plant and green roof expertise with every order. We are widely experienced green roof consultants, and have worked with architects, designers, installers, and maintenance professionals on green roofs in all geographic regions of the lower 48 states, as well as internationally in England, France, New Zealand, China, Australia, Mexico, and Morocco. We use our knowledge and experience to provide real-world plant solutions for your green roof projects.

Our nursery operations and business practices are founded on the core ideas of long-term economic, social, and ecological sustainability. Becoming a B Corp made perfect sense for our company, because we have been operating as one since we incorporated in 2004. In October 2010, Emory Knoll Farms became one of the first Benefit Corporations in Maryland under the nation's first Benefit corporation statute.

The Change We Seek	

Emory Knoll FArms became involved in the green building industry because they believe strongly in the significant environmental and public benefits that green roofs provide: mitigating storm water runoff, filtering and sequestering atmospheric pollutants, reducing the urban heat island effect, providing essential pollinator corridors, and restoring green space in urban environments. Green roofs also benefit building owners and occupants by lowering cooling costs, increasing property values, and by turning otherwise unused space into potential amenity space. Emory Knoll Farms also seeks to be a role model for other nurseries and small businesses of any kind, proving a business can operate in environmentally responsible and socially just ways, while providing equity for stakeholders. To this end, we:Hire local people, employ them year round, and pay them as professionals. Our payroll supports just a few talented and dedicated people that contribute to our bottom line(s) in every way.Designed our operations to require the minimum possible amount of all energy sources, saving money AND the environment. We use alternative and renewable energy sources such as on-site solar and wind energy. The majority of our nursery is run off the grid. We also off-set the carbon footprint of every shipment of plants.Utilize Integrated Pest Management practices (IPM), minimizing the use of chemical fertilizers, and avoiding altogether the use of pesticides except in the rare case where they are required by law.Maintain a restoration program for native flora and fauna, providing vital habitat and food sources in a heavily developed agricultural area.

Bull City Burger and Brewery & Pompieri Pizza are locally owned, independent restaurants. Plus they have a craft brewery all located in downtown Durham, NC. The restaurants serve lunch and dinner. They offer a family friendly atmosphere featuring children’s play areas, outdoor patios as well as a private meeting room for business gatherings, events and presentations all within full view of our food preparation, brewing and cooking.
 
The restaurants are very much “farm-to-fork,” working closely with North Carolina pasture-raised beef and pork farmers supplying meat with no added hormones and no antibiotics. They work with farmers growing vegetables for their restaurants. They are also "back-to-scratch" with the menu streamlined and nearly everything produced on-site including house made buns, sauces, cured meats, gelato, hot dogs and bacon. The restaurants do not use artificial sweeteners, high fructose corn syrup, or hydrogenated oils. Their kitchens really do prepare everything including the mustard, the slaw, the pickles, the mayo, the aioli, the pepperoni, the mozzarella cheese, the crusts, the sausage, the relish, yes everything but the ketchup (we couldn't keep up with the ketchup demand).
