Audiences today identify more personally with their favorite brands and causes. They say their choices tell you something about who they are, their values, and what they believe. They understand it’s no longer okay to be an oil baron by day and a philanthropist by night.



Inward Point is a full service events agency telling powerful brand stories while transforming an outdated industry. All their events are environmentally smart and socially conscious -- with the data to prove it. They also integrate behavioral science + biophilic design to deepen guests' delight and drive their engagement. Their happy clients include Fortune 250s, nonprofits, universities, conferences, and individuals.



Since Inward Point's inception, the company's core value has been to use business to make the world a better place. One of the great things about being event producers, is that we get to decide who we hire. Which is why we put an emphasis on targeting local mission focused companies that are trying to be more environmental conscious or socially responsible. We also look for companies that are owned by previously marginalized groups.



The B Corp community is a group of companies with similar goals. By being a part of this community we will have the support and resources to ensure that our business is as impactful as possible. By being a B Corp, it differentiates us from other events production companies, that do not consider their impact when planning an event.





The Change We Seek	



In real life (IRL) marketing and events, tend to be extravagant wasteful affairs. Companies use these events to impress people and typically no cost or luxury is spared. Decisions such as beef as the main course, using balloons as a promotional tool, or purchasing more materials than are needed and then sending most of those materials to the landfill, are regular aspects of most events. These decisions undermines companies, especially companies that are trying to do the right thing. We help companies integrate environmental and socially responsible behavior, into a critical and outward facing aspect of their business.



Inward Point would like to see every aspect of an event have a purpose, aimed at making the world a healthier more socially beneficial place.

Elvis & Kresse have been reclaiming heroic materials ever since they fell in love with London Fire Brigade's decommissioned fire-hose. After a distinguished career fighting fires and saving lives the hoses were destined for landfill. They started to rescue the hoses in 2005 and never looked back.
 
More materials soon followed, Kresse has always had an obsession with waste and likes nothing better than discovering and intercepting something new. The challenge is the same every time - what can be done to prove value, change perception, and respect these resources.

Today, Elvis & Kresse's highly skilled craftspeople make beautifully designed bags and homeware. 50% of Elvis & Kresse's profits are donated to charities related to their raw materials, 50% of their profits from the fire hose range go to The Fire Fighters Charity. London's fire hose was just the beginning, the team reclaims more than 12 different materials and has saved over 300 tonnes of material from landfill.

Abramar is a multi-disciplinary real estate developer, pioneer of Social Urbanism, meeting rigorous standards of social and environmental performance, accountability, transparency and financial returns. The profitable, award winning company leads its markets by selling top-quality yet affordable housing to lower-middle income buyers while remaining a steward of the city and the environment. Abramar's projects are audited by Deloitte LLP, have received an A- credit rating from Austin Rating, obtained GERIC from Caixa and has credit lines with most major banks. Abramar is a frequent keynote speaker on such as events like "social entrepreneurship" (at the Beijing Forum), "happiness" (At Columbia University), "real estate development" (At REIW São Paulo) and "online business management" (At Google HQ), and has been featured in publications such as The Economist and Money Today.

The team represents 6 nationalities, is 50% bi-lingual, 50% women, 70% practice sports regularly, and thanks to its low turnover tenure length averages 4 years. One fifth of the team is dedicated to intellectual property which allows Abramar to innovate technology and design for scalable positive impact in the neighborhoods it develops.

We believe that value is measured not just in financial return but also social and environmental impact, so we wanted to be part of a community of companies that feel the same. The B Corp community is a step in the right direction of changing the conversation world wide on what value really is. We think that as part of the B Corp community we can broaden our reach to evolve the build world.

The Change We Seek	

Over the next 20 years the world will construct enough housing that if we stacked it, it would equate to 5 buildings to the moon! The way we develop these 'moonscrapers' will influence our quality of life, consumption, energy usage, nature and the urban landscape. Through Social Urbanism we've created a method of high environmental and social standards that can improve the quality of life for thousands of families and future generations directly and indirectly not just in Brazil but any country.

Your Message Media provides a full range of communications services for local, regional, national and international non-profit organizations, foundations and labor organizations, as well as progressive political causes and enterprises. You can see the full array of YMM's professional services as well as creative samples at www.yourmessagemedia.com.

YMM has extensive experience in branding, advertising and design; writing, design and production of materials such as reports, brochures, posters, packaging, labeling and other collateral materials; traditional public relations services such as strategic communications planning, message development, spokesperson training, preparation of press releases and relationships with reporters and community groups; and internet strategy and writing, web site design, social networking, and texting campaigns.

In addition to being a B Corp, YMM is a certified San Francisco local business enterprise and a certified Small Business with the state of California.

Your Message Media became a B Corp to join its community of good causes and help them develop smart communications strategies, well-designed materials, effectively trained spokespeople, and compelling messages.


 The Change We Seek	

Good causes succeed when they communicate effectively about what they do. For clients looking to find their way in today's rapidly changing media environment, the first question should be: "What's your message?" Devoting precious resources to setting up a social media presence or getting in the news is a waste of time and money if you don't use those vehicles to move your message. Every communication should be strategic and advance your cause. Who's your audience? What's your goal? No matter what your medium, without a message you're just spinning your wheels.

Your Message Media has worked with organizations large and small to craft messages that maximize their communications opportunities.

For Planned Parenthood, YMM created the "Planning is Power" campaign which re-established this pioneering organization as a positive family planning service. For anti-death penalty organizations in California, YMM counseled adoption of the term "state killing" to describe the government's policy of executing prisoners. For foundations and organizations fighting the nation's obesity epidemic, YMM provided language that helped them show how low-income communities cannot eat healthy and burn off calories without access to healthy, affordable foods and safe places to exercise and play. For San Francisco Bay Area transit unions facing concerted attacks on public employees, YMM helped them remind people of their value providing "safety and service" for their daily commutes.

No matter what medium you use to communicate, you need a message. Your Message Media can help you find, craft and target yours.
column10: Full service advertising, branding and public relations

Quality, durability, performance, and necessity are our enduring values due to the near-mythical challenges of the unpredictable Icelandic climate and because, as a small nation, our customers have always been our friends, family, and neighbors. Our clothes reflect the sometimes-hostile nature around us and our promise of protection for our community.

We want the world to experience the power and beauty of the North. This means clothes that make life and activity possible where there would otherwise be none, and business practices that conserve and protect the North at a time when our glaciers, and natural landscape are under dramatic threat from climate change. This is what we mean when we say our products are “Made for Life.”

Reel Change If it feels like we’re making an awfully big deal out of seemingly small things like toilet paper and paper towels, well, we are. But here’s the thing: nearly everyone uses toilet paper and paper towels every single day. By making a small change to the products we buy and use on a daily basis, we can collectively make a very meaningful impact on big issues like deforestation, plastic pollution and climate change. 

Switching to tree-free, plastic-free toilet paper and paper towels might initially seem like a drop in the ocean—one that only produces a few ripples. But as more consumers demonstrate an interest in more sustainable products, more businesses will invest in developing solutions to meet that demand. And as more people vote with their wallets, more politicians will take note and draft more legislation pushing sustainability initiatives. Before long, those ripples turn into waves. And that’s how Reel Change becomes possible.

Delight manufactures and distributes hearing aids at affordable prices. While untreated hearing loss may lead to social isolation of the elderly population, Delight aims to prevent such emotional and social consequences with its products, hearing aids. In order to provide qualified products at affordable prices, Delight used appropriate technology to standardize the hearing aids that are more fit for Asian physical characteristics and distributed them solely via its directly owned branch stores nationwide. Delight was able to launch a product at an innovative price of approximately $299, which was equivalent to the government subsidy for hearing impaired people in Korea. Today Delight provides diverse models ranging from 2 to 16 channels.


As an established pioneer in the realm of social enterprises in Korea, Delight endeavors to continuously enhance its identity as a well-intentioned and yet sustainable corporation. Connecting with B Corps worldwide will enable us to gauge where we are currently at and to guide where we should be heading to set the global standards.

The Change We Seek	

Delight’s primary goal is to “make a world where there is no one who cannot listen because one has no money.” It cut down costs with appropriate technology and lean distribution channel. For those who have difficulty in paying a lump sum upfront, Delight provides interest free installment payment services up to 12 months when paying with credit cards. In addition, Delight created job opportunities not only for senior citizens who are aged over 65 to deliver the products from the headquarters to the branch stores, but also for the hearing-impaired people who are dexterous and highly developed in hand-eye coordination.

Most furniture purchased today will have a date with a landfill within a decade. Contrast that with the lifetime warranty on all residential furniture from The Joinery, an Oregon manufacturer of handcrafted hardwood furniture since 1982. In its 20,000 square foot Portland woodshop and showroom, The JoineryÕs talented artisans create pieces that are as beautiful as they are durable, using classic joinery construction techniques, sustainably harvested wood, and natural oil finishes. Each piece of furniture is signed by its builder. This level of ownership is a source of pride and signals a deep commitment to each and every piece.
 
 For The JoineryÕs skilled designers and master craftsmen, there is a clear relationship between form, function, material choice and sustainable practices. The overwhelming majority of lumber used in its products is locally sourced, certified by the Forestry Stewardship Council, or both.
 
 No wood scraps or sawdust are ever sent to the landfill. All scrap wood is recycled into new products or donated to area woodworking programs. One symbol of this commitment is the companyÕs annual Metamortise Award, which honors the employee who designs and builds the most innovative piece of furniture from leftover lumber.

IBA (Ion Beam Applications S.A.) is the world leader in particle accelerator technology. The company is the leading supplier of equipment and services in the field of proton therapy, considered to be the most advanced form of radiation therapy available today. IBA is also a leading player in the fields of industrial sterilization, radiopharmaceuticals and dosimetry. The company, based in Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium, employs approximately 1,500 people worldwide, in Belgium, USA, Germany, China and more than 20 other countries. IBA is listed on the pan-European stock exchange EURONEXT.
IBA is proud to join the B Corp community, which is the culmination of a long process that involved all aspects of the company. It is the starting point of a new approach which was already present since years in its culture but which now takes on a whole new dimension. The assessment that led to the B Corp certification helped identifying the points that IBA can work to improve upon. In accordance with B Lab requirements, IBA has also modified its legal status to formally integrate its commitment to consider the consequences of its activities and the interests of all its stakeholders, namely its shareholders, employees, its customers and their patients, its suppliers, the community, and the planet.

WebChair reintegrates homebound children dealing with chronically diseases or autism into their classrooms using videoconferencing to provide social connectivity.

The WebChair service combines both advanced videoconferencing technology and pedagogical expertise into an innovative solution that enables homebound children -due to chronic illnesses or psychological issues such as autism - to access education from anywhere and enjoy the company of their peers virtually despite their challenges.

The WebChair technology is a simplified videoconferencing system that is both portable and very easy-to-use. From the experience of helping over 900 children the firm has developed a unique expertise in the area of distance education and special needs which is a core portion of the integrated technological structure.

Becoming a B Corp helps us stay sharp, focused and dedicated to our dream and shows the world how social impact and financial profit combined can be successful. We believe that doing business for good is the only way to solve the critical social and environmental issues that we are facing today. The B Corp model helps us communicate our great work to the community more effectively and inspire others.

The Change We Seek	

Yearly, more than 250,000 children in Europe - in the age of 5-18 years- are missing school and social contact with their peers because of somatic or mental disorders. Currently, their parents, schools and caretakers are struggling with solutions that are resource intensive, involve complex application procedures and they are not applicable and effective to every child.

WebChair addresses the problem of social reintegration for homebound children by giving them a vehicle to remain connected to their school environment, lowering the barriers of isolation so that reintegration becomes possible.

WebChair’s mission is to cultivate and make accessible an environment which fosters the inclusion and engagement of everyone, regardless of any individual differences. Embracing diversity and inclusion are our main priorities that can be found in the social impact that we seek with our service, the selection of our suppliers and the ownership of our company.

Inka Moss is a Peruvian social enterprise - awarded by the Dutch Bid Network in 2009 - that exports sphagnum moss in a sustainable and eco-friendly way. White moss (sphagnum moss) is a wild plant that grows naturally at more than 3,500 meters above sea level in the Peruvian Andes. The final product is 100% organic and has the capacity to absorb 20 times its weight in water. It's also a natural antibacterial and an efficient heavy metals absorbent. It's mostly used as substrate in horticulture, especially in orchid cultivation, but also has multiple other applications such as subtract for green walls, hydroponic crops, topiaries or as water purifier. There is a high international demand for white moss especially in Asia, Europe and America and Inka Moss currently possesses 2% of the market share. 
 
Inka Moss achieves its mission by creating high social impact and insuring responsible treatment of the environment in the highlands of Peru. Indeed, by involving, since 2009, Andean communities in situations of extreme poverty as the fundamental link of its value chain, the company has been building an empowering, sustainable and eco-friendly model of business.

Fraenck is a social & sustainable fashion accessory brand, founded in 2018. It started with two aspiring designers (Ho&Mulder) feeling responsibility for the impact of the things they brought into the world. When they graduated from the Artez Academy of the Arts they felt a disconnect between the inner workings of the fashion industry and the way they wanted to operate. Together they started working on bringing design, fashion and honesty together.

Both operational in the B2C and B2B market, Team Fraenck upcycles and recycles as many (textile) materials they can get their hands on. These are translated into a consumer collection, designed with and made from upcycled vegan leather and sailcloth (tarpaulin), but also a wholesale collection made for companies looking to recycle their own promotional materials, such as flags, banners, building facades and more. Their latest efforts include a collection of outdoor accessories made from discarded polyester tents and a range of items made from leftover textiles from Dutch trains.

Every single item is handcrafted in the social workshop of Fraenck in the city centre of Arnhem, The Netherlands. A core team of fashion professionals guide an ever expanding team of individuals looking to improve themselves and learn new skills everyday.

“Taiwan Blue Magpie Tea”/ “Leopard Cat Rice” is a social enterprise committed to the "River Basin Recovery” contract-farming plan.
"River Basin Recovery" is a model of agricultural and commercial integration, elevating the ecosystem to a brand together with local farmers. The key is to integration the whole catchment area. We are committed to the ''River Basin Recovery" strategy for the sake of "pesticide-free watershed" through environmentally friendly agriculture.
To promote the coexistence of ecology and agronomy, we produce various tea products in Pinling. Those are called "Taiwan Blue Magpie Tea". All of them rely on a 100% pesticide and fertilizer free growing method.
Under the concept of eco-friendly agriculture, we put all our "pesticide-free watershed" social enterprise efforts into promoting a beneficial coexistence of the leopard lats’ habitat and agronomy. To achieve this, the expansion of the habitat is a core element of our overall plan. By relying on environmental friendliness in farming, rather than pesticides or chemical fertilizers, we now grow the "Leopard Cat Rice".

Revolutionizing sexual health and wellness, GLYDE is the first certified ethical, vegan & fair trade premium condom brand. Crafted with patented technology and a clean plant-based formula, GLYDE delivers a more satisfying experience, while eliminating harmful additives, animal products and testing prevalent among conventional brands. Certifications include The Vegan Society, PETA’s Caring Consumer Program, Ethiquette and the Green Business Network. 

GLYDE sources its materials from worker owned and operated producers engaged in fair trade and labor practices, including paying workers far above a living wage. Their natural rubber is grown sustainably, indigenous to the region, and within close proximity to the manufacturing facility to minimize the company’s carbon footprint. GLYDE’s consumer packaging and printed materials are made with recycled materials, soy and vegetable inks. 

The first sexual health company founded on the principles of social engagement, since 1991 GLYDE has donated millions of condoms globally and is instrumental in advancing HIV/AIDS and STI prevention through partnerships with public health agencies and non-profit organizations including the Australian Health Ministry, the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Planned Parenthood and ACON.

Clients also come to them because they know they share their values.

Pala believes in creating a sustainable future for the good of humanity and the planet. As a brand driven by purpose, our mission is to produce high quality, long-lasting eyewear that minimises impact on the planet and maximises positive social on people. 

We work with small family run business in Italy to produce our sunglasses. We use the very best materials only used bio-acetate (100% biodegradable) for our frames and more eco-friendly lenses (39% renewable source). We are able to produce in small batches, avoiding issues around overstock and enabling us to be nimble and easy to collaborate with on custom collections.

Pala was founded on a mission ‘to see the world better’ encapsulating the B Corp values of a better outcome for ‘people and planet.’ We unite our sales to grants to vision centres, dispensaries and screening programmes across Africa totalling over £43,000 to date. 
We work with a Ghanaian NGO to support female weaving communities in Bolgatanga that make our unique recycled sunglasses cases. 

If you have any questions, then please do contact us - we would love to hear from you.

Harvest London is a vertical farming company seeking to transform our unsustainable food system. Food production contributes around a third of global greenhouse gas emissions, increasingly not just from farms themselves, but in activities like transport and processing. Agriculture is also a major contributor to waterway pollution, deforestation and soil degradation. The demand for fresh produce of all types, from across the globe, year-round, will only grow - the cosmopolitan tastes of consumers in developed countries impact the whole world. Harvest London is a specialist in using controlled environment technology to grow great-tasting food, right next to the final consumer.

Bruichladdich distillery is located on the southwestern tip of the remote Hebridean Island of Islay, where they distill four unique spirits.  Home to Bruichladdich, Port Charlotte and Octomore single malt whiskies and The Botanist Islay dry gin.

There are many attributes they share with their distant Gaelic forefathers: stubborn, resolute, self-sufficient, tough, hard-working, enduring, straight-talking, emotional, passionate, philosophical and engaging… perhaps with a certain roguish quality.  They are proudly nonconformist, as has always been the way in these Western Isles – Oirthir Gaidheal, the Coast of the Gaels, the land of the outsider. They passionately believe in terroir – in authenticity, place and provenance, in ultimate traceability. They seek to produce the most natural, thought-provoking, intellectually stimulating & enjoyable spirits possible. 

They believe in asking questions, in moving forward regardless of industry convention or the status quo. They continue to rebel against the staid world of Scotch whisky. They pioneer the foraging movement in gin. Confronting transparency, and reconnecting with nature.  This is not one distillery with one style of spirit; this is one project to break every boundary, to challenge every convention.
column10: Islay single malt whiskies and Islay dry gin.

OMBE is an integrative health center located Boston's Back Bay neighborhood. The eco-friendly center sits above the historic Copley Square area of Boston with beautiful views of the square and surrounding architecture. Services include acupuncture, chiropractic, massage, naturopathy, nutrition, personal training, physical therapy, Pilates, and yoga. Small group classes limited to six individuals ensure that each individual receives the one-to-one attention that they deserve. Classes include ballet barre, meditation, Pilates, and yoga. 



OMBE synergizes Western and Eastern medicine to develop comprehensive treatment plans for their clients. Their practitioners combine their expertise and compassion to help each client discover their unique mind-body balance.  Every year, the center reviews their green practices on Earth Day to improve OMBE's sustainability. OMBE is currently a member of One Percent for The Planet and continues to win awards for its green efforts.  The center only uses organic massage oils, PVC-free yoga mats, organic cotton linens, and is dedicated to being at the forefront of the green movement. Essential to their green approach is their Eco Beauty Bar featuring organic and local skin care lines, energy-neutral policies, and their efforts to recycle just about everything.  Being green is an integral part of their commitment to create a healthy environment for our guests.

Your experience at OMBE will empower you to achieve your best health, strength and well-being.

We’re just one of many small, locally-owned businesses in the Boston area. It’s important to us that our small business makes a difference.  We review our sustainable practices each year on Earth Day, but we feel that it is important to be evaluated by a third party so that we can continue to improve our sustainability and raise the bar.​

The Change We Seek	

OMBE recognizes that good health is directly connected to the air we breathe, the water we drink, and the food we eat. This is why OMBE is committed to integrative medicine and the environment. Through the dedicated work of their licensed practitioners, OMBE has been able to expand its health services and offer specialized programs in several areas such as sports medicine, pain management, fertility, prenatal care, and women's health. Their team collaborates to develop comprehensive treatment plans for their clients and offers the local community several free services and workshops throughout the year.  OMBE knows how important it is to find the right health care practitioner to help clients discover their best health.  They continue to work closely with other health care providers in the Boston area in an effort to integrate various forms of medical services for their patients.

A revolution in feeding little ones, NurturMe is the first and only family of certified-organic, dried fruit and veggie meals and snacks created for children 4 months to 4 years. The first “stage-free” food for little ones, NurturMe’s organic dry NurturMeals pouches and Yum-a-Roo’s dried fruit and veggie snacks help parents feed their babies better from the ground up – from infants to toddlers, and everywhere in between.

NurturMe organic dry meals and snacks are made from nutrient-packed super-foods including green kale, quinoa and squash (and many more) that are quick-dried in order to preserve freshness, flavor and vital phytochemicals. Designed for maximum versatility, NurturMeals can be mixed up with breast milk, formula or water to create the desired consistency, or mixed in to toddler favorites like pastas, baked goods or yoghurt for an added boost in protein and nutrients. NurturMe’s comprehensive family of products are certified organic, gluten-free (excluding the NurturMeals “Sweet Potatoes, Oatmeal and Bananas” flavor), non-GMO and kosher, with no added preservatives, sugars or salts – only the good stuff. 

Good for baby and Mother Earth, NurturMeal dry meal pouches weigh less than one ounce each and are packed using recyclable materials made with wind energy, leaving a smaller carbon footprint on our planet than the other options found in the baby aisle.  

We are, at the core, all about taking a modern approach in order to connect with and improve the wellbeing of a new generation of consumers (and future generations to come) – both through our organic family of products and dedication to social and environmental responsibility.  B Corporation represented to us the opportunity to align with other sustainable and mission-minded companies that are part of this paradigm shift and doing business differently, in order to create the community of brands that tomorrow’s consumers, and their parents, deserve.

 The Change We Seek™

NurturMe is dedicated to improving nutritional value for little ones by delivering honest, nourishing meals and snacks that promote overall wellness and support healthy growth. Founded in 2009 by mompreneur Caroline Freedman and her good friend, culinary expert Lauren McCullough, the idea behind NurturMe was born after Caroline had her first child and recognized the need for a more versatile, nutrient-rich and eco-friendly alternative to the traditional baby foods on the market. After spending two years consulting with organic farmers, health and medical experts, scientists, drum-drying experts, and eco-conscious packaging experts, the duo created the first and only certified-organic baby food made from nutrient-rich, quick-dried fruits and vegetables. 

Today NurturMe continues to revolutionize the baby food industry by providing nutrient-packed and versatile dry meals and snacks made from specially selected 100% organic super fruits and veggies that are grown in the U.S. and free of any harmful synthetic pesticides and fertilizers. From dry pouch meals that can be mixed with breast milk for even more nutrients with each feeding, to the first 100% quinoa alternative to rice cereals, to dry toddler snacks that deliver 1.5 servings of fruit AND veggies in each pouch, NurturMe strives to find innovative and sustainable ways to make it easy for busy, modern parents to ensure their little ones are getting the nutrients they need. From the soil to their spoon, each earth-loving, lightweight NurturMe pouch provides added convenience and peace of mind.

Atelier 10 est un projet multifacette qui a, au cœur de sa mission, la publication de textes originaux, soignés et susceptibles de nous permettre de mieux comprendre les enjeux de notre époque, de prendre part activement à la vie de notre société et de mener une vie plus signifiante et satisfaisante. Nous publions deux fois par année le magazine Nouveau Projet, de même que la collection d’essais Documents et la collection de textes dramatiques Pièces.

Nous avons choisi de devenir une B Corporation afin de nous astreindre aux plus hautes normes de transparence, de responsabilité sociale et de performance environnementale.

Atelier 10 is a multifaceted project which, at its heart, aims to publish original and well-crafted writings that can help people better understand the issues of our time, engage fully in society and lead a more meaningful and satisfying life. Twice a year, we publish Nouveau Projet Magazine, as well as the Documents short essays series and the Pièces drama series.

We wanted to become a B Corporation to help us meet the higher standards of social and environmental performance, transparency, and accountability. 

The Change We Seek	

Plus qu’une simple maison d’édition, Atelier 10 cherche à devenir un agent de changement social et culturel.

Ce changement passe d’abord par nos publications, qui ont pour mission de publier les meilleurs auteurs et journalistes, de soutenir les forces progressistes et novatrices sur les plans politique et artistique, et de contribuer à l’effervescence de la société québécoise et de la culture francophone en Amérique du Nord.

Mais nous cherchons également à faire en sorte que l’ensemble de nos actions soient posées dans l’intérêt de toutes les parties prenantes: public, employés et collaborateurs, fournisseurs, communauté locale, etc.

Au niveau environnemental, par exemple, nous faisons en sorte que toutes nos publications soient imprimées sur du papier recyclé et certifié FSC, ce qui assure que la production de celui-ci respecte les procédures garantissant la gestion durable des forêts.

Nous nous assurons aussi de payer nos collaborateurs de manière juste et équitable, et de leur offrir des contrats respectueux de leurs droits d’auteur et leur droit moral.

Nous cherchons par ailleurs à avoir un impact positif sur notre communauté locale, soit celle du Mile End, à Montréal. Des projets sont présentement en développement à ce niveau.

Pour nous, la certification B Corporation n’est que le début d’un long processus qui nous mènera vers une forme d’entreprise et un ensemble d’actions nous permettant de favoriser les progrès sociaux et culturels qui sont notre raison d’être.

Payton Communications delivers strategic public relations counsel, brand marketing solutions, philanthropic expertise, media relations, and editorial services to nonprofits, healthcare organizations, and socially responsible businesses. Its purpose is to help advance nonprofits and encourage corporate social responsibility. The Payton Communications team has combined experience in many business sectors including consumer health and safety, beauty, tech, retail, airline, and financial services. They have also worked with nonprofits that address environmental protection, children’s health and safety, public education, human services and disaster preparedness and response.


Payton Communications measures success for clients through increased public awareness, improved stakeholder engagement, increased revenue or other mutually agreed upon criteria. The firm embraces simplicity, brevity and clarity in all communication channels and avoids clichés, ambiguity, pretentiousness and jargon.


We embrace what the B Corp community stands for—a socially responsible way to do business. In addition to our mission to serve the public good, we are committed to working with local, independent practitioners and small businesses. We especially strive to work with women-owned, minority-owned and socially responsible businesses and believe that inclusiveness contributes to enhanced creativity, insight, teamwork and enthusiasm.





The Change We Seek®


Child drowning prevention is our corporate social responsibility (CSR) focus. In loving memory of Alicea Payton, the daughter of company founder, Beverly Payton, and sister to Charlotte Payton, Payton Communications will dedicate a percentage of its financial, intellectual and human capital to child drowning prevention. Alicea drowned in a neighbor’s unsecured swimming pool in May 1988, a week before her fourth birthday. In response to this tragedy, Beverly worked with the Drowning Prevention Foundation to pass a swimming pool barrier code in Pennsylvania. Both Beverly and Charlotte now serve as board officers for the Drowning Prevention Foundation. According to the CDC, drowning remains a leading cause of death to children ages 1-4. Payton Communications will help educate the public about water safety best practices and will work collaboratively with organizations focused on drowning prevention. We will provide steeply discounted fees and, when possible, pro bono consulting services to help achieve our shared mission.


Payton Communications takes seriously its responsibility to protect the Earth for future generations through environmental stewardship. The Payton Communications team is committed to recycling, repairing and reusing products as much as possible to reduce overall waste. 


As a virtual corporation, Payton Communications partners with service providers who work remotely, thus reducing its carbon footprint by eliminating the need for a daily commute. This also allows firm principals and associates to have a flexible work schedule to achieve a better work/life balance. The firm also seeks to work with fellow members of the B Corp community.

Aequilibria’s services range from the carbon footprint quantification of product and organization to the compliance with mandatory tools on climate change (e.g. EU ETS), to the development of targets (such as the submission of SBTI targets) and of strategies for GHG emissions mitigation.
Aequilibria supports organizations in the development and optimization of EMS, and it's also very active in the implementation of analyzes of materiality and in the drafting of sustainability reports.
Training is a further core activity of Aequilibria, combining asynchronous online training alongside normal face-to-face, catalogue or tailor-made courses for clients in various countries (e.g. Kazakhstan, South Korea, Cambodia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Colombia), through the use of a dedicated moodle platform.

A critical step to building circularity is increasing the value of recovered plastic which stimulates greater investment in collection and sortation, and pulls material currently lost to landfill, incineration and the environment back into the recycling stream.  Kamilo’s innovative technology platform responds to the need to improve the market value of recovered plastics and provide low cost, transparent and trusted techniques to measure, track, and verify the sustainable management of reusable resources. 
Kamilo’s system also quantifies the prevention of plastic pollution, the avoidance of greenhouse gases (GHGs) associated with fossil fuel production and the manufacturing of virgin plastic, and the space saved through the avoidance of landfilling.  Kamilo confirms that the facilities in their network meet minimum environmental stewardship criteria to qualify as a Kamilo partner; they track recovered plastic and validate Post-Consumer Resin (PCR) content in repurposed products; they provide increased value to recovered plastic while ensuring it does not pollute the environment; and they provide B2B GIS data-analytics to enable lowest-carbon transport emission matches between plastics supply and demand.

Beam Australia has broken up with the 40-hour work week. They believe employee impact should be measured on outcomes not time at a desk. Beam helps companies grow in two key ways. We unlock the most amazing, productive group of talent: part-time professionals. We also provide businesses with the tools to get flexible, increase employee wellbeing and prepare for the future of work.

Why Beam: Co-Founders Stephanie Reuss and Victoria Stuart left corporate careers to start Beam because they wanted to change the conversation around part-time. It was personal. When they became mums, because of big careers, they were forced to burn out or drop out of the workforce altogether. The obvious middle ground — part-time — wasn't an option because most businesses weren't doing it well or at all. 

The brain drain of amazing women at this stage of life is crazy and has enormous implications for women in leadership roles, superannuation, wellbeing and more. But Beam isn't just about mums. Lots of people can't work full-time even though they're still ambitious and super productive — parents, carers, athletes, those with portfolio careers, people starting businesses… 

Since 2016, Beam has helped add $13 million in new roles to the economy and topped up women’s superannuation by over $800,000.
column10: Where smart employers find high quality, hidden talent — powered by part-time.

When Wetherby was founded in 1990, the concept of independent investment advice was considered a novel proposition. The firm's founder, Deb Wetherby, wanted to create a new model that rewarded objectivity and results and eschewed the product and sales-driven culture present in most firms at that time. She made the decision to separate fees from investment recommendations, a novel idea that became the industry standard. Wetherby has no internal products and prides itself on offering objective investment advice to clients. 
 
Growth of the firm has been centered on the founding values of independence, objectivity and exceptional client service. These tenets were especially crucial in Wetherby's early embrace of impact investing, enabling the firm to be flexible and respond to client demand for investments that could align their portfolio with their values. Wetherby is dedicated to ensuring these founding principles remain part of the firm's culture into the future thus our owners periodically offers key employees the opportunity to become owners of the business.

Posits’s primary purpose is to create free and open-source software for data science, scientific research, and technical communication. This allows anyone with access to a computer to participate freely in a global economy that rewards data literacy; enhances the production and consumption of knowledge; and facilitates collaboration and reproducible research in science, education and industry.

To reliably contribute to the deeper understanding and improvement of the world, data science tools must be sustainable over the long haul, which requires a stable, long-term source of financial investment. Today, millions of people download and use Posit open-source products in their daily lives while thousands of organizations and individuals, who have the need and ability to pay for their commercial products on premises or online, help them to sustain this work. Together, these products form a virtuous cycle. The adoption of open-source data science software in organizations creates demand for our commercial products, which enable teams to adopt open-source data science software at scale. The revenue from our commercial products, in turn, enables ongoing investment in the open-source software that benefits all users.
column10: Free & open tools for R; enterprise software for R & Python data science teams

Fermenstation was established with the mission of creating a circular economic society by regenerating and upcycling unused resources through its original fermentation technology. Their unique production system creates zero waste, utilizes green energy, and does not use animal testing. It is also actively partnering with businesses that are looking to reuse their once industrial waste.  Beginning from food and beverage companies to importers of fruits, it has upcycled food waste into alcohol and fermented extracts, then to various cosmetic, aroma and homecare products.  Founded upon fermentation technology discovered and developed in Japan, Fermenstation is the supplier of clean beauty, organic, upcycled materials worldwide as well as develop its own Japan beauty brand. Chiesi Group is an international research-focused pharmaceuticals and healthcare group with over 85 years’ experience with more than 6,000 employees worldwide and a commercial presence in 100 countries. Dolphin Blue's business goal is to provide ecologically sustainable products for use in home and business. They are an on-line retailer of paper products, tableware, children’s toys, pet products, remanufactured toner cartridges, calendars, envelopes, garden products and much more. Their mission is: To serve as your trusted source of the world’s most environmentally and socially responsible products - to assure your well being and a healthy, sustainable planet.
 
Today, it is virtually impossible to tell the difference between virgin materials and quality post-consumer recycled materials. In order to make it onto Dolphin Blue's virtual "shelves," a product must be made of at least 20% post-consumer recycled materials and made in the USA. In addition, they favor products that come from sources that are certified for sustainability, particularly in their papers. 100% post-consumer recycled, Forest Stewardship Council certified, processed chlorine free, made carbon neutral or carbon plus with renewable energy - these are all characteristics that determine whether a product makes it into their online catalog.

Energylab is a dynamic consultancy specialising in sustainability and sustainable design. We have extensive experience in both design and management across a broad range of sectors where we aim to embrace circular economy principles and low energy design practices.

Our vision is to deliver efficient and flexible environments which are engineered to help people work in an sustainable, effective and collaborative way.

We have a proactive approach to spatial design and how building services integrate within the space. We offer our clients a high quality service by working closely with them and their team to achieve a successful end product which meets the ESG agenda.

We believe the building services elements of the workplace are often not considered at the outset, yet they are fundamental to the successful functionality and operation of space. Too often standard solutions are offered, which then need to be ‘force-fitted’ into a space which is already designed. The results can mean a dysfunctional work space with high operating and energy costs.

Energylab want to change that way of working by providing a more strategic and integrated approach to workplace design.

column7:
The Bark House at Highland Craftsmen Inc	 handcrafts beautiful wall coverings for interior and exterior design solutions. Made from reclaimed tree bark, our products express our rich heritage of artisanal craftsmanship and form an authentic connection between nature, individuals, and the built environment.

Our highest-quality standard is built upon three key elements: process, product, and purpose. At the culmination of these elements, fine craftsmanship is uniquely combined with certified sustainable manufacturing processes. While our richly textured wall coverings adorn a selection of America’s most sought after real-estate, the core purpose of our company involves more than creating beautiful buildings; it is also about building community beautifully. Assurance rests in the fact that we are the original designers and crafters of every bark product we sell. We created this niche industry and have a 25 year history behind us. Bark House	 is proud to have earned the only Cradle to Cradle™ Gold Product Certification for siding. This third-party certification verifies our commitment to providing sustainable products that are safe for humans, the environment, and future life cycles. We are an awarded “Legacy C2C Company”.

We became a B Corp because the structure helps us to communicate a strong, verified message about who we are. This certification makes our performance standards transparent so that our clients retain the "Power of Their Purchase™" and can “Invest with Impact™”.

The Change We Seek	

Highland Craftsmen was co-founded in 1990 by North Carolina natives, Marty and Christie McCurry. Inspired by nature’s design, our work celebrates RAW™ (Reclaimed Appalachian Wood Waste) materials. With a new industry, jobs were created in an economically challenged region of the Appalachians that fit both the culture and the economy of this community, and we take pride in knowing that what we do has a low impact on the environment. Highland Craftsmen Inc has earned a rare spot on the B Corp Best for the World List. With a methodology that celebrates pure nature, we look forward to many more years of striving for positive social and environmental impact while continuing to hand-craft the finest architectural products for our discerning clients worldwide. The Bark House	 brand verifies authenticity and can help “find your pristine nature within”:We honor the environment through thoughtful management, procurement, and refinementWe honor people by maintaining a proud heritage of quality workmanship, by providing training and methods for growthWe build prosperity in our community by creating new income streams, paying a living wage and giving back

Citizenfund is a cooperative and impact investment fund. Any citizen or company can invest a little bit of its money in the fund. With these amounts, we finance companies that have a positive impact on society.
It is the cooperators (shareholders) of the Citizenfund who choose the social businesses that the fund finances, after meeting the entrepreneurs.
Citizenfund operates according to the cooperative governance principle of "1 person = 1 vote". Each member has the same voting power, regardless of the type of share and the amount invested, for both investment decisions and internal governance.
Citizenfund uses finance as a virtuous instrument to bring about the positive changes that society needs.
Already 235 cooperators invested over 500.000 € in the Citizenfund. 23 social businesses were funded since the creation of the fund.

Positive Impact Law Group is a boutique law firm for social entrepreneurs that was founded in 2010 and is based in Toronto. PILG appreciates their clients’ uniquely valuable role in society and is committed to guiding their clients through every stage of growth and risk as they build a profitable blended value company without compromising their social purpose. PILG’s legal services and legal counsel is predicated on the understanding that legal frameworks for businesses are fundamentally about creating, developing and managing internal and external relationships. PILG understands that social entrepreneurs and blended-value businesses naturally have a greater desire for congruency between their business purpose(s) and how their businesses operate. This desire for congruency can create a greater business risk where new business relationships are formed from within the conventional legal methodology. PILG creates a positive impact that ensures and upholds their client’s authenticity by applying a holistic and innovative approach to balance purpose and profit.


We became a B Corp because we know there is power in the fusion of business and social purpose to create sustainable, positive effects in the lives of people locally and the larger world community. Part of our mission is to provide support to these unique businesses, and it only felt natural to subscribe to B Corp’s ongoing assessment standards because they are based on values that we adhere to.


PILG’s client-centric and forward-thinking business structure is guided by the belief that their clients, regardless of business development stage, require access to the support they need to operate with confidence. Technology, a network of experienced legal professionals and values-driven pricing models are among the ways PILG has created energy and cost-efficiencies; and their clients benefit from the peace of mind that comes with knowing that high value legal support is feasible.
The Change We Seek®


The Change We Seek is for For-Profit social enterprises to have structural and operational barriers diminished to enable their full potential to be realized.


The Change We Seek is for businesses to have the option to be structurally supported to pursue profit and positive impact in a sustainable and scalable manner. To that end, we welcome statutory legal recognition that profit and positive stakeholder impact are not mutually-exclusive concepts and that they can purposefully co-exist within the constitution of a business.


The Change We Seek is for businesses to have congruency between their blended-value corporate DNA and their operational legal frameworks. It's one thing for a business' corporate DNA to be values-based; it is another, more empowering idea for the DNA to be carried through the business' blood streams.

Established in 1996, Deep Ecology is a full-service, five-star PADI Dive Center located on Oahu's famous North Shore in historic Haleiwa.  Their history includes ghost net recoveries and over 50 endangered Green Sea Turtle rescues, which resulted in the creation of the North Shore's first marine sanctuary.  They're committed to providing their divers with top notch dive locations.  They are also a National Geographic recognized diver center, offering a specialty course designed to train their customers to become skilled divers and naturalists.  

We were a social enterprise before even knowing the term; intuitively we knew that ethical business held great capacity for positive change.  Over the years we have seen this intuition grow into a movement and becoming a B Corporation is like coming home.   

Whether you are just starting out or acquiring new training, their instructors will guide you in a unique and special experience.  From the first cautious breath during a Discover Scuba Dive or the exploration of a shipwreck during Advanced and Specialty training, they will provide the best training possible to keep you diving, learning and exploring.  The Change We Seek®  

They envision the day where every dive operation uses the resources inherent in such businesses to give back as they have done.  Having led by example, they are preparing for the logical step of expanding and possibly franchising their business model to accelerate and achieve this goal.  

• Protecting the marine environment has been a passion and focus for Deep Ecology. Through their initiatives, and with the cooperation of the North Shore community, a marine sanctuary was created at Sharks Cove to protect all sea life. They have rescued over fifty Green Sea Turtles, trapped by fishing line or debris. When they see an injured or trapped turtle, they act immediately to help that creature. They work actively to protect marine life from entrapment in abandoned fishing nets, and to clear the ocean of other debris. Through dives and regular beach clean ups, they have collected over 5 tons of debris. Whenever they are in a position to reduce human impact on marine life they will, so long as it does not compromise their divers' safety. Their record is impeccable.

Founded in Canada in 1986, Mondetta – which combines the French word ‘monde’ (world) with the Latin suffix ‘etta’ (small) – was created with the ambitious goal to harmonize the globe. Developing simple yet sophisticated sportswear with unique flag-bearing sweatshirts, the brand skyrocketed to success creating ‘A Spirt of Unification’, selling clothing and uniting people around the world.
 
Mondetta has evolved from a sportswear brand to a global leader in sustainable, technical lifestyle and activewear. The Company has grown exponentially and today has 3 divisions: direct-to-consumer, wholesale and private label, and maintains a vast supply chain comprised of facilities spanning 13 countries. Despite its growth and success, Mondetta has remained committed to its core values: high-quality product, value and accessibility, ethical business practices and continuous evolution, and is dedicated to reaching the highest level of social, economic and environmental responsibility by constantly improving its business model to reduce its environmental footprint and implement socially responsible practices
 
In 2004 the Mondetta Charity Foundation was established as a means to give back. The Foundation supports a school in Africa, an orphanage in Kenya and charitable causes in North America.

Twirl is an adventurous, spirited event planning boutique that specializes in crafting and curating human experience with creativity, care and conscience. Twirl designs mind-blowing creative experiences that care for their clients and the collective. And have a really good time in the process.

Their philosophy is simple: Everything about events can be outrageously fun, unforgettable AND ecologically conscious when you plan them with creative sustainability, a process that goes beyond environmental to explore the notion of universal happiness and well-being. Twirl believes fiercely that enriched quality of food and goods and localization of capital make events better for you and the world. They honestly just care. And they love a good party.

Twirl plans great, gorgeous, good for people and the planet events – from idea generation to conscious cleanup: Anything with a guest list and attendees – Corporate & Social Affairs, Conferences, Meetings, Incentives, Retreats, Roadshows, Pop-ups, Special Events, Weddings, Galas, Festivals, Concerts, Fashion Shows, Employee Appreciation and on and on.

Twirl has operated like a B Corp since it incorporated in 2007. Becoming a B Corp 6 years later was a way to illustrate to our stakeholders that our business operations aligned with a growing movement of business to benefit not just the client or the bottom line but the world in which they operate. 

The Change We Seek	

Twirl's hope is to spread their practices of infusing care for people and the environment into events as far and wide as possible. They want to transform the event industry into one that’s about more than just a good party; but about concern for footprint and our collective interdependence. The more people who make their events sustainable, the better.

KINeSYS Inc. is a pioneer in the skin care and sun protection industry. As creator of the first oil, alcohol, PABA, preservative and paraben-free spray sunscreens, with topical anti-oxident Vitamin E to scavenge free radicals, KINeSYS has been instrumental in changing the way sunscreen is applied since 1994. Today, KINeSYS is best known as a company that manufactures, markets, and promotes a premium line of award-winning sustainable sun protection products for the active family.

KINeSYS Inc. became a B Corporation after learning more about their mission and was pleased to find that ethics are still alive and well in America. The truths held to be self-evident by B Corporations are not yet self-evident to all and we hope to be part of the next industrial revolution that enlightens the masses. We believe good ethics are good business.

KINeSYS is a leader in their community with their practices, support and actions. They believe they have demonstrated that it is possible to be commercially viable by making ethical manufacturing choices. In addition, they have become a driver in their industry to push for more local manufacturing, sustainable and reduced packaging and less impactful logistical choices. In the long run, they strive to create products that protect health but do so at no net cost to our planet or our quality of life. They aim to enrich the lives of their users, their retailers, their  stakeholders and their neighbors. This is the KINeSYS Ecosystem and the basis of their triple bottom line. They will lead by example, not hyperbole and inspire others to follow.

The Change We Seek	

KINeSYS was founded with one overriding goal – to protect the health of active families (our mission). We have come to understand that this requires more than just making products of the highest quality. It requires ‘holistic’ thinking and the realization that our actions on every level have immediate and significant ripple effects now and in the future. This means showing due consideration for how we make products and how we sell products.

We are proud of our environmental stewardship since inception in 1994, using 100% recyclable packaging, manual powered sprayers, post recycled shipping boxes, and brochures.

KINeSYS is a carbon neutral manufacturer, purchasing carbon offsets for all the energy used during production, at our offices and for our vehicles.

For twenty years Topical BioMedics, Inc., has established itself as the R&D leader of topical natural cellular biomedicines for relieving pain by enhancing and supporting the body’s ability to heal the damage that is causing the pain.  The company’s founder, Lou Paradise—an accomplished physiology and natural medicines researcher—was inspired to develop Topical BioMedics’ flagship patented pain relief and healing technology, Topricin, initially as a means to treat the war injuries he endured from the physical demands of serving as a decorated helicopter combat medevac crew chief in the U.S. Marine Corps in the republic of Vietnam. Mr. Paradise is a man on a mission determined to end physical suffering and reverse the devastation of Rx opioid addiction for everyone who is afflicted.  He is a recognized pain management expert and thought leader having created what has been designated as a “21st century approach to pain relief,” and discusses how to build and support a sustainable healthcare model.     

Topricin has earned a sterling reputation for providing robust health benefits that include reducing need/dependency for all classifications of oral pain medication, an important contribution with addiction to Rx opioid medications being at epidemic levels in the U.S.  Topricin uses a patented synergized combination of homeopathic biomedicines and a proprietary system to deliver the medicines at the cellular level. The products contain no petroleum, parabens, volatile oils, fragrances, or irritating chemicals. The formulas have no known side effects, are ideal for the entire family and those with diabetes, as well as supporting a healthy, active lifestyle. In 2009 Topricin products were awarded a patent for the topical treatment of pain associated with neuropathy and fibromyalgia. As well as representing a breakthrough healing technology, Topricin used both before and after surgery is known for reducing the time of recovery of post-surgical trauma—an important benefit to reduce the use of opioid pain pills and the risk of addiction. All Topricin products are made in the U.S.A., formulated with approved medicines as found in the HPUS (Homeopathic Pharmacopoeia of the United States). All products are in compliance with federal rules for homeopathic over-the-counter medicines.  Topricin is available in pharmacies, natural food/supplement stores, specialty retailers, and other fine retailers nationwide. The company offers affordability programs to seniors and people economically challenged, which includes individuals with disabilities and our nation’s military veterans.      

Topical BioMedics provides the highest ethical standards and product solutions for changing how pain is diagnosed and treated and delivers superior treatment protocols to doctors and their patients, which have materially contributed to the company’s goal of reversing and preventing addiction to Rx pain pills. By doing so, it has established a cornerstone in patient-centered outcomes and opened up the discussion of building a sustainable wellness healthcare model.  



The legacy we want for our nation and the people and children of the world is for every single one of us to have the opportunity to live a robust, healthy, joyous life that honors our interrelationship and fosters the spirit of taking care of each other. 

We became a B-Corp to be a part of a robust community dedicated to help solve the serious issues we’re facing, including the state of our economy, the effects of climate change, healthcare (or lack thereof) and the epidemic of addiction to Rx pain pills, all of which have torn at the very fabric of society.  

Solving these and other pressing global problems are crucial, and require all likeminded entities to join together to truly B-the Change.  The Change We Seek	

Topical BioMedics, Inc., through the Topricin pain relief and healing project, is dedicated to educationally empowering doctors, patients and their families with a clear understanding of how to look at what pain truly is:  a vital signal from the body alerting us to the fact that there are damaged or inflamed muscles, joint, or nerve cells it wants to fix, and it needs some help to balance its natural healing chemistries. This awareness provides a clear, sustainable pathway to safer, more effective treatment options that promote lasting results.  

Unresolved chronic pain impacts us financially, physically, and emotionally while contributing to the massive epidemic of addiction to opioid pain pills, thus stressing both personal and professional relationships while undermining the fabric of society.  In the workplace, the cost of pain and suffering for the individual as well as the employer is staggering, into the hundreds of billions of dollars.      

The unique nature of Topical BioMedics’ work and depth of experience offer a solid thought-leader platform, providing products representing viable solutions balanced with educational components that doctors, patients, and employers can use and share to unravel the many factors that have contributed to the massive problems created by pain and addiction.  

The Topricin project provides a discussion platform for all stakeholders to understand key components that enable the nation and the world to move from a sick-care model to a robust and sustainable prevention and wellness healthcare model. The company’s contributions and activities have transformed the landscape of how pain is diagnosed and treated and enhanced the relationship between doctors and their patients.  By offering smart, innovative tools, and demonstrating the sincere compassion to help, Topical BioMedics has attracted entire communities in winning the battles to overcome doubt, confusion, and fear with knowledge and solutions that can be readily applied, thus returning dignity, sanity, hope and quality of life to individuals. 

Topical BioMedics is dedicated to fighting for the right of everyone who suffers to have the safe, effective options they need. The company’s commitment is to reverse the devastating effects that all pain pills have on society and ultimately solve this pressing issue with viable, vibrant, sustainable solutions and partnering with communities that will further this cause.  It is the birthright of every person on the planet to experience the joy of physical life; doing the things they love with the people they love...And Topical BioMedics believes this goal is ultimately attainable.

ProtoTest tests web and mobile apps to ensure functionality, performance, usability and accessibility. Their lab is staffed with experts and equipped with a great variety of devices, including all the leading smartphones and tablets. They test on all browsers, against dynamic content, responsive sites, mobile sites and apps; you name it, they've tested it.  Their clients include product, development and test managers from many industries including healthcare, information technology, financial, e-retail, and energy.

Unlike some Certified B Corps, ProtoTest did not have sustainability in its DNA when we founded the company in 1998. But along the way leadership and employees became better informed about the social and environmental challenges our world faces, and about the potential role of business in solving those challenges. We could find no better tool than the B Impact Assessment for driving our efforts to transform, and for validating our actions as meaningful.The Change We Seek	

At ProtoTest, our software dream is a world without bugs. Our business dream is a world where success means caring for all stakeholders, including those without a voice. Every interaction is an opportunity to share our dreams and invite others to dream with us.

Origin Climate's projects help businesses and individuals reduce their greenhouse gas emissions and fight climate change by generating renewable energy and destroying greenhouse gases (GHGs). Since 2005 Origin Climate's projects have destroyed over 5 billion pounds of CO2e and helped put enough renewable electricity on the grid to power 75,000 homes for a year.

At Origin Climate we believe that corporations can be a driving force in fighting climate change. We also believe that social and environmental stewardship is good for business in the long term. Being a B Corp allows us to lead by example and measure our success by metrics other than short term profits.

For Businesses: Origin Climate provides better, smarter sustainable energy solutions for companies. Origin Climate helps corporations and other institutions identify, assess, finance and implement projects across a full range of technologies, such as biogas, solar, wind, hydro and geothermal. Origin Climate powers business with the best and smartest renewable energy available.

For Individuals: Origin Climate helps individuals measure and reduce their carbon footprints with a comprehensive carbon footprint calculator and carbon offsets. All carbon offsets come from projects located in the U.S. and support local communities by creating jobs and reducing air pollution and groundwater contamination. Now that’s a breath of fresh air.The Change We Seek	

Origin Climate believes that everyone can take action to fight climate change. There is a better way to power the world. Origin Climate is seeking to help businesses and individuals reduce their carbon footprints through projects that destroy greenhouse gases, generate renewable energy and benefit small communities throughout the U.S.

Hawaiian Legacy Hardwoods (HLH) has found a way to occupy the sweet spot where “doing good” meets “doing well” by planting rare high value endemic koa trees on Hawaii Island. Some trees are planted for investors for eventual harvest, while others—“Legacy Trees”—are planted to permanently reforest the land, sequester carbon, advance science and inspire environmental awareness. The “For Harvest” model has many supporters, and for good reason.
 
What people may not realize, however, is that the economic benefit to society by not harvesting the tree is just as compelling. Over a 50-year lifetime, one single tree generates $31,250 worth of oxygen, provides $62,000 worth of air pollution control, recycles $37,500 worth of water, and controls $31,250 worth of soil erosion. Furthermore, each tree is equipped with a proprietary state-of-the-art RFID geo-tagging system, which electronically tracks each individual tree in the forest.
 
HLH has been actively building strategic alliances with green minded companies and associations to further the cause of the koa restoration project. With these organizations, HLH has planted more than 200,000 trees in just four short years. In addition, their Legacy Tree sponsorship program supports more than 240 charities worldwide.

Hives for Lives, a honey company, was started six years ago by Molly and Carly when they lost their grandfather to cancer. He was 63 -- they were 9 and 11. The kids raise honeybees and sell the honey at local events, fairs, and retail stores like bakeries, kitchen stores, and grocery stores. The company is entirely kid-run. The VP of Marketing, COO, CFO, and VP of Sales are all under eighteen.


We believe that B Corps will very soon be a recognized indication to customers of not only a good product but also of a good company doing well in the world, and we want to be a part of that. Hives for Lives and B Corporations represent a world in which business is conducted as if people mattered.


Hives for Lives donates 100% of its profits to cancer research centers all over the country to help find a cure. Hives for Lives is both a local and national company, selling honey from the kids' own beehives locally and the honey of their partner beekeepers in Whole Foods nationwide. Profits made through Whole Foods sales in regions other than their own are donated to other regional cancer centers with a program called "Local Honey / Local Money," which focuses on building local communities.
The Change We Seek®


Their motto is very similar to B Corps': "Bee the Cure We Seek," and they try to live this every day. The mission of Hives for Lives has been to beat cancer with our business -- one jar of honey at a time.


Almost all of the work in the Hives for Lives company is done by student volunteers who receive no compensation for their time. These volunteers are primarily middle school and high school kids they call Helper Bees who donate their time and expertise in any number of ways: painting and building hives, tending bees, bottling honey, selling honey, managing the books and marketing, and attending presentations and meetings. .


With our Local Money/Local Honey program, profits from the sales of honey in each region stay in the region and go to regional but nationally renowned cancer research centers and hospitals. Places like St. Jude's, the Mayo Clinic, MD Anderson, Stanford Hospital, and the Abramson Center at University of Pennsylvania, among many others have all received profits from the sale of Hives for Lives honey in their region.

EKO is a specialized investment firm focused on discovering and monetizing unrealized or unrecognized environmental assets. They do this by matching smart capital with people, projects, and companies that are poised to profit from new and emerging environmental markets (markets for carbon, water, and biodiversity). In doing so, EKO hopes not only to harness the power of capital markets and help allocate resources to their "highest and best" ecological use, but also to help preserve ecosystems for future generations. EKO is, in short, a "merchant bank" for the world of environmental markets.

EKO seeks to stimulate the development of environmental markets by providing capital and market intelligence to the best projects and people in the field. Their focus is on "green" environmental assets (i.e. land-based carbon and forestry carbon rather than industrial emissions reductions, and wetland mitigation banking/conservation banking rather than pollution abatement technologies).

We became a B Corporation because we want to be held accountable to higher standards. EKO prides itself on being an organization that values people and place, not just profits. We hope to inspire others to do the same.The Change We Seek™

We seek to protect the environment by investing in market-based strategies for doing so. Threats to global biodiversity and global warming are key challenges facing the world today. We believe that market-based approaches have the potential to constructively effect how organizations and individuals approach the environment.

• EKO invests in the environment in many different ways including: land with undeveloped or unrecognized environmental assets; the development of credits destined for environmental markets derived from land-based assets (e.g. carbon credits from avoided deforestation projects in developing countries); companies that are poised to profit from these emerging markets (e.g. carbon project developers, mitigation bankers, etc.). In addition, we sometimes structure joint ventures and special purpose vehicles for investment in environmental assets, credits, or companies in the environmental market space.

• By providing our clients with many different opportunities for impact investing and creating tangible social impact, we stand out as a profitable and powerful asset management firm that creates both financial and social returns.

Kuflink Ltd owns and manages the peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platform and is authorised as an operator
of an electronic lending system and to hold client money under CASS 7 rules. It acts as a financial
intermediary; matching individual lenders with borrowers in the property lending sector that are seeking
capital in the form of short-term bridging finance facilities, conducted in accordance with the framework in
Article 36H of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Regulated Activities) Order 2001. Corporate
lenders enter into a corporate lender agreement on the platform. For the service of P2P platform funding,
Kuflink Ltd receives an agreed income from Kuflink Bridging Ltd.
Kuflink Bridging Ltd is authorised to carry out credit broking, debt administration and collection. The loans
that are originated by Kuflink Bridging Ltd are then matched to P2P lenders on the platform and Kuflink
Bridging takes up to 5% exposure which both evidence ‘skin in the game’ and acts as a first loss piece for
any impairments on the underlying loan.

Since 1994, Old Town Glassworks (formerly Yellowknife Glass Recyclers) has produced and sold top-quality northern glassware featuring original designs and recycled materials. The product is highly regarded and of excellent quality. Created by Matthew Grogono, the company came into existence attempting to find a way to transform unwanted glass bottles from the Yellowknife waste stream into useful decorative glassware. Operating from a small building located in the “Old Town” Yellowknife, the business evolved a method of creating drinking glasses, bowls, vases, candle holders and other assorted glassware from the unwanted bottles. Each piece of glassware is fully finished, handcrafted and etched with original northern designs.

The staple product of the business is drinking glasses in a variety of sizes and colours. Bowls, lamps, vases, candle holders, guitar slides, and soap pump bottles are also produced and are popular – as well as awards, custom engraving and corporate or event orders. The product and the company achieved recognition in the market place and gathered renown as an iconic northern product.

Because of Yellowknife's status as a tourist and visitor’s destination, and transient northern population, glassware from OTG can be found across Canada and around the world.  The busy giftshop is open everyday and fun, glassware workshops are also offered everyday to groups of 2-10 people where they can make a one-of-a-kind eco-friendly souvenir or gift. Product may be ordered from the companies website and they ship worldwide.

Becoming a B Corporation is another step in Old Town Glassworks being leaders in recycling in our community.  At a time when marketing efforts often “greenwash” anything remotely environmentally friendly, we wanted to measure and prove that our company is sustainable and good for the environment, our customers and our employees.  The certification process has shown us areas where we can continue to improve and will help shape our company and activates in the future.

The Change We Seek	

The increasingly disposable economy was the catalyst for the birth of Old Town Glassworks. The trend toward “throwing away and getting new”, is not sustainable, cannot continue and means profits at the expense of our planet. Old Town Glassworks has proven that you can make a successful business out of making beautiful things from unwanted trash. You can employ people and share the fun and importance of recycling. OTG offers a green alternative for corporate promotional products and given the choice, businesses, governments, and organizations, will choose green.  They need more innovative, recycling business ideas to divert raw material from the waste stream. It does work!
