Fiddleheads Health & Nutrition is proud to be the trusted source for health and wellbeing in their community. Celebrating 15 years in business in 2014, Kim Boril and Jenn Arsenault have expanded through the Kitchener – Waterloo Area while maintaining the passion and integrity that brought them to this industry years ago. From one small health food store in 1999 to 4 locations which provide supplements, grocery, smoothie bar cafes, educational seminars, yoga & meditation classes, as well as recently opening the True Wellness Integrative Health Centre by Fiddleheads, Kim & Jenn prove their ambition to be leaders in the Natural Health Industry. 



Fiddleheads Health & Nutrition gives back to the community by hosting free natural health seminars, customer appreciation events, and supporting local charities and programs that give back to people and planet. The Fiddleheads Smoothie Bar Cafés source organic, local produce and makes a point of recycling and composting when ever possible. They source compostable cups and packaging and power their stores with 100% renewable energy.



Fiddleheads Health & Nutrition is determined to source effective and innovative products with a focus on whole food and non-GMO ingredients. Their passion to inspire health and positivity is exemplified in their knowledgeable & dedicated staff members who feel proud to work for a company that support a nourishing work environment. As an ongoing initiative, Fiddleheads Health & Nutrition is committed to being a valued resource for healthy families everywhere. 



Our B Corp certification allows us to “tell our story” and shines light on all of the actions we take to contribute to our community, our employees, and to the planet. B Corp certification also challenges us to take our commitment to the next level by implementing new strategies, such as switching all of our locations to 100% renewable energy through Bullfrog Power. Becoming a B Corp has opened us up to an incredible community through which ideas and innovations are shared openly for the betterment of all parties involved, making us proud to be an integrative part of the journey towards the new economy.

The Change We Seek	



Fiddleheads Health & Nutrition is committed to being environmentally conscious. They believe that it is everyone’s individual responsibility to be accountable for the impact they have on our planet and that we are responsible for making our impact as negligible as possible. Fiddleheads has implemented numerous initiatives to reduce their impact, from sourcing local, organic produce for their kitchen, to implementing recycling programs where they did not exist before, to most recently switching to 100% renewable energy. Furthermore, they are continuously measuring their impact and looking for innovative ways to further reduce their footprint on the environment.



As well as being environmentally conscious, Fiddleheads Health & Nutrition is dedicated to making a difference in the life of each customer who walks through their doors by providing the resources needed to achieve overall wellness. Fiddleheads truly believes in the power of whole foods and are committed to providing non-GMO, whole food options to nourish their consumers. Through their full support of the non-GMO movement, they provide a safe haven for consumers who are conscious of the effects GMOs have on their health as well as on the environment. 



Finally, Fiddleheads has a passion for education and fully utilizes their large conference space to host educational sessions, yoga classes, and meditation classes. They believe that education is indispensable and that as consumers are educated about things like GMOs, alternative medicines, and B Corporations, they are given the power to make the choices that can ultimately lead them to true wellness.

SMART Watering Systems is a water efficiency consulting firm and a "hands on" irrigation water management company that works with municipalities, parks departments, architects and property managers to reduce potable water use on landscapes. SWS measures, manages and monitors it's clients water use through technology that enables leak detection, water use reporting and weather based schedule adjustment using weather information from it's private, dedicated weather network. SWS offers water auditing, irrigation upgrades, irrigation system monitoring, rain water system design and irrigation design services that help clients identify and act on water saving opportunities.

SMART Watering Systems acts on a simple philosophy. "If we are going to continue to use potable water on our landscapes, we must make every effort to use it responsibly". This means we must identify and eliminate waste and also move towards alternative water sources as the true value of our water resources is realized. SWS believes that a truly sustainable business contributes positively to the global marketplace not just through business but through leadership and by encouraging others to think critically about their staff and operations. SWS became a B Corp to demonstrate to our clients and staff that we are not only committed to their sustainable water use, we also want to ensure that how we run our business is sustainable as well.

The Change We Seek	

We hope that through our leadership, other organizations will be proactive in looking at their business impact as well as "water footprint"" and investigate ways to reduce it. We hope that globally, there is an increased focus on sustainable business and that water is a resource that we all start to think differently about. While it may be abundant for some of us, it is also finite and a key economic driver for all of us.

Little Duck Organics is an organic food company with a mission to provide families with fun, healthy snacks & meals for kiddos of all ages. Started by Zak Normandin in 2010, Little Duck Organics launched with the first complete line of non-GMO project verified, organic snacks for kids, containing no added sugar and only 100% fruit. Tiny Fruits is available in four tasty blends: Blueberry & Apple, Strawberry & Mango, Apple & Banana and new for Summer 2012 Pineapple & Mango.  Within two short years, the Tiny Fruits line continues increase distribution – with products available in over 4,000 retailers in the U.S. and Canada.  

Little Duck Organics became a B Corp because it is committed to creating the highest quality organic food products for kids, striving to support fair trade initiatives and foster lasting relationships with local and developing farm communities.     The Change We Seek®  

Little Duck Organics is genuinely committed to creating products that are nutritious, non-GMO project verified, kosher, and gluten free.  Additionally, Little Duck prides itself on the commitment to produce products the way nature intended -- free from added sugars, preservatives or additives.  

Little Duck Organics works directly with farming communities where ingredients are sourced, in an effort to establish a reliable and loyal supply chain. Through a  partnership with 1% for Humanity a portion of annual revenue is dedicated to social and humanitarian efforts in these regions.  

In addition to establishing a steadfast and ethical supply chain, Little Duck Organics partners with likeminded and socially responsible organizations within local and regional communities in an effort to promote and foster good will and social leadership.

The Pachamama Coffee Cooperative of Small-Scale Coffee Producers (Pacha) is the most direct way to buy coffee from organic farmers around the world. Pacha, the leading farmer-owned distributor of premium coffee in the U.S.A., is cooperatively owned by thousands of farmers in Ethiopia, Nicaragua, Guatemala, Mexico and Peru. A unique social enterprise, the cooperative markets and distributes its members' best coffee under these Farmer-Owned brands: Pacha Coffee, CoffeeCSA, and Traceable Coffee. Pacha is 100% farmer-owned and democratically governed.


Pacha was founded in 2001 by leading farmer-owned coffee cooperatives in Peru (COCLA) and Nicaragua (PRODECOOP) -- in an effort improve the lives of coffee farmers by shortening an inefficient supply chain and connecting farmers and consumers directly. Pacha has worked closely with businesses, non-profits, certifiers and sustainability organizations since its founding. Pacha supports the B Corporation community's aspiration to raise the bar through better business practices.




 
The Change We Seek™







Pacha is a global cooperative that embraces the power of commerce to improve the lives small-scale coffee farmers around the world by connecting them directly with the end-consumers of their coffee. Pacha seeks more efficient global supply chains with greater producer ownership of branding and distribution.

Feelgoodz LLC is a triple bottom line company that markets and distributes natural footwear.  Their flagship product, Feelgoodz, are the world's most comfortable flip-flops.    Made from 5L steamed latex in Thailand, their product uses 70% more rubber than any other brand on the market. In addition to being dyed naturally, the product is recyclable and biodegradable.


As a social enterprise, it is vital that our business's core values remain true as we facilitate growth. It is also important to educate consumers on ways to build a responsible company. We wanted to become a B Corporation to ensure that our values remain intact and that we spread this new kind of business to the world.





Feelgoodz's retail at $19.99, and their distribution strategy is to target the ever-growing and progressive socially responsible, eco-conscious market.  They have partnered with organizations such as Ashoka, Pencils of Promise, TransFair USA, and UniquEco-Designs.  They run flip-flop upcycling campaigns, education campaigns, and eco-tourism adventures.
The Change We Seek®


Feelgoodz seeks to become a global leader in conscious capitalism through sales of all natural, ethically sourced, comfortable footwear and through partnerships with value-aligned organizations.


• Feelgoodz is committed to creating a sustainable business, and we believe in steppin' easy as we walk the Earth. We use biodegradable natural rubber. We use recycled paper and recycled flop hangers. We're not environmentalists, but we're doing our part. And our contribution of 1% for the Planet enables us to support environmental organizations worldwide.


• We are started this business with a ground-level ethos of treating your entire supply chain, from farm to flop, with responsibility, ethics, and consciousness. We use the Materials Economy to guide our business decisions.


• We believe in a zero flip-flop waste world. We believe every child deserves a high-class education. We believe we shape ourselves through travel. And we believe in steppin' easy while we do it!

We qualified for years to be a b corp and are proud to have finally made it official!

B Revolution, Inc. builds the social enterprise and sustainable business revolution through four innovative ventures:


B Revolution Consulting provides turnkey startup and transitioning-entity services for social entrepreneurs, sustainable business owners, and nonprofit organizations seeking to utilize the B Corporation certification and legal structure. B Revolution Consulting specializes in optimizing profit-impact synergy by forming, planning, and capitalizing social enterprises, and helping those ventures develop an integrated strategy to scale for both profit and impact. B Revolution Consulting offers a unique, collaborative approach to consulting relationships, delving deep into the management team and operations of the venture to create lasting and impactful solutions.


B Revolution Capital is a network of mission-aligned early-stage investors which funds and mentors exclusively B Corporation startups for growth in profit and impact.


ezBcorp provides comprehensive, low-cost legal and consulting services through a web-based platform. Services include: B Corporation-compliant legal formation and related legal services, expert business plan and pitch deck review, and social media, digital marketing, and web development services.


Social Enterprise University provides peer-to-peer e-learning and venture-building tools for for-benefit entrepreneurs, and builds the for-benefit entrepreneurship community through the intra-community exchange of financial, intellectual, and human capital.

WaterSmart Software is a proven customer engagement and data analytics platform.

WaterSmart leverages utility meter data to better communicate with residential customers about their water usage. Water utility partners also receive analytics that reveal insights into their customers, consumption habits, and program participation. Using their least-cost technology leads to smarter consumption habits, increased water efficiency, and higher return on investment for utilities. The WaterSmart platform is deployed through the cloud and requires no integration or hardware.

As of March 2016, WaterSmart is a legal Public Benefit Corporation.

WaterSmart is dedicated to changing behaviors to save our most precious natural resource. We aim to create an ethic of sustainable water management in our technology. Becoming a B Corporation and a legal Benefit Corporation demonstrates the alignment of our company mission to our products and services to our employees, utility partners, and stakeholders.The Change We Seek	

WaterSmart is focused on helping water suppliers and consumers use water more sustainably. They believe that data analytics and behavioral science, applied to water use, can lead to more efficient practices. In an era of limited water availability, water efficiency should be central to our lives. WaterSmart's hope is that the use of their innovative water efficiency data and engagement platform will lead to beneficial impacts on the world -- that people can use less water to do the same things with an enhanced quality of life, leaving more water in our streams and rivers for a healthier planet.

Lovesocial is on a mission to create human engagement in the online world. The way they see it, all people communicate to convey a message, and they strive to help their clients do this in the most authentic and innovative way possible. However big or small the organization, conglomerate or campaign, for Lovesocial it always starts with this one step: discovering the unshakable (and sometimes intangible) grain of value that everything will fall into place around. People do not need to be sold what is not needed, and the last thing the world needs are campaigns that are not rooted in commitments. By creating initiatives with this process in mind, they help build online communities who want to be there – that is why they stick around.

We wanted to become a B Corporation because we understand the difference between a campaign and a commitment, and we strive to embody the latter. We want to create sustainable changes and know transparency and accountability are the best way to do that.

The Change We Seek	

Lovesocial is seeking to create a movement of conscious communication, where all efforts, online and off are done with awareness in mind. In a world cluttered and saturated with messaging, they would like to be something of an anti agency that services clients, partners and collaborators in the most authentic and transparent way possible.

Tech Ranch Austin is a community of vibrant tech start-ups surrounded by the people, processes and materials needed to drive business success. The technology incubator is headquartered in Austin, Texas, nestled inside the the Hill Country and the Austin Startup Community.

Tech Ranch Austin is focused on accelerating pre-seed and seed stage technology companies that can change the world. Tech Ranch was founded by long-time Austin entrepreneurs Kevin Koym and Jonas Lamis who together have a long history of startup ventures, and shared the desire to help technology entrepreneurs take it to the next level. Tech Ranch Austin engaged in the B Corp community to support the statement that doing good business means thinking beyond the bottom line. Tech Ranch Austin's mission depends on community and the social capital generated enables success at a higher level for the entire cohort. We believe that the B Corp certification sets the right tone for the future of business that is community-centric at a level not seen in the past.

The Change We Seek	

The Tech Ranch Austin mission is building a community of inspired technology entrepreneurs who create innovative solutions to real world problems. This community drives down the costs of launching, building and growing start-ups, allowing entrepreneurs to take greater risks with less downside so that more technology areas get explored.

Based in Winnipeg, this company is the industry leader in research, development and commercialization of tree-free pulp and paper. Phase one for the company is the manufacturing and importing of Step Forward Paper.  Phase two will include constructing a 100% tree-free, state-of-the-art, eco-mill in the Canadian prairies, where millions of tonnes of leftover straw are readily available.

Step Forward Paper is the first widely available straw-based copy paper in North America, made from 80% wheat straw fibre with 20% Forest Stewardship Council	 certified wood fibre.

What sets Step Forward Paper apart from other papers made of agriculture-fibre waste (ag-fibre) in the North American market is that Prairie Paper’s product is higher-quality and more affordable. The paper is also more environmentally friendly.

We chose to become a Certified B Corporation to reaffirm our commitment to sustainable business practices. We are passionate about creating a sustainable future and are proud to join a community of like-minded businesses.

The Change We Seek	

Prairie Paper has been the industry leader in research, development and commercialization of tree-free pulp and paper for the past 15 years. Based in Winnipeg, the company is led by president Jeff Golfman and chairman Clayton Manness, who co-founded the company with Oscar nominated actor Woody Harrelson.

Between three and six billion trees are cut down each year. Approximately 50% of those trees are used to make paper. This creates tremendous pressure on the world’s ancient and endangered forests and threatens the species that rely upon those forests for survival.

With this in mind, Prairie Paper set out to create a new paradigm in the paper industry: tree-free paper.

A local business’s most powerful asset is the connection it has with its community. inKind helps nurture and engage that community in order to grow the business. inKind provides capital to a business in exchange for credit towards the goods and services that business offers. inKind then sells this credit as high dollar gift cards to members of the local community. The business gets to “pay back” the capital simply by doing what it loves to do - servicing customers. The customers get to help out their favorite local business, and earn a little bonus credit along the way.
 
After owning their own restaurant in DC, the team behind inKind had their eyes opened to how difficult it is for a local business to get fair financing. At their restaurant, they started selling high dollar gift cards. Then realizing that their biggest supporters in the community were happy to get lots of yummy food, rather than cash returns as investors. It worked really well, and so the idea for inKind was born. Not only does the model provide a business with funding, but also targeting customers at the right time can significantly increase their lifetime value, increase check averages or basket sizes and bring in high spending customers.

About OTEP, Inc.

 

OTEP Inc. (The Online Testing & Evaluation Platform) has offices in Toronto and Windsor, Canada. The management team has a proven track record of building and growing innovative technology companies, and their list of advisors, partners and University researchers is extensive. Their patent-pending adaptive video game engine is used to identify and improve cognition in children aged 6 to 12. 

40% of children in school today are identified as having some type of learning problem. The issue is deeper than poor grades, however, it deals with the actual learning ability of each child, which must be determined before real help can be achieved. The parent has to figure all this out by themselves which is usually quite stressful on the family and the child. OTEP has developed Think2Learn, an online, parent-monitored brain training platform that identifies a child's learning profile andimproves cognitive weaknesses through game play and supports parents with reporting that helps them understand what makes their child unique while offering targeted recommendations and interventions.

The business world is changing – todays for-profit companies can have a social mandate and it’s important to put measures in place that can identify this.  Being B-Corp certified is one such measure that is gaining recognition around the world and it was important for us to have this 3rd party validation.



 The Change We Seek	

 

OTEP’s  Mission is to help families with children struggling in school overcome barriers to effective help. Everyone associated with the company has in some way been affected by this –and have dedicated themselves to making a difference. Up to 40% of kids in school today struggle with learning differences that affect the way they learn and develop, yet methods for helping them are increasingly expensive and ineffective. Parents need tools to be active advocates for their children and need to feel that they are part of the solution – not part of the problem as they often do. OTEP wants to see the end to the destructive practice of labelling children as “learning disabled” by creating parent-focused tools that can be used in the privacy of the home with the kids doing something they love – playing video games.

As a results-based consulting firm committed to simultaneously benefiting the triple-bottom-line of people, planet, and profit, SSC is recognized in Hawaii as a model business for the new economy. Specializing in sustainability, energy training and organizational change, SSC’s successes include designing the University of Hawaii Community College-Johnson Controls (JCI) Sustainability Educational Program; training Brigham Young University to cut its energy bill by 9%, saving approximately $528,000 annually; and facilitating program and leadership development for Family Programs Hawaii, a social service agency.  With a proven track record and consistent measurable results, SSC has a scalable business model with potential for high growth.



SSC’s Student Energy Ambassador Development (SEAD) and the Achieving the Energy Independence Mission (AEIM) have worked with the Department of Education and the State Department of Defense to identify approximately $100,000 dollars in savings per training session.  SSC worked with JCI to provide five university level courses on sustainable energy, food and water; coordinate several Renewable Energy Training Summits; and develop a sustainability focused Fellowship Program.  The diversity of these inititatives demonstrates SSC’s expertise in engaging the uniqueness of each organization’s culture to ensure a positive, long-term, systemic change.



I chose this business model so that I could leverage my experience as both a business and non-profit leader. We operate with the agility and flexibility of an innovative business, while remaining purpose-driven and transparent in the way of a non-profit. This allows us to work closely with diverse clients to facilitate workshops and efficiently design and implement programs that transform organizations and institutions,” says SSC’s Founder and Director, Shanah Trevenna.

The Change We Seek	



Smart Sustainability Consulting is working to create an energy independent Hawaii through energy education, individual empowerment, and transformational institutional change. According to Triple Pundit “Hawaii is positioning itself as the nations leading test-bed for the new economy based on alternative energy.” SSC's current contracts to train the DoD and DOE to reduce the two largest energy bills in the state will set a model for all organizations, ultimately shifting Hawaii's culture towards energy literacy and action. Through motivational seminars, innovative workshops, and strategic planning SSC is creating a ripple effect of systemic change that will create a thriving sustainable economy.

Pacific Northwest Kale Chips is part of the real food movement, focused on bringing truly nourishing food to their customers and providing a bridge between organic, sustainable farms and their local communities. They have implemented a business model where farmer, producer, consumer, and community benefit: Farmers are paid fair prices. Employees are paid living wages with paid volunteer days and profit-sharing opportunities. Consumers are offered the truth about where their food comes from and how it's cultivated. And 10% of profits are donated to local charitable organizations.  We are committed to holding ourselves accountable to rigorous standards and transparent business practices that impact our employees, environment, and society in strong and beneficial ways. We will successfully harness the power of business to solve social and environmental problems, co-creating a new economy and a new way of doing business. Pacific Northwest Kale Chips has challenged itself to set the standard for healthy snacking by sourcing more than 75% of their ingredients with local farms and suppliers, adding zero oils, sweeteners, artificial ingredients, or preservatives, and utilizing zero animal ingredients. We value the health of our customers and ecosystem, which is why we are committed to organic and sustainable agriculture. The Change We Seek	

 *Pacific Northwest Kale Chips' objective is to strengthen the local community and local economy. More than 75% of their suppliers and more than 75% of their customers are located within 200 miles of where their food is produced. Dollars are cycled and recycled through the local economy, providing a bridge between small, local farmers and the community.  *Pacific Northwest Kale Chips visits each of the facilities and farms that supply their organic ingredients. They build long-term and mutually beneficial partnerships and friendships with their farmers that include paying fair prices. They offer their customers the highest level of transparency to know where their food comes from and how it is cultivated. *Pacific Northwest Kale Chips endeavors to become a waste free facility. They have implemented a recycling program with local farmers and stores to re-use cardboard and paper boxes. They donate their food scraps to local farms for feed. They utilize non-toxic cleaning supplies and as many recyclable materials as possible in their offices, including office paper, toilet paper, and paper towels made from recycled paper (not from trees). *Pacific Northwest Kale Chips has capped executive compensation at industry averages and committed themselves to paying living wages to their employees. They offer employees paid volunteer days (12 days per year) and offer profit-sharing opportunities. *Pacific Northwest Kale Chips donates a minimum of 10% of our annual profits to charitable organizations, 75% of which are located within their local economy.

About Channel Islands Outfitters

Channel Islands Outfitters has been in the business of outfitting people for paddle sports and backcountry adventures since 1993. CIO’s business model is to have equipment on location and ready to use. The company strives to provide a “Wow” experience every time and has over 200 years of experience on staff.

In 2010 CIO launched the Adventure Co-Op offering convenient and affordable access to kayaks, stand-up paddleboards, and surfboards every day of the week. This fitness center idea blossomed quickly with over 2,000 members in the first 2 years.

CIO is committed to saving the oceans at it’s retail store by having a floor stocked with over 80% “Ocean Friendly Merchandise”. From organic cotton shirts, to recycled flip-flops and boards shorts, CIO’s retail concept is designed around doing no harm.

We are ocean lovers. The ocean is our office, our playground, and our sanctuary. We want to be a leader in the movement to save the oceans; not because it sounds good... but because we cannot in good conscience just stand by watch any more.

The Change We Seek 	

Channel Islands Outfitters believes that consumers are uniquely positioned to have a serious impact on corporate policy and business decisions worldwide. If consumers align purchasing with ethics, it’s possible to motivate positive change.

The Earth is 70% ocean, and the oceans are the least respected place on Earth. If the largest ecosystem on Earth is polluted and destroyed for much longer, every other living thing on Earth will be negatively impacted. The Oceans are a beautiful place that every human must understand to appreciate, and through appreciation comes protection and preservation.

Hoje temos aproximadamente 13 milhões de brasileiros desempregados e com uma estimativa que pelo menos 20% deles não conseguem emprego por falta de qualificação. 

Provi emerged to build and develop solutions for access to education, involving both students and educational institutions.

A cutting edge AgTech company that builds and operates Controlled Environment Farms, providing a future-proof and sustainable solution for growing.
Their farms offer an innovative, technologically-driven approach to growing which don’t require any pesticide or other nasty chemicals. Using their proprietary data to control the growing environment, ensuring that every day is the perfect summer’s day. As a result, their farms are significantly more productive per square metre than traditional farming, which enables more growth in less space, less time, and uses up to 90% less water. 
Operating within dense urban areas brings down the food miles and in turn reduces both food waste and carbon footprint. In fact, all of their farms operate on 100% renewable energy and are certified net carbon-negative so it does not have a harmful impact on the environment. 
Clapham, London, is their first working farm in a disused air-raid shelter some 33 metres underground. They have been supplying retail and restaurants for the past five years. Their expanded capacity to reach this milestone required necessary technical, biosecurity and HR improvements to become BRC, Red Tractor and Field to Fork certified. Zero Carbon Farms stock many of the UK’s major retailers.

Mikado is a social enterprise committed to serve sustainable development and to yield social impact through crafting innovative models and solutions. Mikado believes in and strives to create partnerships among private sector, civil society, academic institutions and international organizations for multidimensional development. 

They wished to become a B Corp to be part of and learn from a community of organizations with social impact and to get closer to our mission of serving sustainable development. 

Mikado is a social enterprise; on the one hand it helps and equips different organizations to better serve communities and become agents of change, on the other hand it generates socially innovative projects itself. Mikado is like a “social innovation catalyzer, generator and incubator”. 

Mikado’s fields of activities are structured to reach and serve sustainable development: 

1. Corporate responsibility and sustainability solutions for a responsible private sector 

Mikado assists private sector companies to develop their corporate responsibility and sustainability strategies in order for them to meet their responsibilities towards their internal and external stakeholders in an ethical, transparent and accountable manner. 

Activities that fall under this scope include, corporate responsibility strategy development and coordination, provision of climate change solutions, sustainability reporting, corporate responsibility and sustainability reporting trainings, community investment program development and coordination, monitoring-evaluation. 

2. NGO capacity building for a sustainable and transparent civil society 

Mikado, well aware of NGOs’ crucial role in fostering democratization and active citizenship, assists them to strengthen their organizational capacities and expand their social impact. Mikado’s services in this scope include organizational capacity building, NGO management trainings, monitoring – evaluation and social impact reporting 

3. Social innovation 

The Future is Brighter Project, developed and incubated by Mikado, can be held up as a good example of social innovation, in that it makes the most efficient use of available resources, such as the Internet, online tools and volunteers to empower youth and enable the sharing of experiences and knowledge without the constraints of time or space. www.gelecekdaha.net

Skoodat wants to help education leaders fulfill the promise of learning for all. They deliver cloud education applications and agile development components to help IT leaders innovate more quickly and flexibly. Skoodat uses cloud technologies to dramatically reduce environmental impact and costs. They help improve learning for all by making education data useful, in real time, for everyone in the learning community.

Instead of building, powering and cooling rooms full of servers and software silos, schools will be able to shift expenditures to new capabilities for monitoring student learning in real time, providing dramatically better information to drive learning performance.

Skoodat is a values-driven company, seeking to make a profound social and environmental impact in partnership with many who share our passion. Becoming a B Corporation helps establish and build trust among our partners and customers by sending a clear signal that our commitments will not be compromised.The Change We Seek	

Skoodat is a key leader in a change movement within education, bringing greater equity and sustainability to education systems. By providing a cloud-based education platform, Skoodat enables schools to focus on education innovation instead of information technology management.

• Skoodat services will enable innovation to fulfill the promise of learning for all. Skoodat envisions an education system that is dramatically different than the current system, one where every child and adult can master competencies that will improve their ability to contribute to society. We aim to bring equity and sustainability to the system, ensuring that the needs of under-served communities and individuals are met though innovative approaches to gathering and reporting on learning data in real time to promote rapid intervention.

• Skoodat services will be good for the environment and will free up capital for other purposes. Because the Skoodat education platform is delivered through cloud technologies, schools can be more environmentally and fiscally responsible. Schools will no longer need to devote money and other resources to servers and software. Skoodat services eliminate the need for many paper-based systems by delivering information over the Internet. Our services can eliminate significant costs within schools and deliver dramatic new capabilities for improving the learning system.

• Skoodat services will improve the flow of money to where it is needed most. Public sector funding for schools is increasingly linked to performance data. Unfortunately, many schools lack the resources necessary to reporting reliable data to government agencies, and therefore do not receive adequate funding. By providing real-time data tracking student performance, underserved schools can receive more money from funds designed for struggling school districts.

Alexis is Greek for "helper, defender." 

The founder, Roberta Keller, started the firm in direct response to what she believed to be a need in the marketplace. To build a firm that focuses on sound advice, rather than product sales. To build a firm that is transparent in all that they do. To build a firm that focuses on consumer education, including understanding total costs and services received for fees paid.
 
Alexis Advisors offers investment management and financial planning services to families, women and small businesses. As a fee-only Registered Investment Advisor, their mission is advocate for the working professional - to engage, educate and elevate consumers in being informed, confident financial decision makers.
 
They believe that everyone should have a life plan - supported by a financial plan and you should be able to clearly understand how your money is invested, and how much you are paying for services rendered.When it comes to managing your money, they believe that the best offense is likely a good defense. They invest clients’ money in their proprietary portfolios. They actively manage exposure to equities in each of our portfolios with the goal of mitigating catastrophic losses.

For more than 100 years, Danone has sought to bring health through food to as many people as possible around the world. In Australia and New Zealand (ANZ), Danone’s wholly owned entities have a strong focus on the Specialised Nutrition category with a range of products to support healthy growth and development during the first 1000 days, as well as products that address some of the world’s biggest health challenges including faltering growth, food allergy and rare metabolic diseases, age-related conditions and chronic disease, frailty, cancer, stroke, and early Alzheimer’s disease.

Biomimicry 3.8 is the world’s leading bio-inspired consultancy offering biological intelligence consulting, professional training, and inspiration. Its mission is to train, equip, and connect the world–engineers, educators, architects, designers, business leaders, and other innovators–to sustainably emulate nature’s 3.8 billion years of brilliant designs and strategies. Whether it’s looking to native ecosystems to build factories that function like forests, or studying the armor-like abalone shell to help capture carbon, Biomimicry 3.8 helps organizations turn time-tested biological strategies into sustainable solutions.
 
 Since 1998, Biomimicry 3.8 has helped more than 250 clients and partners redesign carpets, furniture, manufacturing processes, airplanes, and even entire cities, all in nature’s sustainable image. Postcard uses physical postcards created from locally-sourced and sustainable materials to create tangible opportunities for individual and collective expression through advocacy, arts and education.

On our four platforms, you can turn digitally-captured experiences, thoughts, and feelings into postcards that IMPACT social change, EMBRACE others with shared moments, exhibit limited EDITION artwork, and EDUCATE students through civic participation.

You choose the images and words to create a postcard from your computer or phone. We print and send it. It’s that simple.

To answer a question with a question - why wouldn’t we become a B Corp? The core of what we do is driving positive change in the world through advocacy, arts and education, and being part of the B Corp community inspires us and helps us continue to do better as a company.

The Change We Seek	

Postcard's mission is to redefine how we take action in the digital space. Its platforms use physical postcards, created from locally sourced and sustainable materials to create tangible opportunities for both individual and collective expression around advocacy, arts and education. By exploring the power of physical postcards, Postcard hopes to find new ways to use images and words to send powerful messages and create positive change.

Each of the four platforms utilize the postcard medium in a unique way. Postcard Impact works dementionalize online activism by using a simple, digital tool for creating personalized postcards that are printed and delivered en mass to the real world. Postcard Embrace encourages people to make thoughtful gestures, and create positive impacts in their own lives and relationships every day. Postcard Edition is a place where artists from around the world feature their art and have it printed and shared, and Postcard Educate is a space where students create and publish their own social action campaigns, using the Postcard platform to raise their voices and create their own change. On all four of these platforms, Postcard hopes to bring presence back into the conversation, encouraging people to harness the power of the online world, while also reinvesting in the physical.

Postcard was built from the bottom up to ensure it acts in a mission driven and sustainable way. Postcard was formed as a Public Benefit Corporation, it sources materials and talent locally and employees lead a healthy, happy work lifestyle while keeping the environmental impact as low as possible. From the simple things like using only washable kitchenware to reduce waste, offering organic and healthy snacks and encouraging public transportation use with a discounted Metrocard program and access to Citibike (with helmets at the office to borrow), Postcard also encourages employees to be active citizens and get involved in as much as possible both during and out of work hours.

Ouro Verde Amazonia

Ouro Verde Amazonia is a company created in 2002 by young entrepreneurs in the heart of the Amazon region. Originally built over two strong pillars (a new model of fair relationship with its suppliers – native Amazon communities – and strong investment in R&D to create added value and high nutritional value products made with native Amazon Fruits - mainly Brazil Nut and Açai Berry), The company,  now is part of Grupo Orsa, promotes regional development through the sustainable use of natural resources. Based on fair commerce practices and training programs for gathering, storage and sale of raw Amazonian Fruits, our company was an innovator in developing an equitable and harmonious relationship with the indigenous communities, family farmers and rubber collectors. Thanks to its practices, Ouro Verde Amazonia earned organic certification for the entire product line from Ecocert Brasil. Over its nine years of existence, the company has consolidated a business model that stood out for its distinctive relationship with the traditional communities of the Amazon, including several indigenous ethnic groups, residents of several Resex (Federal Extractive Reserves) and smallholder farmers. This unique model was guided by the fair-trade and above-average prices paid to suppliers.

In Brazil, the extraction of Brazil Nut is characterized by high concentration of production in a few states; the Acre, Amazonas and Pará hold 80.7% of production. Other states (Rondonia, Mato Grosso, Amapa and Roraima) must share the remaining 19.3%. The Northern Region is responsible for 98.72% of national production of Brazil nut, with direct impacts on the lives of extractive communities, small farmers and indigenous people. Through fair trade and ethical practices, Ouro Verde seeks to create more positive impacts in these communities, as well as for consumers.

We believe in a new business model in which sharing benefits, ethical approach and solidarity are the strong bases that should support these “new generation companies.” The ending and fair financial result, which is essential for the longevity of the companies, should be an obvious and necessary result of this equation. By becoming a B Corp, we would like to share these principles with other “sister companies” around the world, learn alternative ways to reinforce these kind of principles, and add an additional water drop to the B Corporations Initiatives by sharing our history .The Change We Seek	

Ouro Verde Amazonia believes that one of the biggest challenges for the future of the Amazon region is to reorder old regional supply chains of its native products, like Açai Berry and Brazil Nut. These supply chains are historically characterized as unbalanced and unfair; by consolidating them in a new business model, they can be made more sustainable and harmonious by sharing the benefits of producing some of the healthiest nature foods with the native Amazonian communities. Implementation of this sustainable business model would generate at least three clear benefits: better life for local Amazon communities, maintenance of the majestic Amazon Forest (no deforestation) and widespread supply of highly healthy food (Açai and Brazil Nut) for consumers around the world. For Ouro Verde, and for all those interested in preserving the world’s largest tropical forest, production of goods made from the Brazil nut is a question of believing in a better future. The mission is to combine economic satisfaction with environmental protection, emphasizing a profound respect for nature and generating opportunities for all suppliers, employees and consumers through the practice of fair trade, ethical values and high quality services.

Ouro Verde Amazonia believes that one of the biggest challenges for the future of the Amazon region is to reorder old regional supply chains of its native products, like Açai Berry and Brazil Nut. These supply chains are historically characterized as unbalanced and unfair; by consolidating them in a new business model, they can be made more sustainable and harmonious by sharing the benefits of producing some of the healthiest nature foods with the native Amazonian communities. Implementation of this sustainable business model would generate at least three clear benefits: better life for local Amazon communities, maintenance of the majestic Amazon Forest (no deforestation) and widespread supply of highly healthy food (Açai and Brazil Nut) for consumers around the world. For Ouro Verde, and for all those interested in preserving the world’s largest tropical forest, production of goods made from the Brazil nut is a question of believing in a better future. The mission is to combine economic satisfaction with environmental protection, emphasizing a profound respect for nature and generating opportunities for all suppliers, employees and consumers through the practice of fair trade, ethical values and high quality services.

Iroquois Valley Farmland REIT, PBC is a restorative farmland finance company providing land access to organic family farmers, with a focus on the next generation. Starting in 2007 (as Iroquois Valley Farms, LLC) and establishing itself as a leader in socially responsible investing before “SRI” and “Impact Investing” were common vernacular, the Company has a long track record of successfully acquiring organic and transitional farmland. In 2016, the Company expanded its scope to include mortgage financing/re-financing.

The Company uses private investment capital to facilitate farmers’ expansion plans through leasing or mortgage financing. The Company is committed to social responsibility and the public health. In that regard, Iroquois Valley Farmland REIT, the parent entity, was established as a Public Benefit Corporation, whose public benefit is enabling healthy food production, soil restoration and water quality improvement through the establishment of secure and sustainable farmland access tenures.

Iroquois Valley Farms has purchased over 8,400 acres of farmland representing nearly $50 million in transaction value (inclusive of land subsequently sold its tenant farmers). All farms are operated by independent family farmers organically.

Bridges Fund Management is a fund manager that specialises exclusively in sustainable and impact investing, with offices in London and New York. They aim to generate attractive risk-adjusted financial returns for our investors alongside measurable positive social and/or environmental impact. Founded in 2002, Bridges has since raised over $1bn of investor capital across its platform of Sustainable Growth, Property and Social Sector Funds. 

Bridges invests in business, properties, social enterprises and outcomes contracts that help to address pressing long-term social and environmental challenges, with a focus on four key impact themes: health & well-being, education & skills, sustainable living and underserved markets. Their strategy is to focus on opportunities where growth and impact go hand-in-hand; that is, where achieving important social and environmental goals also drives better performance. This could be by backing businesses that generate jobs in areas of high unemployment, building environmentally-friendly care homes for the elderly to sustain our ageing population, or providing flexible financing for innovative youth employment programmes.

Linhardt Design is the New York-based fine and fashion jewelry house that is revolutionizing the industry with its extra-ordinary designs coupled with socially and environmentally responsible practices. Linhardt merges design sophistication with the highest principles of sustainability by exclusively using recycled precious metals and mine-to-market gemstones. At a time when jewelry companies are outsourcing, Linhardt manufactures locally, creating jobs right in the Diamond District of Manhattan, while bringing supply chain transparency to the industry.
 
Coined “the green jeweler”, Linhardt was chosen for a "Critics' Pick: Best of NY” by New York magazine. Linhardt Design is a woman-owned business with a percentage of proceeds donated to the education of girls in Africa.

Impact First Investments is the first Israeli investment management firm specifically designed to leverage local innovation to create globally scalable social and environmental impact. In order to realize this objective, the firm is aggregating tradition investment and philanthropic capital to provide early-stage financing for viable and socially driven technology companies. Due to the stage, for-profit nature, and primary social motivation of its portfolio, the firm primarily invests in companies that would not be established, stabilized, or reach their intended markets without its financing and contribution. 
 
Impact First Investments believes that with the right investment strategy, Israeli technology is well positioned to sustainably and effectively address global social and environmental issues. Over the past few decades, Israeli technology has proven its ability to innovate on behalf of the global community, making the world a healthier, cleaner, and more sustainable place. Impact First Investments seeks to harness this aptitude by specifically investing with the intent to maximize social and environmental value as it establishes a new layer of Israeli high tech companies aimed at improving the lives of individuals and communities around the globe.

Junior Explorers is a program designed for elementary school kids with the mission to connect them to the planet by teaching them about wildlife and nature. Every month, Junior Explorers go on wild adventures around the planet, joined by characters Kia and Kyle, to explore new ecosystems and solve mysteries in nature. Kids learn about extraordinary habitats such as the Artic, the Amazon, and the Serengeti through mission kits that are delivered home each month that include fact sheets, cool collectibles and fun activities. The journey then continues online with a rich digital experience that ends with Mission Giveback. Through Mission Giveback, kids convert their points earned playing to dollars and select which non-for-profit they desire to donate back to in support of conservation. The program is both tactile and digital giving kids a mulit-sensory experience.

At Junior Explorers, giving back is a core value of our business and is central to everything we create. Our program is designed to educate and connect kids to the natural wonders that exist across our planet while also supporting non-profits doing frontline work on conservation. We became a B-Corp to hold ourselves to a higher standard and be in the company of other like-minded companies that are "using business as a force for good." We have big dreams here at Junior Explorers, the biggest being to protect our planet.

 

The Change We Seek	

 

Junior Explorers' mission is to inspire the next generation of environmental stewards. It is clear that everyone is talking about the state of the planet, but no one is talking to the ones who will be most impacted: our kids. Junior Explorers was created with the vision to start the conversation around conservation with kids and influence their future actions by creating in them a great love for nature and wildlife. Junior Explorers believes that education, understanding and connection are needed first to bring about positive action to protect our planet.

OLOMOMO Nut Company launched in Boulder, Colorado in 2008 with a simple mission: be The Good Nuts and create one of the first socially and environmentally conscious nut companies.

The innovative brand experience and products are designed to inspire people to be more nutty, good and adventurous. Our company is committed to developing fun, healthy Snacks that infuse the exotic with the familiar and make your mouth water. We only use simple, real, natural ingredients, including fair trade, organic, and sustainable packaging when possible.

From humble origins at Colorado farmers markets – sampling one nut at a time – to a national debut on the Cooking Channel, OLOMOMO is now quickly becoming a national brand selling to grocery stores across the country. Earlier this year New Hope Media picked us as “one of the top 10 brands to watch” in 2014.

We became a B Corp because we believe creating a positive impact on society and the environment is an important part of building a strong company. Inspired by study of development issues in Brazil and Africa, Justin Perkins, OLOMOMO’s founder, set out to start a company that could leverage market forces to help make a positive impact on society. By spreading our message “Be Nutty, Be Good, Be Adventurous,” we encourage all of our customers to be everyday heroes.

The Change We Seek	

OLOMOMO seeks to be part of the movement in changing how a successful business is defined. By meeting higher standards of social and environmental performance, transparency, and accountability, B Corps compete to be the best businesses for the world.  OLOMOMO is committed to developing a fair and healthy workplace, supply chain, and operations that are beneficial for the environment and all of the people involved at every part of the process.

Numi Organic Tea blends premium organic teas and herbs with only 100% real ingredients, allowing nature to speak for itself. As a pioneering, quadruple-bottom line company (people, planet, product, profit), Numi sources its teas and ingredients directly from fair labor gardens that pay farmers and workers fair wages that allow their families to thrive. Over half of Numi’s teas are sourced from Fair Trade Certified gardens, which empower tea growers to invest Fair Trade premiums back into their communities. Fair Trade premiums earned on tea gardens have helped procure and develop new roads, cooking stoves, mosquito nets, schools, college scholarships, maternity benefits, onsite medical staff and life insurance for farming families.
 
 Numi is a company committed to reducing its impact on the planet through ecologically responsible choices in sourcing, production and recycled and non-GMO packaging. Numi Organic Tea sources organic teas and herbs, which helps protect the health of farmers, the consumer and the planet. Numi Organic Tea uses natural, biodegradable, filter-paper tea bags, rather than GMO corn or plastic “silky” tea sachets. Numi’s tea boxes are made of 85% post-consumer waste, printed with soy-based inks and without unneeded shrink-wrap.

Their network of artisans are stewards of their fisheries, and CleanFish is steward of their stories as they connect producers to chefs and consumers in a celebration of fish you can trust with a difference you can taste. You can read about each type of fish in detail on their website.

Spotlight Solar makes aesthetic solar mounting equipment. People call them solar trees. Unlike utilitarian solar ÒrackingÓ equipment, Spotlight products are designed to be seen and touched, making a statement of clean energy advocacy.
 
 Spotlight allows solar to be visually appealing while signaling the ownerÕs environmental stewardship. These solar trees complement other investments, adding image value and property differentiation, and accelerating the adoption of solar energy by raising awareness.

 Spotlight Solar exists to foster the adoption of solar energy by making it more visible and attractive. Solar energy is great - elegantly making power from free sunlight, with no emissions - but it is largely hidden from view. If more great-looking solar structures can be placed in highly visible places, more people will consider using solar themselves. If they can influence only 10,000 people to utilize solar power, they'll have eliminated the amount of pollution generated by burning four million gallons of gasoline every year! As well, they will create jobs people love: jobs which apply people's gifts, which honor contributions, and which have a positive impact on the planet and their communities.

Agora Partnerships accelerates the growth of early-stage impact companies in Latin America. We are a global community of entrepreneurs, investors, mentors, and individuals dedicated to using the power of business to effect positive change in their communities. We work only with early-stage entrepreneurs where the right kind of support can significantly accelerate their ability to create impact. Our aim is to help build a more just, sustainable world primarily though our Impact Accelerator program, which provides entrepreneurs with access to social, human, and financial capital.

Over the course of the last two years, eighteen businesses have participated in Agora's Accelerator, which provides entrepreneurs with personalized consulting, mentors, leadership development, and the opportunity to pitch to impact investors from around the world. All entrepreneurs are GIIRS rated, and Agora plans to become the biggest provider of GIIRS-rated businesses in the world.

We believe B Lab’s insights can be applied to businesses in developing countries – helping them understand how to be better corporate citizens and giving them a way to alert customers and investors that they practice what they preach.

The Change We Seek	

Agora Partnerships seeks to help grassroots, socially responsible small businesses in the developing world create jobs and fight poverty and inequality.

• Business, no matter how big or small, must take into account the needs of shareholders, employees, customers, and the environment. Agora is committed to helping small business entrepreneurs become leaders and role models in their community for the way they run their business.  They recognize that the most powerful force for attacking poverty is people and their will to create value where none exists or can even be imagined. Building trust and investing in relationships with change agents helps them live up to their potential to make a difference in their communities.

Agora Partnerships Results

•There are many investors, consultants, technicians, students and professionals who want to help socially responsible developing world entrepreneurs overcome the odds but don't know how. Through our Accelerator, Agora allows these people to engage in socially responsible investing. By connecting this “missing middle” with a variety of willing investors, Agora fills the gap between microfinance and larger-scale investments and lending.

• Businesses working with Agora have increased the number of full-time jobs they contribute to their communities by 17%. 83% of startups coming out of Agora’s process were still functioning one year after launch. On average, Agora supported businesses have increased their profits by 57%.

Agora Impact Accelerator Results

•Agora’s first Accelerator was founded in 2011 and included nine selected companies from an assortment of sectors and four different Central American countries. Over 50% of participating companies received investment. In 2012, we selected nine companies from Central America and Mexico, of which nearly 70% are currently in negotiations with investors.

•In less than two years, Accelerator companies have attracted more than US$3,500,000 dollars in investment. In 2013, we will be accepting over 30 companies from throughout Latin America.

SQA Pharmacy is a “closed door” institutional pharmacy that provides pharmacy services to community based managed health care facilities. Every day 365 days a year, SQA provides high quality, affordable, and reliable pharmaceutical healthcare to consumers. SQA maintains a constant level of outstanding professionalism and courtesy to its clients. SQA practices a sustainable business model - 75% of the profit distribution from SQA Pharmacy is put into a foundation that awards grants to 501(c) organizations and government entities to help community based health care centers serve the low income population and the under-insured. SQA also services one federally certified 340B local health center. For Profit Efficiency with Non-Profit Ideals…

We became a B Corporation to engage in the discussion and actions on how we can ensure a better quality of life today for our people and our planet.The Change We Seek	

Service, Quality, and Accuracy...Not Just Our Name Our Business

IGNIA is a venture capital investment firm that supports the founding and expansion of high growth social enterprises that serve the base of the socio-economic pyramid (BoP) in Latin America.

IGNIA's social investment focus is to fight poverty by developing profitable, highly scalable businesses that serve the needs of the Base of the Pyramid population in areas of exceptional need including health, housing, and education. These businesses provide services and products that ultimately improve the quality of life of the BoP and enable them to generate wealth for themselves.

The B Corp certification provides a standard, credible means for investors and partners to recognize IGNIA's commitment not only to deliver substantial social change in our core business of investing in the BoP, but also in how we treat our employees, environment, and stakeholders.The Change We Seek™

By providing effective responses to the enormously underserved needs of low income populations, both as consumers as well as active participants in productive value chains, IGNIA empowers entrepreneurship and generates social impact while creating attractive financial returns for its investors.

The largest market in Latin America is comprised of people who earn less than US$3,000 per year. These 360 million people represent the BoP market, which, in aggregate, is estimated at US$510 Billion. By providing capital to businesses in this marketplace, we enrich the community to higher standards of living while at the same time using this goal to attract investors and create a profitable return.

IGNIA believes that the only way to address the poverty disparity in the BoP and tap into the aggregate market presence is through business. This is not achieved through one firm, but through the creation of an industry, which is the natural outgrowth of an economic activity which generates levels of profitability equal or higher than those with the same risk profile. IGNIA is jump-starting this industry and opening the door for other sources of capital to support impoverished regions of Mexico.

Accion Verde is a Colombian for profit enterprise that obtains revenues by producing positive social and environmental impacts, by planting trees in strategic places of Colombia, calling on third party Social Responsibility resources.
 
Accion Verde's founder has been involved in sustainable development, associating my two careers, Economics and Anthropology since the beginning of his professional career. Accion Verde believes that the basis for a more just society, with people and the Planet, must include generating employment, entrepreneurship, with economic benefits for owners as well as collaborators. This social/environmental thrust for sustainable and just development, motivated their team to become a B Corporation.
 
Accion Verde strives to generate ecological restoration in strategic places of Colombia, prevent natural disasters while mitigating climate change. They hope to create a new society, more inclusive and in tune with the protection of the environment, that will help improve the basis for Colombian and Planetary sustainable development. Each person, each enterprise must and should, do a green action (Acción Verde), and Accion Verde offers them that possibility with protective reforestation.

Shifting Patterns works alongside changemaker leaders to develop the collaborative competencies to bring about positive change in their workplaces and communities. They help clients identify what’s really getting in the way of effective teamwork, such as ineffective meetings, unhealthy conflict, and lack of accountability, build the skills to address these challenges, and put a support system in place to maintain improved performance.

Shifting Patterns works alongside clients to plan and lead meetings that are participatory, action-oriented, and consistently meet expectations. They help teams articulate their purpose, set goals, develop action plans, and put the structures and processes in place that contribute to effective teamwork. They also work with associations, networks, alliances, and coalitions to define their purpose and membership criteria, conduct stakeholder mapping, and determine how members will work together.  

Shifting Patterns has helped social enterprise accelerators, like Ashoka Changemakers, socially responsible business associations, like B Local: Mid-Atlantic Region, and social justice networks, like National Justice for Our Neighbors to determine their strategic direction, strengthen team leadership skills, and improve communication and coordination.

RSF Capital Management, PBC is a wholly owned subsidiary of RSF Social Finance (RSF), a financial services organization dedicated to transforming the way the world works with money. RSF offers investing, lending, and giving services that generate positive social and environmental impact while fostering community and collaboration among participants. Since 1984, RSF has made over $275 million in loans and over $100 million in grants to non-profit and for-profit social enterprises. RSF Capital Management was formed in 2008 to manage all of RSF’s lending activity to for-profit social enterprises. RSF Capital Management provides senior working capital and subordinated term debt to businesses meeting a rigorous social enterprise profile.
 
RSF offers investing, lending, and giving services to individuals and enterprises committed to improving society and the environment. It currently has over one thousand clients who are creating enormous positive impact by helping the company redirect the flow of money from global capital markets to local ones. Together, they are creating a shift from financial transactions that are complex, opaque, and anonymous to those that are direct, transparent, and personal.

EKA Legacy Partners, LLC., DBA: EarthKeeper Alliance is dedicated to the conservation, preservation, restoration and thoughtful development of large tracts of pristine land that had previously been slated for large‐scale development. As Impact Investors and Land Stewards, we are dedicated to supporting Living Family Legacies through Land Undevelopment ™. We protect pristine land so that over development does not take place and the land stays in balance with the environment. Our goals are to foster sustainable timber and water resource management, biodiversity and habitat restoration.  We donate 10% of our profits to our sister company; Earth Services, Inc. who’s initiative include; urban gardens and youth educational centers in the inner cities of America. Our focus is to conserve open spaces and preserve flora and fauna habitats. 

Certified B Corporations meet higher standards of social and environmental performance, transparency, and accountability.  The performance standards are comprehensive and transparent.  We want to lead the way for “Responsible Business Practices in Real Estate Development”.  

We are honored to be a Certified B Corporation. The B Corp mantle helps us be accountable to our investors, employees, the environment and the community at large.

 

"We support the legacy of our investors for the benefit and well being of our greater humanity."


 The Change We Seek™

To provide Leadership in Impact Environmental Stewardship. To implement and support the business community in the practice of Earthonomics. 

Earthonomics: A holistic relationship between the earth and material prosperity, a balanced exchange of goods and services that preserve the earth; the interaction of mankind and the earth that aligns conservation, preservation, and restoration of the land and our selves.

Our operations are strategically located in Boulder, Colorado, a city widely regarded as the epicenter of the natural products industry.



We became a B Corp to better align institutional capital with the needs of impact oriented entrepreneurs.

Greenmont Capital Partners seek to better align institutional capital with the needs of impact-oriented entrepreneurs to leverage the power of free markets for the benefit of the environment and society.

Restore Capital’s vision is to be a leader in bringing private investments to environmental and infrastructure restoration projects. They help by combining capital from all sources (public, private … debt, equity…etc.) into cost effective funding solutions. Their goal is to increase the amount of funding available in order to create a sustainable model going forward.

We became a B Corp to join a community of like minded companies, and to publicly exclaim the social and environmental "DNA" of Restore Capital.The Change We Seek™

During the last decade, the private sector has been asked to help create and fund solutions for this pressing cause due to the limits and funding shortfalls of the traditional sources – government and philanthropy.  We believe private enterprise and funding is necessary for any truly permanent and sustainable change to take place.  The size of the effort demands that we engage the private sector into the solution since it has the scale and scope.  For this reason, Restore Capital was formed.

We believe the private sector offers the best means in our country’s economy to affect change.  We do need the partnership with government to set goals and regulations, and environmental activists are key to maintaining focus and commitment.  Still, the “heavy lifting” must be done by private businesses and enterprises that have the capital and resources to perform the tasks.

Farmigo is the world’s first online farmer’s market, connecting people and communities – such as workplaces, schools and community centers – with local farms to provide a personalized online marketplace for local, fresh-from-harvest food. The company was founded in delivering technology to farms to help them manage their community supported agriculture (CSA) subscriptions. Three years later, hundreds of farms are using the technology and Farmigo has connected them to over 3,000 delivery sites, including Google and Twitter offices. Farmigo is now building on this foundation by expanding the traditional model – where farm’s sell a subscription to their farm for the season – to offer the selection of a farmer’s market through an easy, online order system, utilizing the power of the web to make it accessible to everyone. 
 
 The food industry is ripe for change and there has never been a better time or opportunity to disrupt the status quo and improve access to fresh food. With keen consumer interest in better food options, advances in technology, and increased e-commerce adoption, the time is ripe to fundamentally change the way food is purchased and distributed.

Solmetric Corporation is a test and measurement company that designs and manufactures tools for the solar installation industry. Its shade analysis tool, the patented SunEyeTM, is a hand-held electronic tool that instantly measures shading and solar access data of a particular location. The device is an indispensable on-site tool for accurately designing a new solar system and maximizing its return on investment. The SunEye has received awards throughout the world and has been adopted as the preferred shade analysis tool for solar installers. Solmetric’s PV Designer is a software tool that allows solar installers to design a solar system by dragging modules onto a roof, importing SunEye shade measurements, and simulating the energy output of the system.

Solmetric became a B Corporation to reflect our commitment to running our business in a sustainable and socially conscious way and to provide a framework and community within which to further this commitment.The Change We Seek	

Solmetric is committed to developing products that serve the solar industry. The focus on this alternative energy market sector is as much for the social good that the products enable as it is for the exciting growth opportunities it presents. In addition to developing products that help improve the environment, like tools that make solar systems and those who install them more effective, Solmetric also follows environmentally and socially responsible guidelines in running its business. These guidelines include: company-wide CO2 free operation, a philanthropy program in which it donate 1% of products and 1% of personnel time to non-profit organizations, and the use of sustainably manufactured materials in its products. For example, the molded plastic enclosure for the SunEye-210 includes 21% post-consumer recycled plastic--an achievement that is virtually unheard of in the world of electronics enclosures.

SLOWCOLOR is an integrated bottom line high impact enterprise committed to clothing the world in beauty, health and responsibility. They are revitalizing the use of age-old traditions to dramatically reduce the social, environmental and health impacts of textile manufacturing. By paying artisan producers in India a living wage and sharing in value creation through weaver royalty and community reinvestment, working in only natural (non-synthetic) yarns and using only herbal and vegetable dyes, SLOWCOLOR is creating a transformative model to bring ethical and beautiful fashion to the world at scale.

Project Repat ('Repat') creates fair wage jobs in the USA by upcycling excess textiles into more fashionable and functional clothing accessories. Repat customers send their t-shirts laced with memories to us, and we turn them into blankets, bags, scarves and ties. We also work with brands and universities to turn their excess into a product that can be given out at events, conferences and to donors. Each product is made in the USA by someone making a fair and living wage. Repat production partners include: Opportunity Threads, a worker-owned cut and sew enterprise in Morganton, North Carolina, NuPath- a non-profit in Woburn, MA that employs people with disabilities and also students at Shawsheen Valley Regional Technical School and Artists for Humanity in the Boston area.

We started this business with two principles that we weren't willing to comprise on: all of our products would be upcycled and we would pay people a fair and living wage in the USA to make it. It was very important for us to get B Corporation Certified and join the hundreds of businesses who are committed to making a social impact.

The Change We Seek	

We want show the world that you can create a business that makes money, but can also share the wealth and pay people enough to make their own economic decisions. One of the most important ways to lift people out of poverty is to create jobs that pay a living wage, and in the process, we also want to prevent millions of excess textiles from being dumped in landfills.

Community Sourced Capital helps businesses access capital from their community through innovative financial systems. CSC provides loans to small businesses using funds sourced from people in their community.



The team at CSC designed a simple way for community members to lend money to local businesses they love. It’s great for businesses that need capital to grow, and it’s also an amazing way to involve communities in a new kind of finance–finance that supports local businesses without asking anyone to give away their money.



CSC provides the technology, marketing assistance and administrative work to let companies focus on engaging their community and running their business. Right now, CSC is focused on a simple lending system for people to lend $50 to a business they know. Those $50 loans are called Squares and the lenders are called Squareholders.



Becoming a B Corp is one of the easiest business decisions we’ve ever made. Even though starting a business is tough enough, making sure that we reach B Corp certification is a joyful process. It’s the kind of work we’re happy to carry out late on a Saturday night. This is all good work, and it’s a thrill to be part of the B Corp Community.

The Change We Seek	



At Community Sourced Capital, they're rethinking financial systems from the ground up, and they think that the timing for doing that is perfect. CSC purposefully designs their financial systems to involve the same communities that benefit from what we’re funding. When everyone has a say, the change we seek will be in everyone’s hands. CSC calls it “funding the world you want to live in.”
